tasks.short: Register, match, code and get approval for supplier and agency invoices, then prepare the payment batch.
tasks.statement: Process invoices for payment.
tasks.design: Configure AFAS invoice scanning and approval workflows so invoices arrive registered and route to budget holders without mail. A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform matches invoices to orders and agency hours, with a bounded model step for messy agency lines, and runs duplicate and IBAN-change tests before the batch. The payment batch is still released in Rabobank by two people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agency invoices did not tie to orders without reading free text, and approvals lived in mailboxes, so building matching rules for three agency formats was not worth it.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes the matching job and tests cheap to build, and small model steps can read free-text invoice lines reliably enough when an exact tie-out checks them.
tasks.still_hard: Disputes with suppliers and agencies about rates and hours, and invoices from agencies that change formats. Payment errors are hard to reverse.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a price difference is acceptable, knowing which supplier or agency tends to overbill, and the second signature on payments.

ambition.what: Run payment batches twice a week with early-payment discounts taken, instead of one weekly batch.

tasks.altitude: The accountant handles only exceptions and batch release, and owns the match tolerances and approval routes in AFAS.

tasks.short: Prepare and check monthly records and statements for accuracy, completeness and Dutch GAAP and policy conformance.
tasks.statement: Prepare, examine, or analyze accounting records, financial statements, or other financial reports to assess accuracy, completeness, and conformance to reporting and procedural standards.
tasks.design: A nightly job on the governed data platform pulls the AFAS trial balance, subledgers, Rabobank CAMT.053 and the payroll journal and runs fixed tie-outs, shown in a Power BI close dashboard. A bounded model step drafts variance explanations and the close memo with a trace-to-transaction check; adjusting entries stay with the accountant and are approved by the controller.
tasks.previous_blocker: The tie-outs lived in personal Excel workbooks rebuilt every month; scripting them needed developer time Finance did not have.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes scripted tie-outs on AFAS extracts cheap, and models can draft variance text when every figure is checked against the data.
tasks.still_hard: Judgement on accruals, provisions and Dutch GAAP treatment; no benchmark covers Dutch GAAP. Models make multi-step errors and hidden assumptions, so drafts must be traceable.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing the business behind a number, such as a site's seasonal flex peak, and deciding what to adjust and how to explain it to the controller and auditor.

ambition.what: A weekly soft close with tie-outs and variance list, so issues are fixed during the month, not at day 5.

tasks.altitude: The accountant reviews a ready tie-out dashboard and spends time on adjustments; they own the tie-out definitions and thresholds.

tasks.short: Reconcile bank, agency, payroll clearing and intercompany accounts and clear the differences.
tasks.statement: Review accounts for discrepancies and reconcile differences.
tasks.design: A daily Python job on the governed data platform reads Rabobank CAMT.053, AFAS ledger lines, agency hours and the payroll journal and applies fixed match rules, leaving a short open item list in a reconciliation app. A bounded model step proposes matches for the leftovers; the accountant approves corrections, which are posted to AFAS, and the workpaper is generated for the controller.
tasks.previous_blocker: Matching rules lived in the accountant's head and Excel; agency and intercompany data had to be pulled by hand from different portals.
tasks.enabler_now: CAMT.053 and AFAS APIs give structured data, and AI coding makes match rules and a small review app quick to build and change.
tasks.still_hard: Differences caused by missing documents or other teams' errors still need people to chase. Agency portal exports may lack APIs.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing who to ask and which differences matter, and deciding when to write off or escalate.

ambition.what: Daily bank and agency reconciliation instead of month-end, so agency overbilling is caught before payment.

tasks.altitude: The accountant clears a short daily exception list and owns the match rules and tolerances.

tasks.short: Check books and AFAS processes for control weaknesses, policy breaches and wasted effort; propose fixes.
tasks.statement: Inspect account books and accounting systems for efficiency, effectiveness, and use of accepted accounting procedures to record transactions.
tasks.design: Scheduled control tests on the governed data platform run over every AFAS journal, user right and vendor change and feed a Power BI controls and process dashboard. A bounded model step flags manual journals that may breach the SharePoint accounting policy and drafts findings; the accountant confirms and discusses fixes with the controller.
tasks.previous_blocker: Testing every transaction needed scripting skills and AFAS log access; sampling by hand was the only option.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes full-population tests cheap, and models can read journal descriptions against written policy with a human checking every flag.
tasks.still_hard: Judging whether a process is effective, and changing how other teams work. Tests on user activity can count as employee monitoring, which needs works council consent and an AVG check.
tasks.human_edge: Judging root causes, weighing control risk against effort, and persuading colleagues to change a process.

ambition.what: A monthly controls report for the Finance Director and auditor covering every transaction, not samples.

tasks.altitude: The accountant moves from sampling to designing and tuning tests, and gains a say in which controls and process changes Finance adopts.

tasks.short: Calculate and book month-end accruals, prepayments, deferrals and corrections in AFAS, with support for the controller.
tasks.statement: Prepare adjusting journal entries.
tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform pulls the AFAS trial balance, open purchase orders and agency hours. It applies a versioned accrual rule table and writes a balanced journal batch with a tie-out workbook. A bounded model step drafts the one-off entries and memos from contracts and mails. The controller approves the batch in a simple review screen, which then posts it to AFAS through the UpdateConnector.
tasks.previous_blocker: The rules lived in personal Excel workbooks and in the accountant's head. Building and testing a governed job against AFAS and three agency portals cost more than two accountants could justify.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes the extraction, rule table and tie-out cheap to build and test. Models can now draft month-end entries reliably on structured scenarios [S1], and vendors ship 'prepare, not post' entry agents [S5].
tasks.still_hard: Estimates and provisions need judgement, and multi-step reasoning across files is still where models fail [S2]. Agency portal exports change without notice, and the auditor has to accept the new trail.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a disputed agency invoice or a provision is probable and how big it is. Defending that judgement to the controller and the auditor.

ambition.what: A weekly soft close of flex worker and freight accruals instead of month-end only, so the forecast sees cost trends three weeks earlier

tasks.altitude: The accountant reviews a ready batch and a short exception list instead of building the sheet. They own the accrual rule table and decide which items move from judgement to rule.

tasks.short: Assign, chase and check the bookkeepers' filing and recording work and send record packages to auditor and tax.
tasks.statement: Direct activities of personnel engaged in filing, recording, compiling, and transmitting financial records.
tasks.design: Replace the Excel close checklist and the mail chasing with a Microsoft Lists close tracker plus a nightly Python check on the AFAS extract. The check flags bookings without a document, unprocessed agency invoices and late approvals, and sends Teams reminders to the owner. A Power BI page shows close status by site. A small answer desk over the SharePoint procedures handles routine questions. Record packages for the auditor are compiled from the PBC list, and an accountant sends them.
tasks.previous_blocker: The checklist and chasing were cheap enough by hand and no one owned a link between AFAS and Teams. Completeness checks over every booking needed SQL nobody in finance wrote.
tasks.enabler_now: The nightly AFAS extract already feeds Power BI, and AI coding makes the completeness checks and Teams notifications a few days of work.
tasks.still_hard: Tracking bookkeepers' task completion is personnel monitoring and may need works council consent. Sending to the auditor and tax adviser cannot be undone and stays gated.
tasks.human_edge: Coaching bookkeepers, setting priorities when the close slips, and deciding what goes to the auditor.

ambition.what: Site managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo get their own list of open invoice approvals and missing receipts before close, not a forwarded mail

tasks.altitude: The accountant stops chasing and starts the week from a status page. They decide priorities and handle the exceptions that the reminders did not fix.

tasks.short: Keep the chart of accounts and coding rules in AFAS, code unclear entries, and fix miscodings.
tasks.statement: Establish tables of accounts and assign entries to proper accounts.
tasks.design: Configure AFAS supplier defaults as the first line of coding. A nightly Python job on the governed data platform runs outlier tests over every ledger line (account against supplier history, VAT code against country, cost centre against site). A bounded model step proposes codes for the lines the defaults miss. The accountant works one Power BI exception page and approves reclasses, which post to AFAS through the UpdateConnector.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coding checks were done by sampling at year end because testing every line in Excel was too slow. Free-text invoice lines could not be classified by rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Testing every transaction with plain code is cheap to build now. Models can classify short free-text lines against a known account list, with code checking the output.
tasks.still_hard: Chart of accounts changes affect reporting, Power BI and the audit, and stay a deliberate human decision. Reverse charge and intra-EU VAT coding need care.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding how the chart of accounts should reflect the business (sites, transport against warehousing) and when a new cost type deserves its own account.

ambition.what: A monthly miscoding sweep over every ledger line in place of a year-end sample, to cut audit adjustments

tasks.altitude: The accountant spends less time coding and more time owning the rule table and the exception page. They decide when a recurring exception becomes a supplier default.

tasks.short: Design, build, change and document finance processes, AFAS setup, Excel tools and reports.
tasks.statement: Develop, implement, modify, and document recordkeeping and accounting systems, making use of current computer technology.
tasks.design: Move the accountants' Excel macros and one-off tools into version-controlled Python and SQL jobs on the governed data platform, built with an AI coding assistant. Each job has a test suite that runs against the AFAS extract. Procedures are drafted from config exports into SharePoint, and every change is approved by the controller before go-live.
tasks.previous_blocker: Accountants could configure AFAS and Excel but not write and test code, so tools stayed in fragile workbooks. Documentation was always behind.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding lets an accountant build and test small jobs 10 or more times faster, and models draft procedure text from config.
tasks.still_hard: Design choices affect audit, tax and reporting. Code needs an owner, review and access control on the platform, and IT must govern it.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing how Noordhaven's warehouses, transport and agencies actually run, and turning that into a ledger and process the auditor accepts.

ambition.what: Readiness for Dutch B2B e-invoicing (1 July 2030) and KVK SBR filing of the annual accounts, which AFAS does not file [S8][S10]

tasks.altitude: The accountant becomes the builder of finance tools, not their user. They decide which tools move from Excel to governed jobs, and the controller approves.

tasks.short: Build the monthly management pack from AFAS, explain variances and present it to management.
tasks.statement: Report to management regarding the finances of establishment.
tasks.design: Replace the Excel pack with a scheduled Python job on the governed data platform that reads the AFAS extract, applies a versioned account mapping and builds the pack and a Power BI page each night after close. A bounded model step drafts variance commentary from journal lines with a tie-out check; the accountant edits and the controller approves before it goes to management.
tasks.previous_blocker: The account mapping and commentary lived in people's heads and Excel; building a pipeline for a 10-person finance team was not worth the developer time.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes the mapping job and pack generator a few days of work, and models can draft commentary from journal text with numbers checked by code.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining why a variance happened often needs a call to a site manager; one-off events and accrual timing need judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which variance management will care about and saying what it means for the business, in the room.

ambition.what: A weekly flash of margin per site (Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo) including flex labour cost, not only month end.

tasks.altitude: The accountant stops building tables and spends the time on the three or four variances that matter; they own the account mapping and the materiality thresholds for commentary.

tasks.short: Prepare VAT returns and the corporate tax position from AFAS and file them with the tax office.
tasks.statement: Compute taxes owed and prepare tax returns, ensuring compliance with payment, reporting, or other tax requirements.
tasks.design: Configure the AFAS VAT return and Jonas checks, and add a scheduled Python job on the data platform that reconciles VAT accounts to the return and tests every invoice line (missing or wrong VAT code, reverse charge on agency and foreign invoices, ICP totals against intra-EU sales). Exceptions land in a list for the accountant; the corporate tax estimate stays a human workpaper, and filing and payment keep the controller's approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Checking every invoice line against VAT rules took too long by hand, so checks were sampled, and nobody had time to code the tests.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS Jonas now assists in tax returns including VAT from 2026, and AI coding makes line-level VAT tests cheap to write and maintain.
tasks.still_hard: Fiscal adjustments, provisions and positions on unclear cases need judgement and are on the human review list; no benchmark covers Dutch VAT.
tasks.human_edge: Taking a defensible position on a grey area and standing behind it with the tax office and auditor.

ambition.what: A monthly corporate tax provision estimate in the close instead of a year-end catch-up.

tasks.altitude: The accountant reviews exceptions instead of ticking lines and owns the VAT test set; filing rights stay with the controller.

tasks.short: Review balance sheet and profit and loss accounts each month for errors and unusual movements.
tasks.statement: Review data about material assets, net worth, liabilities, capital stock, surplus, income, or expenditures.
tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on the data platform reconciles every balance sheet account to AFAS sub-ledgers, Rabobank CAMT.053 statements and agency portal invoices, and a Power BI close dashboard shows breaks and movements above threshold. The accountant works only the flagged accounts and proposes adjusting entries; the controller approves them before posting in AFAS.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reconciliations were Excel files rebuilt each month, and the agency portals had no feed into AFAS.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes per-account reconciliation scripts and portal parsers quick to build; CAMT.053 files are a standard format.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding whether an unusual movement is an error, a timing issue or real business needs context; agency portal exports may change without notice.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising that a movement does not fit what is happening at a site and asking the right person.

ambition.what: Daily reconciliation of bank and flex worker accruals instead of once at month end.

tasks.altitude: The accountant moves from ticking reconciliations to owning the reconciliation rules and thresholds and investigating the breaks.

tasks.short: Test internal controls, investigate exceptions and write findings reports for management and the auditor.
tasks.statement: Prepare detailed reports on audit findings.
tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on the data platform tests every AFAS transaction and master data change (duplicate invoices, IBAN changes before payment, users who can both create vendors and approve payments) and writes results to a control dashboard. A bounded model step drafts findings in a fixed template with tie-out checks, and a SharePoint list tracks actions with Teams reminders to owners.
tasks.previous_blocker: Testing full populations needed scripting skills the team did not have, so controls were sampled by hand in Excel.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes full-population tests cheap to write, and models can draft finding text that code checks against test output.
tasks.still_hard: Interviewing owners, judging whether a control really failed and agreeing on fixes stay human; user rights data in AFAS may be hard to export cleanly.
tasks.human_edge: Judging severity, asking the uncomfortable question and getting an owner to fix the control.

ambition.what: Weekly IBAN-change and duplicate-payment checks before each Rabobank payment batch, not quarterly.

tasks.altitude: The accountant tests 100% of transactions and spends time on root causes; they own the control test catalogue and severity scale, with the controller signing reports.

tasks.short: Work out Noordhaven's corporate tax and VAT positions, depreciation differences and the tax provision each quarter and year-end.
tasks.statement: Evaluate taxpayer finances to determine tax liability, using knowledge of interest and discount rates, annuities, valuation of stocks and bonds, and amortization valuation of depletable assets.
tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform pulls the AFAS trial balance, asset register and VAT ledgers through the AFAS API, computes the fiscal adjustment schedule by fixed rules, and runs one bounded classification pass over unclear cost lines. It generates the tax workpaper in a fixed template on SharePoint; the accountant judges positions and signs, and AFAS Jonas is used for its checks when filing the returns.
tasks.previous_blocker: The fiscal rules lived in one person's Excel workbook, and booking descriptions were too free-form to classify by rules alone.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes a tested rule engine over the AFAS API cheap to build, and a model can tag free-text cost lines with a reason that a person can check; AFAS Jonas already assists with corporate tax and VAT returns.
tasks.still_hard: Uncertain positions (innovation box, interest limits, intercompany pricing if any) need judgement and the tax adviser; nothing tests models on Dutch tax.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which tax position the company takes and defending it to the tax adviser, the auditor and the Belastingdienst.

ambition.what: A tax provision updated each month-end instead of once a year, so the forecast includes a credible tax line.

tasks.altitude: The accountant stops rebuilding the workbook and spends the time on the three or four judgement calls; they own the fiscal rule set and sign off the provision before the controller sees it.

tasks.short: Review AFAS, bank and agency-portal processes and recommend controls that keep financial data reliable.
tasks.statement: Examine and evaluate financial and information systems, recommending controls to ensure system reliability and data integrity.
tasks.design: Nightly deterministic tests on the governed data platform run over every AFAS mutation, payment batch, CAMT.053 statement and agency invoice (segregation of duties, IBAN changes, duplicates, unmatched agency hours) and feed a Power BI exception dashboard. Findings are drafted by a bounded model step and tracked in a SharePoint list; walkthroughs and the advice stay with the accountant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Testing was sample-based in Excel because writing and maintaining full-population tests across AFAS, Rabobank files and three agency portals cost more than the team had.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes the test suite and connectors cheap to build and change; data already flows nightly to Power BI.
tasks.still_hard: Agency portals may lack APIs; deciding which exception is a real control weakness needs knowledge of how people work around the system.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing why people bypass a control and proposing one they will actually follow.

ambition.what: Continuous control monitoring: every payment and master-data change tested nightly instead of a yearly sample.

tasks.altitude: The accountant moves from sampling to triaging a daily exception list and decides which tests the company runs; they become the owner of the control test catalogue the auditor relies on.

tasks.short: Prepare and check monthly figures and the annual financial statements from AFAS for management, auditor and KVK.
tasks.statement: Prepare, analyze, or verify annual reports, financial statements, and other records, using accepted accounting and statistical procedures to assess financial condition and facilitate financial planning.
tasks.design: A close pipeline on the governed data platform pulls AFAS balances nightly, runs tie-outs against subledgers, CAMT.053 bank files and agency accruals, and generates the statements and notes from a maintained ledger mapping in a fixed template. A bounded model step drafts variance commentary with a number tie-out gate; the KVK filing via SBR runs through a separate filing tool since AFAS cannot file it.
tasks.previous_blocker: The mapping and tie-outs lived in yearly-copied Excel files, and commentary needed someone to dig through journals by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes a tested close pipeline cheap; models now draft commentary from journal detail, and benchmarked month-end scenarios show they follow instructions well when checked.
tasks.still_hard: Estimates (provisions, accruals for agency hours not yet invoiced) and audit discussions stay judgement; Dutch GAAP notes are not benchmarked.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the estimates and telling the auditor and the business what the numbers mean.

ambition.what: A management pack with tied-out figures and commentary on working day 3 instead of day 8.

tasks.altitude: The accountant reviews tie-out breaks and drafts instead of building workbooks; they decide the ledger mapping and the close calendar.

tasks.short: Check transactions against evidence and rules, and ask staff about exceptions, to confirm correct booking and compliance.
tasks.statement: Examine records and interview workers to ensure recording of transactions and compliance with laws and regulations.
tasks.design: A workflow on the governed data platform tests every agency invoice, payment and payroll journal instead of a sample: it pulls AFAS and portal data, extracts unstructured agency PDFs in a bounded step, and checks rates, hours, VAT, G-account splits and agency certificates by rule. Exceptions land in a Power BI list with a generated findings template; the accountant does the interviews and approves corrections.
tasks.previous_blocker: PDF invoices in three layouts and rules spread over contracts and CAOs made full testing too labour-intensive, so it was sampled.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction from PDFs with sum checks is now reliable enough, and AI coding makes the rule checks cheap to write and keep current.
tasks.still_hard: Interviews, unclear contract terms and deciding whether a deviation is an error or an agreed exception; payroll data is personal data under the AVG.
tasks.human_edge: Asking the right questions in an interview and judging whether an answer holds up.

ambition.what: Site managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo get a monthly list of their agency hours that do not match invoices.

tasks.altitude: The accountant spends the week on interviews and the exceptions that matter, not on sampling; they decide which compliance rules are tested and at what tolerance.

tasks.short: Analyse cost and revenue trends and commitments in Excel to project income and expenses and advise management.
tasks.statement: Analyze business operations, trends, costs, revenues, financial commitments, and obligations to project future revenues and expenses or to provide advice.
tasks.design: A nightly job on the governed data platform reads the AFAS GL and open items through the AFAS API. It writes a Power BI trend model per site and a driver-based projection in Python. A bounded model loop pulls commitments from SharePoint contracts into a schedule the accountant confirms, and drafts the movement section of the memo, which the accountant rewrites into advice.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contract commitments sat in free-text documents and the projection lived in personal Excel files, so automating either needed costly custom development.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes the AFAS-to-platform pipeline and projection code a matter of days. Models can pull contract fields with page references well enough to check them.
tasks.still_hard: Judging which trends will hold (season peaks, losing a customer, agency rates) and turning that into advice the business trusts. Projection errors cost money and are only seen later.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing the business behind the numbers: which customer is wobbling, which site manager is optimistic. Standing behind the advice in front of the Finance Director.

ambition.what: A monthly rolling cost and commitment outlook per site instead of an ad hoc analysis a few times a year

tasks.altitude: The accountant stops building the dataset and spends the time testing assumptions with site managers and FP&A. They gain ownership of the projection drivers.

tasks.short: Pull transaction data and test for weak controls, duplicates, waste, fraud and policy breaches.
tasks.statement: Collect and analyze data to detect deficient controls, duplicated effort, extravagance, fraud, or non-compliance with laws, regulations, and management policies.
tasks.design: Scheduled SQL and Python tests on the data platform run weekly over every AFAS payment, vendor master change, journal and Rabobank CAMT.053 statement. The results go to a Power BI exception dashboard with Teams notifications. A bounded model loop triages exceptions against the scanned invoices and agency hours, and drafts the findings. Interviews and findings stay with the accountant and the Controller.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tests ran as samples in Excel because full-population testing needed scripting skills and data access Finance did not have. Matching to scanned documents was manual.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding writes and maintains the test suite quickly. Models can read invoice scans and approval mails to triage, with a script checking every claimed match.
tasks.still_hard: Telling fraud from sloppy process, tuning thresholds so the list stays short, and handling people with care when a finding points at a colleague.
tasks.human_edge: Asking the right person the right question, reading reactions, and deciding whether something is an error, a control gap or fraud.

ambition.what: Weekly full-population control testing of all payments and vendor changes instead of yearly samples

tasks.altitude: The accountant moves from collecting samples to owning the test library and the follow-up of a short weekly exception list. They gain the right to propose control changes to the Controller.

tasks.short: Maintain budgets and prepare periodic budget-versus-actual reports per site and cost centre.
tasks.statement: Develop, maintain, or analyze budgets, preparing periodic reports that compare budgeted costs to actual costs.
tasks.design: Load the budget into AFAS budget tables and extend the existing Power BI finance model with a budget-versus-actual page per site and cost centre, refreshed nightly with an automated GL tie-out. A small workflow sends variances above threshold to budget holders by Teams. A bounded model loop turns their replies and the journal lines into draft commentary the accountant approves.
tasks.previous_blocker: The budget lived in a separate workbook, and nobody had time to build the mapping and the Power BI model. Explanations depended on chasing mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Power BI already runs on the nightly AFAS extract, so this is mostly configuration. AI coding speeds up the mapping and tie-out scripts, and a model can draft commentary from replies.
tasks.still_hard: Getting budget holders to answer, and deciding which variances signal a real change in the business rather than timing.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which variance matters and challenging a site manager's explanation.

ambition.what: Site and warehouse managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo get a self-service monthly budget view with commentary

tasks.altitude: The accountant stops building the report and spends the time on the few variances that matter and on reforecasts with FP&A.

tasks.short: Audit payroll and personnel records for correct premiums, wage tax, insurance and chain liability compliance.
tasks.statement: Audit payroll and personnel records to determine unemployment insurance premiums, workers' compensation coverage, liabilities, and compliance with tax laws.
tasks.design: A monthly Python job on the data platform reads payroll journals, wage tax returns and contract fields from AFAS, then applies coded rules: WW low or high premium per contract, the 30% overtime recalculation, and Zvw and sector premiums. It reconciles the results to the GL and the Rabobank payment. A second rule set checks agency invoices against portal hours, NEN 4400-1 registration and G-account splits. Exceptions go to a restricted Power BI page; corrections and any supplementary return stay with the Payroll Specialist and the accountant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Premium rules change yearly and the data is special-category personal data, so checks stayed as annual samples in Excel run by one person.
tasks.enabler_now: The rules are fixed and written down, and AI coding makes it cheap to write them as tests and update them each January. AFAS and the agency portals provide exports or APIs.
tasks.still_hard: Edge cases in contracts (on-call, mixed hours), access control over BSN and absence data, and corrections that go to the tax office and cannot be undone.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a deviation is an error to correct with the Belastingdienst, and agreeing it with Payroll and the Controller.

ambition.what: Every monthly payroll run checked for WW premium category and chain liability before the wage tax return is filed

tasks.altitude: The accountant moves from yearly sample audits to reviewing a monthly exception list, and owns the premium rule set together with the Payroll Specialist.

tasks.short: Advise the Finance Director and HR on the cost of pay, benefit, tax or system choices.
tasks.statement: Advise clients in areas such as compensation, employee health care benefits, the design of accounting or data processing systems, or long-range tax or estate plans.
tasks.design: A scheduled extract on the governed data platform joins AFAS payroll, headcount and ledger data with agency hours into one cost baseline. A parameterised scenario workbook (CAO rise, pension premium, flex share) reads it, and a bounded model step drafts the memo with every figure tied back to the model.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each question needed a fresh hand-built extract from AFAS and agency portals, so there was no stable baseline to reuse.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes a reusable extract and scenario model cheap to build; a model can draft the explanatory text once figures are fixed.
tasks.still_hard: Questions vary a lot, and long-range tax or pension advice depends on judgement and on rules that change.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what the Finance Director and HR actually need to decide, and saying clearly where the numbers are uncertain.

ambition.what: Cost every CAO or flex-mix proposal before each OR or negotiation meeting, not only once a year.

tasks.altitude: Less time building spreadsheets, more time in the room where pay and staffing choices are made; the accountant owns the cost model used in those decisions.

tasks.short: Test whether new or changed finance systems and interfaces will post and control correctly before go-live.
tasks.statement: Conduct pre-implementation audits to determine if systems and programs under development will work as planned.
tasks.design: A reusable test harness in Python posts scripted test transactions through the AFAS Profit connectors into the test environment and compares results with expected postings, VAT codes and approval flows. A bounded model step turns design documents into a draft risk list; the accountant signs the go-live advice.
tasks.previous_blocker: Test runs were manual clicks in AFAS and comparison in Excel, too slow to repeat after each design change.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes a scripted AFAS test harness quick to build and to extend per project.
tasks.still_hard: Spotting what the design leaves out, and getting a test environment with realistic data.
tasks.human_edge: Judging which control gaps matter for the audit and the close, and saying no to a go-live.

ambition.what: Rerun the full finance regression test before every AFAS update, not only for big projects.

tasks.altitude: From clicking through test cases to designing the test set and owning go-live sign-off for finance controls.

tasks.short: Report on asset use and audit results to management and recommend changes.
tasks.statement: Report to management about asset utilization and audit results, and recommend changes in operations and financial activities.
tasks.design: A nightly job joins the AFAS fixed asset register with ledger and fleet or forklift usage data and feeds a Power BI page on use, idle assets and book value per site. Audit findings move from a mail-and-Excel log into a SharePoint list with owners and due dates, and a bounded model step drafts the commentary with a tie-out gate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Usage data sits outside AFAS and had to be matched by hand to asset numbers each time.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes the matching job and the Power BI page cheap; Power BI and SharePoint are already licensed.
tasks.still_hard: Usage data from fleet and warehouse equipment may lack asset numbers, so matching needs a mapping someone maintains.
tasks.human_edge: Recommending which assets to sell, move between Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, or replace, and holding owners to audit actions.

ambition.what: A monthly idle-asset review per site instead of a yearly report.

tasks.altitude: From assembling the report to running a monthly asset review with site managers; the accountant proposes disposals and transfers.

tasks.short: Key supplier and agency invoices into AFAS, match them to orders or hours, post them, and pull lists into Excel.
tasks.statement: Operate computers programmed with accounting software to record, store, and analyze information.
tasks.design: Turn on AFAS UBL intake and Scan & herken so one-to-one matches post and approve themselves; a small extraction loop handles PDFs that AFAS cannot read and fails to a queue. A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform matches the three agencies' invoices to the hours in their portals and AFAS, and a Power BI page replaces the Excel open-items exports.
tasks.previous_blocker: Many PDFs from small suppliers, agency invoices that need hours from three portals, and no one owning match rules or tolerances.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS Profit 8 reads UBL and PDF to line level and books one-to-one matches; AI coding makes the agency hours matcher a few days of work; models read odd PDFs well enough when checked against totals.
tasks.still_hard: Agency portals without a stable export, partial deliveries, and suppliers who keep sending PDFs; the touchless share will be lower than vendors claim.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which supplier or agency is sloppy, and calling them to fix a recurring error at the source.

ambition.what: Check every agency invoice line against worked hours before payment, instead of spot checks.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper works an exception queue instead of keying, and gains the right to set match tolerances and block supplier records with bad master data.

tasks.short: Check postings, VAT codes, ledger accounts and sums for errors, and correct them before close.
tasks.statement: Check figures, postings, and documents for correct entry, mathematical accuracy, and proper codes.
tasks.design: A nightly rule job on the AFAS extract checks every posting for VAT code against supplier country and type, account against the supplier's usual account, duplicates and IBAN changes, and posts the hits to a Power BI exception page with a Teams notice. AFAS bank matching stays the first line; a bounded model loop proposes matches for the leftover bank lines, and the bookkeeper accepts and corrects.
tasks.previous_blocker: Checks lived in personal Excel sheets run before close, so errors were found weeks late and rules were never written down.
tasks.enabler_now: The nightly AFAS extract already feeds Power BI; rule checks are quick to code; models can read free-text bank descriptions under a sum check.
tasks.still_hard: Writing the norms per supplier and VAT case (reverse charge, intra-EU) and keeping them current; false alarms will need tuning in the first months.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether an odd posting is an error, a one-off deal, or a sign of fraud, and talking to the budget holder about it.

ambition.what: Check every posting daily instead of a sample at month end, which takes days off the close.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper reviews a daily exception list and owns the check rules with the controller; they can hold a payment when an IBAN change is not confirmed.

tasks.short: Assign ledger account, cost centre, site and VAT code to each invoice per the coding procedure.
tasks.statement: Code documents according to company procedures.
tasks.design: Set default ledger account, cost centre and VAT code on every regular supplier in AFAS so most invoices code themselves, and move approval from email into the AFAS approval workflow with reminders. A small model loop proposes codes only for new suppliers and free-text lines, checked against the allowed code list, and the bookkeeper confirms.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier defaults were never maintained, the procedure sat in a SharePoint document, and approvals ran by email, so coding was done by memory.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS supports supplier defaults and digital approval out of the box; models can classify free-text lines against a fixed code list with a check.
tasks.still_hard: Mixed invoices that span sites or cost types, and budget holders on warehouse shifts who do not open AFAS.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding the right code when an invoice is genuinely unclear and agreeing it with the controller so it stays consistent.

ambition.what: Spend by site and cost type that the FP&A analysts can trust daily, because coding is consistent.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains supplier defaults and the code list instead of coding line by line, and decides when a new supplier gets a default.

tasks.short: Calculate amounts due, payment discounts, late interest, g-rekening splits and balances for payments and customers.
tasks.statement: Perform financial calculations, such as amounts due, interest charges, balances, discounts, equity, and principal.
tasks.design: Configure payment terms, discounts, dunning and interest calculation in AFAS so the payment proposal and interest invoices come out of the system, with a check that no small supplier gets terms over 30 days. Deterministic code on the agency invoice applies the agreed wage tax and VAT share to the g-rekening and adds it to the payment batch; the bookkeeper approves the batch in Rabobank after reviewing IBAN-name warnings and new payees.
tasks.previous_blocker: Terms and agency percentages were kept in Excel, interest was charged by hand when someone noticed, and the g-rekening split was keyed per invoice.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS already does terms, discounts and dunning when set up; the g-rekening split is a few lines of code; the bank IBAN-name check flags wrong payees.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing with sales whether to charge interest to key customers, and keeping agency g-rekening percentages and statements current.
tasks.human_edge: Approving money leaving the bank and deciding when a warning is real; choosing with collections when charging interest hurts a customer relationship.

ambition.what: Apply late-payment interest and early-payment discounts on every eligible invoice instead of when noticed.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper approves batches and maintains terms and g-rekening percentages instead of calculating; they gain a say with collections on interest waivers.

tasks.short: Select due payables, calculate amounts and splits, build the payment batch and send it to Rabobank.
tasks.statement: Calculate and prepare checks for utilities, taxes, and other payments.
tasks.design: Configure the AFAS payment proposal to select due items by term, with a 30-day flag for small suppliers. A small deterministic job on the AFAS data checks IBAN changes against the supplier change log, duplicates by amount, date and invoice number, and the g-rekening share from the agency invoice. Only exceptions go to the bookkeeper, and the controller signs the batch in Rabobank as today.
tasks.previous_blocker: The g-rekening split, tax payments and fraud checks lived in Excel and in people's heads, so the AFAS proposal could not be trusted without a full manual pass.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS proposals and the bank file are standard. The checks are simple rules that can now be coded and tested in days, and the IBAN-Name Check adds a bank-side signal.
tasks.still_hard: Agency invoices with a varying g-rekening percentage, one-off tax assessments and urgent manual payments stay exceptions. Payments are irreversible, so the signing gate stays.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding what to do with a suspicious IBAN change or a name-check warning, and calling the supplier on a known number, is a judgement about fraud risk that stays with a person.

ambition.what: Run the payment batch twice a week instead of weekly, so that small suppliers are paid well within the legal 30 days.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper reviews an exception list instead of building the batch line by line, and owns the duplicate and IBAN-change rules. The controller keeps the signing right.

tasks.short: Tick AFAS reports against Excel side-lists and journals, find differences and correct them.
tasks.statement: Compare computer printouts to manually maintained journals to determine if they match.
tasks.design: Move the Excel side-lists (accruals, manual journals, agency hours) into a small governed app or AFAS free tables, then run a nightly Python job on the data platform that pulls AFAS connectors and agency portal exports and matches them by rule. A bounded model step suggests causes for unmatched lines, and a Power BI exception page shows the bookkeeper only what is left.
tasks.previous_blocker: The side-lists were kept in Excel because AFAS had no place for them, and the matching rules differed per list and per person.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS connectors and the nightly Power BI extract already exist, AI coding makes a matching job and a small entry app cheap to build, and a model can read free-text descriptions for the remaining lines.
tasks.still_hard: Agency portal exports differ per agency and change without notice. Getting people to stop keeping their own Excel lists is a habit change, not a technical one.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a difference is an error, a timing issue or a sign of something wrong at a supplier, and who must fix it, stays with the bookkeeper.

ambition.what: Reconcile subledgers, bank and agency hours daily instead of at month end, so the close starts with few open differences.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper works from a short exception list each morning and owns the match rules and tolerances. They gain the right to set tolerances within limits agreed with the controller.

tasks.short: Answer supplier and internal questions about invoices, payments and account balances by looking them up in AFAS.
tasks.statement: Access computerized financial information to answer general questions as well as those related to specific accounts.
tasks.design: Route the AP shared mailbox through a small workflow that classifies each mail, looks up the invoice in AFAS via its connectors and drafts a reply in Outlook for the bookkeeper to approve. Internal budget holders get a Power BI page on the nightly AFAS extract showing open invoices and approval status for their cost centre, so their questions stop.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every question needed a person to search AFAS screens, and there was no safe way to read free-text mails or to expose AP data to budget holders.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS connectors give read access to invoice and payment status, models can classify mails and draft short replies, and Power BI already runs on an AFAS extract.
tasks.still_hard: Questions about disputed invoices, credit notes or changed bank details need a person. Showing data to budget holders needs row-level security per cost centre.
tasks.human_edge: Handling an annoyed supplier, a disputed amount or a request to change bank details needs judgement and relationship care.

ambition.what: Give site and department budget holders in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo a self-service view of their open invoices and approval status.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper approves drafted replies in batches and keeps the hard conversations. Nothing changes in their decision rights.

tasks.short: Check aging, loan and lease schedules and supplier terms so that payments in and out are up to date.
tasks.statement: Monitor status of loans and accounts to ensure that payments are up to date.
tasks.design: Build a Power BI page on the nightly AFAS extract with AP and AR aging, loan and lease instalments matched to bank lines, and invoices stuck in approval near the 30-day limit. A scheduled job sends a Teams message to the right owner (collections, approver or controller) for each new flag, so the tracking sheet goes away.
tasks.previous_blocker: Loan and lease schedules sat in Excel outside AFAS, and nobody had built the rules that link instalments to bank lines.
tasks.enabler_now: The Power BI extract runs nightly already, and the rules are simple enough to code quickly with AI help.
tasks.still_hard: Loan and lease schedules must be loaded once and kept current when contracts change. Deciding what to do about a late customer remains collections work.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing whom to chase and how firmly, and seeing when a late payer signals a bigger problem, stays human.

ambition.what: Review overdue items and approval delays daily instead of weekly, so no small supplier passes the 30-day term.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper stops running reports and keeps a short daily list of follow-ups. Nothing changes in their decision rights.

tasks.short: Check each supplier and agency invoice against the order, goods receipt or hours, then record it in AFAS.
tasks.statement: Match order forms with invoices, and record the necessary information.
tasks.design: Switch on AFAS Profit UBL intake, Scan & herken and line-level three-way matching with set tolerances, so one-to-one matches are posted and released for approval without a touch. A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform reads agency portal hours, checks agency invoices, proposes the g-rekening split and posts only differences to a review queue. A small model step classifies the remaining exceptions and drafts the query for the bookkeeper to send.
tasks.previous_blocker: Many invoices arrived as PDF, goods receipts were registered late at the sites, and agency hours lived in three portals outside AFAS.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS reads UBL and PDF invoices to line level and posts one-to-one matches; AI coding makes the small agency-hours job cheap to build.
tasks.still_hard: Late or missing goods receipts at the warehouses and agency invoices that do not line up with approved hours stay a people problem.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a price or hours difference is acceptable, and settling it with a site manager or agency without souring the relationship.

ambition.what: Weekly check of every agency invoice against approved hours and g-rekening split, instead of spot checks at month end

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper stops opening matched invoices and spends the week on exceptions and on setting match tolerances and supplier master data with the controller.

tasks.short: Key debits and credits into AFAS and total accounts in Excel to check they balance.
tasks.statement: Debit, credit, and total accounts on computer spreadsheets and databases, using specialized accounting software.
tasks.design: Replace hand keying with a fixed Excel journal template that a script validates (balanced, valid accounts, cost centres, VAT codes) and posts through the AFAS import connector as unapproved entries for a second person to release. Recurring entries move into AFAS periodic journals, and the Excel totalling is replaced by a Power BI balance check page on the nightly AFAS extract.
tasks.previous_blocker: Workings came in many Excel layouts, and nobody owned a template or import routine, so keying was the safe default.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS connectors and AI-assisted coding make a validated import script a few days of work; Power BI already reads AFAS nightly.
tasks.still_hard: Getting colleagues to use one template, and the corrections that need judgement on accounts and periods.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which account and period an odd item belongs to and spotting an entry that balances but is wrong.
tasks.altitude: Less keying; the bookkeeper releases imported batches and handles corrections, with no new decision rights.

tasks.short: Assign ledger account, cost centre and VAT code to transactions and summarise records for the close.
tasks.statement: Classify, record, and summarize numerical and financial data to compile and keep financial records, using journals and ledgers or computers.
tasks.design: Set supplier default coding in AFAS for fixed suppliers and add a bounded model step that suggests coding for the rest, checked against an allowed-account table and VAT rules, with the bookkeeper confirming. Bank lines and costs are booked by AFAS bank rules, and the Excel summaries become a Power BI page per site on the nightly extract, with drill-down to the coded line and the reason.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coding depended on each bookkeeper's memory of suppliers and sites, and own accounts and VAT codes made rule sets incomplete.
tasks.enabler_now: Coding suggestions from vendor history are now common in AP tools, and a checked suggestion step can be built cheaply around AFAS data.
tasks.still_hard: Mixed invoices across sites and new suppliers; touchless rates often fall short of vendor claims.
tasks.human_edge: Judging the right account and VAT treatment for unusual purchases and explaining the choice to the controller or auditor.

ambition.what: Site managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo get a weekly cost-per-site view they never had

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper confirms suggestions and maintains supplier defaults and the allowed-account table, a decision right shared with the controller.

tasks.short: Copy figures from agency, expense and other side journals into AFAS or Excel data sheets.
tasks.statement: Transfer details from separate journals to general ledgers or data processing sheets.
tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform fetches agency and expense files, maps them to AFAS accounts and cost centres with a maintained mapping table, and posts them through the AFAS connector as unapproved journals. The job ties source totals to posted totals, sends rejected lines to the bookkeeper in Teams, and the bookkeeper releases each batch.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each source had its own layout and no IT capacity existed for small interfaces, so Excel was the glue.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes small file-to-connector jobs cheap; AFAS connectors accept journal imports.
tasks.still_hard: Agency portals change layouts without notice and some may only offer manual downloads.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when a source file is incomplete or a mapping no longer fits, and deciding whether to post or hold.

ambition.what: Flex labour cost posted weekly per site instead of once at month end

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper stops copying and owns the mapping table and the batch release; days to close shorten because flex costs are already in.

tasks.short: Match bank, ledger and agency invoice lines; chase and report what does not match.
tasks.statement: Reconcile or note and report discrepancies found in records.
tasks.design: Turn on and tune AFAS bank matching with tolerances, and replace the reconciliation Excel sheets with a scheduled Python job on a governed data platform that reads AFAS open items, ledger balances and the three agency portals' hours and invoices. A bounded model step proposes matches for leftover bank lines; everything that stays unmatched lands in one queue and a Power BI page the controller reads at close.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agency portal data and AFAS lived in separate exports joined by hand in Excel, and free-text bank descriptions defeated fixed rules.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS matching rules already cover the bulk [S3]; scripting the portal and AFAS joins is now cheap to build, and a small model can read free-text bank descriptions.
tasks.still_hard: Getting stable exports from three agency portals, and partial or combined payments from customers that no rule or model can resolve without asking.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a difference is an error, a dispute or a fraud signal, and who should be asked about it.

ambition.what: Daily instead of monthly reconciliation of agency invoices against hours, so overbilling is caught before payment.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper spends the week on a short exception queue and owns match rules and tolerances; they can set tolerances within limits agreed with the controller.

tasks.short: Post payroll journal, pay net wages, wage tax and pension, reconcile payroll accounts.
tasks.statement: Prepare and process payroll information.
tasks.design: Payroll and ledger are both in AFAS Profit, so configure the payroll run to post its journal straight to the general ledger with site cost centres and to create the payment batches. A small deterministic check compares batch totals to payroll totals and flags new or changed employee IBANs before the finance director approves the batch in Rabobank; clearing account balances show on a Power BI page.
tasks.previous_blocker: Payroll and finance worked as separate hand-offs by mail and Excel, and nobody owned the configuration of the automatic journal link.
tasks.enabler_now: The link is a configuration in software Noordhaven already owns; the checks are a few rules that are quick to write.
tasks.still_hard: Off-cycle corrections, flex and shift allowances under two CAOs, and keeping the cost centre mapping right when sites change.
tasks.human_edge: Approving money leaving the bank and judging whether a payroll difference is a real error before employees are paid.
tasks.altitude: Little changes for the bookkeeper's week beyond less checking; they keep the reconciliation and the IBAN-change check.

tasks.short: Calculate customer charges for storage and transport, issue invoices and send account statements.
tasks.statement: Calculate, prepare, and issue bills, invoices, account statements, and other financial statements according to established procedures.
tasks.design: Move the contract rates from Excel into AFAS (or a rate table on the data platform) and let a scheduled job read operations exports, price them and create invoice proposals in AFAS. The bookkeeper approves the batch only where it deviates from last month by more than a set margin; AFAS sends invoices and monthly statements on its own schedule.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customer rates sit in contracts and Excel, and billable activity comes from operations systems that never fed AFAS directly.
tasks.enabler_now: A pricing script and export reader are now days of work, and AFAS already sends invoices and statements once data is clean.
tasks.still_hard: Customer-specific contract clauses, minimum charges and ad-hoc jobs that operations do not record consistently.
tasks.human_edge: Judging a disputed charge with the customer and deciding on a credit note.

ambition.what: Invoice storage and transport weekly instead of monthly to lower days sales outstanding.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper reviews outlier batches and owns the rate table; they can hold a batch but rate changes stay with the controller and sales.

tasks.short: Enter purchase orders from requests and process staff expense claims with receipts.
tasks.statement: Prepare purchase orders and expense reports.
tasks.design: Configure AFAS InSite purchase requests and expense claims so requesters enter their own orders and claims, with approval workflows by cost centre and budget limits. Receipts uploaded with a claim pass through a bounded extraction step that fills amount, VAT and a suggested account; policy rules flag exceptions for the bookkeeper and approved claims flow to payroll or the payment run.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrive by mail from three sites, approvals sit in inboxes, and receipts are paper or photos that need retyping.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS workflows are configuration; receipt reading by a small model with VAT arithmetic checks is now reliable enough for a review queue.
tasks.still_hard: Getting site managers to use the request screen instead of email, and receipts with mixed VAT rates or foreign VAT.
tasks.human_edge: Saying no to a claim outside policy, or making a fair exception, with the employee's manager.

ambition.what: Shift leads and drivers can file expenses from their phone instead of handing in paper receipts at the office.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper stops typing orders and claims and handles a small exception queue; they can reject claims that break policy.

tasks.short: Work out costs of materials, overhead and expenses from quotes and price lists, and check invoices against them.
tasks.statement: Calculate costs of materials, overhead, and other expenses, based on estimates, quotations and price lists.
tasks.design: Replace the Excel cost sheet with a small price-register app on the governed data platform, fed by a bounded extraction loop for PDF quotes and rate cards and approved by the bookkeeper. A scheduled Python job computes costs and overhead allocations per site from AFAS volumes and checks every incoming AFAS invoice line against the register, sending only deviations above tolerance to the bookkeeper; results feed a Power BI page for controller and FP&A.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prices live in mails, PDFs and personal Excel sheets with no structure, so there was nothing to check invoices against automatically.
tasks.enabler_now: Models read free-form quotes well enough for a checked extraction loop, and AI-assisted coding makes a small register app and checking job a matter of days.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping the register current when rates change by phone or mail, and agreeing allocation keys for shared overhead across the three sites.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a price deviation is a supplier error, a valid surcharge or a change someone agreed without telling finance, and raising it with the buyer.

ambition.what: Price check on every supplier and agency invoice line instead of spot checks on large invoices.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper stops retyping prices and spends the time on deviations; they gain the right to hold an invoice that breaks agreed rates and to approve register changes.

tasks.short: Match daily Rabobank statement lines to open invoices and ledger postings in AFAS and clear differences.
tasks.statement: Reconcile records of bank transactions.
tasks.design: Set up the AFAS automatic CAMT.053 import and tune its matching rules and tolerances so most lines clear without touch. A scheduled job on the remaining lines runs a bounded model loop that reads descriptions and remittance mails and proposes matches that must sum exactly; the bookkeeper approves in AFAS, and a daily Teams notification lists open lines older than three days to collections.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rules only cover clean references; free-text descriptions, combined payments and remittance advice in mailboxes needed a person to read them.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS already offers rule-based bank matching with tolerances, and a model can read the leftover free text while the amount check keeps it safe.
tasks.still_hard: Customers who pay many invoices in one amount without reference, and agency payments split between normal account and g-rekening.
tasks.human_edge: Judging unknown receipts and deciding when to call a customer or supplier, and booking differences that affect the ledger.

ambition.what: Daily instead of weekly reconciliation, so DSO and cash position are current every morning.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper reviews a short exception list each morning instead of matching for hours; they own the matching rules and tolerances in AFAS.

tasks.short: Build AP, AR, cash and P&L tables and reports from AFAS exports in Excel.
tasks.statement: Compile statistical, financial, accounting, or auditing reports and tables pertaining to such matters as cash receipts, expenditures, accounts payable and receivable, and profits and losses.
tasks.design: Move the recurring AP, AR and cash tables into Power BI on the nightly AFAS extract, with subscriptions instead of mailed Excel files. A scheduled job ties report totals to the trial balance and blocks publication on a mismatch, and a bounded loop drafts comments on top movements for the bookkeeper to edit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports grew as personal Excel files with manual tweaks, and nobody had time to rebuild them in Power BI.
tasks.enabler_now: The nightly AFAS extract in Power BI already exists, AI-assisted building makes report pages quick, and models can draft checked variance comments.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing one definition per report with the controller and retiring the old Excel versions people trust.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which movements matter to the business and what is behind them, from talks with sites and suppliers.

ambition.what: Site managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo get their own weekly AP and cost view for the first time.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper no longer builds tables; they check comments and answer questions on the numbers, and own the report definitions with the controller.

tasks.short: Run and check the month-end trial balance in AFAS before handing it to the accountant and controller.
tasks.statement: Prepare trial balances of books.
tasks.design: A scheduled job on the AFAS extract runs a close checklist daily in the last week: postings complete, suspense and intercompany balances zero, balances within expected ranges, and sends a Teams status to the bookkeeper and controller. Flagged accounts get a bounded loop that explains the cause and drafts a balancing correction, which the bookkeeper posts or rejects in AFAS.
tasks.previous_blocker: AFAS produces the trial balance, but the checks around it lived in a personal Excel checklist and in people's heads.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding turns the Excel checklist into scheduled checks quickly, and models can read posting descriptions to explain odd balances.
tasks.still_hard: Setting expected ranges per account without many false alarms, and accruals that depend on information outside AFAS.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which corrections are right and taking responsibility for the books toward the accountant and auditor.

ambition.what: A daily soft trial balance in the closing week instead of one check at month end, cutting days to close.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper starts close with a clean list of exceptions rather than hunting; they gain the right to sign off completeness before the accountant takes over.

tasks.short: Gather actuals, prior budgets and site estimates into the budget workbook for FP&A.
tasks.statement: Compile budget data and documents, based on estimated revenues and expenses and previous budgets.
tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform reads the AFAS general ledger and prior budget, applies a maintained account-to-budget-line mapping and writes the budget pack to SharePoint. Site estimates come in through a Microsoft Forms or Power Apps entry screen with reminders, and a bounded model step drafts variance notes from site comments for the bookkeeper to check before FP&A gets the pack.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inputs come from many site managers by mail in their own formats, and the mapping lived in one person's spreadsheet. Building and keeping a pipeline for a task of about 30 hours per FTE a year was not worth it.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes a small mapping job and entry form a matter of days, and the AFAS extract already exists for Power BI. A language model can draft the short variance notes from free-text comments.
tasks.still_hard: Site managers still send late or vague estimates, and judging whether an estimate is realistic stays with FP&A and the controller. The mapping table must be kept up to date when cost centres change.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which site estimate is padded or missing a known event, such as a new customer contract or a peak season flex plan, and calling the site manager about it.

ambition.what: A refreshed budget-versus-actual pack every month instead of only at the yearly and quarterly budget rounds, so FP&A can reforecast sooner.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper no longer builds the workbook; they own the mapping table, check flagged lines and talk to sites about missing input. FP&A remains the owner of the budget.

tasks.short: Record stock of packaging, pallets and consumables in the ledger and reconcile it to counts.
tasks.statement: Maintain inventory records.
tasks.design: A scheduled job reads count and movement exports from the warehouse systems and purchase lines from AFAS, values stock with fixed rules and produces a draft stock journal through the AFAS connector. Differences above a tolerance show on a Power BI page per site, and the bookkeeper approves the journal before it posts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counts arrive by mail as site spreadsheets in different layouts, and stock is a side task with small volume, so nobody built an interface.
tasks.enabler_now: Cheap custom code for file parsing and the AFAS connectors, plus the existing Power BI setup, make a small reconciliation job affordable.
tasks.still_hard: Count quality at the sites, missing movements, and pallet exchanges with customers and carriers that are not recorded anywhere structured.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding with the site manager whether a difference is a counting error, a booking error or a real loss, and what to write off.

ambition.what: Monthly stock and pallet balances per site instead of quarterly, so write-offs are found while they can still be traced.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper stops typing counts and checks a difference list instead; they own the valuation rules and tolerances and approve the journal.

tasks.short: Prepare and file VAT and ICP returns, statistics and agency liability papers to Belastingdienst and others.
tasks.statement: Complete and submit tax forms and returns, workers' compensation forms, pension contribution forms, and other government documents.
tasks.design: Use the VAT and ICP reporting and digital submission already in AFAS, and add a scheduled rule job that flags suspicious VAT lines, with a bounded model step that proposes a code from the invoice text for the bookkeeper to accept. A small tracker on SharePoint or the data platform requests and records agency payment-behaviour statements and checks each agency payment batch for the g-rekening split, alerting the bookkeeper to gaps.
tasks.previous_blocker: VAT checks need reading invoices for edge cases, and agency liability papers arrive by mail on no fixed schedule, so the work stayed manual in Excel and Outlook.
tasks.enabler_now: Rule jobs on AFAS data are cheap to build now, and a model can read invoice text to propose a VAT code within a fixed list. Coming e-invoicing and 5-day reporting pressure make early checks worth more.
tasks.still_hard: Unusual cross-border cases and corrections of earlier periods need tax knowledge. Filing is irreversible and the company carries the liability, so a person must approve every submission.
tasks.human_edge: Signing for a filing to the tax office and judging grey cases (place of supply, corrections, agency liability) with the controller or tax adviser.

ambition.what: A continuous VAT and agency-liability check that runs weekly, ready for the coming Dutch e-invoicing reporting with its short deadlines.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper reviews a short exception list and approves filings instead of checking every line; they own the VAT rule table and the agency liability file.

tasks.short: Log call outcomes, promises to pay, disputes and customer credit facts in Excel tracker and AFAS notes.
tasks.statement: Record information about financial status of customers and status of collection efforts.
tasks.design: Replace the Excel collections tracker with a small case app on the governed data platform that reads AFAS open items through the API and writes notes back to AFAS debtor records. A bounded model step turns call notes into structured outcomes the officer confirms; a nightly job checks KvK changes and insurer limits; the Power BI finance model gets a collections page instead of the weekly mail.
tasks.previous_blocker: The tracker sits between AFAS and Outlook and nobody owned an integration; free-text notes could not be structured cheaply.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS has a REST connector, AI-assisted coding makes a small case app a matter of days, and models extract amount and date from short notes reliably enough to confirm in one click.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping one source of truth when sales and operations also talk to the same shipper; insurer portals may lack an API.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a promise is credible and what a customer's tone means for the next step.

ambition.what: Weekly credit-limit review per top-50 shipper instead of a yearly check

tasks.altitude: The officer stops typing logs and spends the saved two hours a week reviewing broken promises and limit changes, with the right to propose limit changes to the Controller.

tasks.short: Export AFAS open items, build ageing and priority list in Excel, check payments, pick whom to chase.
tasks.statement: Locate and monitor overdue accounts, using computers and a variety of automated systems.
tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform pulls AFAS open items and the latest bank match status each morning, applies ageing and priority rules (amount, days overdue, broken promise, insurer limit) and fills a daily work queue in the collections case app plus a Power BI ageing page. AFAS auto-matching is tuned first so paid items drop out before the list is built.
tasks.previous_blocker: The ageing logic lived in one person's Excel; AFAS reports were not trusted because bank matching lagged.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS bank-statement auto-match rules can be configured, and AI coding makes a rule-based priority job cheap to build and change.
tasks.still_hard: Unmatched receipts still need a bookkeeper; priority rules need tuning with the officer's judgement for the first months.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which shipper pays late but always pays, and which silence means trouble.

ambition.what: Daily re-prioritised chase list instead of a weekly Excel refresh

tasks.altitude: The officer starts the day with a ready queue and owns the priority rules with the Controller, adjusting weights monthly.

tasks.short: Send reminders and final notices by mail, phone debtors who stay late to get payment.
tasks.statement: Locate and notify customers of delinquent accounts by mail, telephone, or personal visits to solicit payment.
tasks.design: Configure AFAS dunning with Noordhaven's reminder sequence and Dutch/English templates so standard reminders go out without touch; a deterministic generator on the data platform drafts final notices with BW 6:119a interest and the EUR 40 minimum, which the officer approves. Before each call the case app shows a brief built from AFAS data plus a bounded model summary of the mail thread.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reminders were tailored by hand because templates and contract terms varied per shipper, and interest calculations were done in Excel.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS dunning is standard functionality; statutory interest is pure rules; models summarise mail threads well enough for a brief a person reads.
tasks.still_hard: Customer-specific payment terms must be clean in AFAS first; calls stay human and take most of the time.
tasks.human_edge: Persuading a shipper on the phone, reading their situation and keeping the commercial relationship intact.

ambition.what: Small shippers under EUR 5k get a timely reminder sequence for the first time instead of being skipped

tasks.altitude: The officer's week shifts from writing letters to calls with the 30-40 accounts that matter, with the right to approve every final notice.

tasks.short: Answer shipper mails and calls about invoices, statements, delivery proof and disputed charges.
tasks.statement: Answer customer questions regarding problems with their accounts.
tasks.design: Put a bounded classifier on the shared debtors mailbox that tags requests and invoice numbers, after which deterministic code pulls statements and invoice copies from AFAS and proof of delivery from SharePoint and sends standard replies from templates. Explanations get a model draft for approval, and disputes open a case in the collections app that routes to sales or operations and to a bookkeeper for credit notes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrive as free text in mixed Dutch and English, and documents sit in three places, so rules alone could not sort them.
tasks.enabler_now: Models classify short business mails reliably within a checkable output, and AFAS plus SharePoint can be read by API.
tasks.still_hard: Proof of delivery may sit in a transport system outside the listed ones; disputes over damage and surcharges need operations input.
tasks.human_edge: Resolving a disputed charge fairly while keeping the shipper as a customer.

ambition.what: Self-service statement and invoice copy link for shippers, sent automatically on request

tasks.altitude: Routine document requests disappear from the officer's day; they gain the right to log dispute causes and report them monthly to sales and operations.

tasks.short: Call and mail overdue shippers, explain the claim, and agree payment, a plan or a return.
tasks.statement: Persuade customers to pay amounts due on credit accounts, damage claims, or nonpayable checks, or to return merchandise.
tasks.design: A collections workbench on the governed data platform reads AFAS ageing nightly, ranks accounts and assembles a dispute file per debtor with a bounded model summary of Outlook threads. The officer calls with the file open, confirms model-extracted outcome fields that write back to AFAS, and sends template confirmations; Finance Director approves plans above a set amount.
tasks.previous_blocker: Dispute evidence is spread over mailboxes, SharePoint and AFAS, and summarising free-text mails needed a person; bespoke tooling was too costly for one officer.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes a small workbench cheap to build, and language models can summarise mail threads with citations that are checked against AFAS.
tasks.still_hard: Proof of delivery and damage-claim status often live with operations in other systems; summaries that miss a promise can damage a relationship.
tasks.human_edge: Reading a shipper's real situation on the phone, choosing when to press and when to give time, and keeping a commercial relationship intact.

ambition.what: A promise-to-pay or plan agreed with every overdue shipper above EUR 1,000 each week, not only the largest accounts.

tasks.altitude: Most of the week becomes conversations with prepared files; the officer gains the right to agree plans within a limit without asking.

tasks.short: Import bank statements, match payments to open invoices in AFAS, and clear the mismatches.
tasks.statement: Receive payments and post amounts paid to customer accounts.
tasks.design: Turn on the automatic Rabobank feed and AFAS auto-match rules, then route the remaining unmatched payments to a small queue where a bounded model loop reads remittance mails and proposes matches that must pass sum and open-item checks. The officer approves proposals and books differences; a Power BI page replaces the daily cash sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: Remittance advices come as free-format mails and PDFs, so the tail of unmatched payments needed a person reading each one.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS already matches on rules [S4]; models can now extract invoice numbers from messy advices, with arithmetic checks catching errors.
tasks.still_hard: Netted payments, credit notes and payer entities that differ from the invoiced entity still need judgement and sometimes a call.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a short payment is a dispute, an agreed discount or an error, and whom to ask.
tasks.altitude: Cash posting shrinks to a short daily review; the officer spends the time on calls, and short payments surface the same day as disputes.

tasks.short: Keep debtor records current: address and contact changes, mergers, closures and bankruptcies.
tasks.statement: Perform various administrative functions for assigned accounts, such as recording address changes and purging the records of deceased customers.
