tasks.design: A mailbox classifier and a KvK lookup feed a change queue; verified address and contact changes are written to AFAS after one-click approval, and IBAN or name changes need a second person. A nightly KvK and insolvency-register check on all active debtors raises bankruptcy alerts so credit is blocked early.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changes arrive by unstructured mail and each needs a register lookup; volume was too low to justify a build.
tasks.enabler_now: Cheap custom code with AI coding, KvK APIs and a bounded classifier for free-text mails.
tasks.still_hard: Fraudulent IBAN change requests need strict four-eyes control; group structures and mergers need judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a suspicious change request and judging what a merger or bankruptcy means for open items.

ambition.what: Daily insolvency and KvK-change monitoring of all active shippers, with automatic credit-hold proposals.

tasks.altitude: Record keeping becomes a short approval queue; the officer gains early warning on failing customers.

tasks.short: When shippers stay silent, put them on credit hold, inform sales, and hand files to agency or lawyer.
tasks.statement: Notify credit departments, order merchandise repossession or service disconnection, and turn over account records to attorneys when customers fail to respond to collection attempts.
tasks.design: An escalation workflow on the data platform flags accounts that finished the reminder sequence, proposes a credit hold that the officer approves and that notifies sales and planning in Teams. For accounts the officer sends on, it builds the hand-over file from AFAS and SharePoint with code-calculated interest and costs and a cited model chronology, checks the agency's Wki registration, and tracks case status.
tasks.previous_blocker: Files had to be assembled by hand from several systems, and interest and cost calculations were done in Excel each time.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-coded document assembly is cheap; models can draft a cited chronology; legal-step drafting tools exist in the Dutch market [S1].
tasks.still_hard: Errors in the first letter or calculations only surface in court [S5]; the decision to escalate weighs commercial relationships.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing escalation against the value of the customer relationship and agreeing it with sales and the Finance Director.

ambition.what: A weekly escalation review of every account past the reminder sequence, instead of escalating only when someone notices.

tasks.altitude: The officer chairs a short weekly escalation review with sales and approves files instead of building them.

tasks.short: Check and approve payment requests and invoices against policy, budget and mandates before payment runs.
tasks.statement: Receive, record, and authorize requests for disbursements in accordance with company policies and procedures.
tasks.design: Configure the AFAS Profit invoice workflow so every request runs a deterministic rule set (budget line, contract or PO, duplicate, IBAN change against supplier master, mandate register) before it reaches anyone. Requests below threshold that pass all checks go straight to the payment batch; non-PO and agency invoices get a bounded model step that matches them to policy and portal hours, and only flags and high-value items land in the controller's queue. Payment release in Rabobank keeps dual signing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Checks lived in the controller's head and an Excel mandate list; agency invoices and non-PO requests need reading, so everything went to one person.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS workflow and API make rule checks cheap to build with AI coding, and a small model step can read invoice documents reliably enough to sort clean from flagged.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping the mandate register and thresholds current, and judging requests that fit no rule, such as one-off settlements or urgent supplier prepayments.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether an unusual payment is right for the business and carrying the accountability for releasing company money.

ambition.what: Daily payment runs instead of weekly, with every request checked against the full rule set.

tasks.altitude: The controller stops ticking routine invoices and spends about an hour a week on flagged cases; they set the approval thresholds and own the mandate register.

tasks.short: Watch cash position, reserves, tax and covenant deadlines daily so the company stays liquid and compliant.
tasks.statement: Monitor financial activities and details, such as cash flow and reserve levels, to ensure that all legal and regulatory requirements are met.
tasks.design: Replace the daily Excel cash sheet with a scheduled job on the governed data platform that loads Rabobank CAMT.053 statements and AFAS open items, and feeds a Power BI cash and 13-week dashboard. Deterministic rules raise Teams alerts for reserve floors, covenant ratios and VAT and loonheffing payment dates; a bounded model step proposes matches for bank lines AFAS rules leave unmatched and drafts the weekly cash note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bank data came as manual downloads and the cash forecast lived in one person's spreadsheet; building connectors was not worth it for a 10-person team.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes a CAMT.053 loader and AFAS connector a matter of days, and Power BI is already in place on an AFAS extract.
tasks.still_hard: Forecasting seasonal flex labour costs and customer payment behaviour; a nightly extract still lags intraday movements.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a dip is a timing issue or a real problem, and deciding when to warn the finance director or the bank.

ambition.what: A daily checked cash position with alerts, instead of a weekly spreadsheet.

tasks.altitude: The controller reads a dashboard each morning instead of building it; they set reserve floors and alert thresholds and decide escalations.

tasks.short: Assess when the company needs funding or has surplus cash, and recommend credit or deposit actions.
tasks.statement: Evaluate needs for procurement of funds and investment of surpluses and make appropriate recommendations.
tasks.design: Build a deterministic scenario model in Power BI or Python on top of the 13-week cash view and AFAS data, with drivers for flex labour peaks, capex and payment terms. A bounded model step extracts terms from bank offers into a comparison table and drafts the recommendation memo, which the controller rewrites and owns.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inputs were scattered over FP&A sheets and AFAS, and scenario models were rebuilt by hand each time.
tasks.enabler_now: Once the cash data is on a platform, a scenario model is cheap to code; models extract terms from documents well enough for checked use.
tasks.still_hard: Judging seasonality and customer risk, and reading the bank relationship; the decision stays with the finance director.
tasks.human_edge: Weighing risk appetite, timing and the bank relationship, and arguing the case to the finance director.

ambition.what: A monthly funding and surplus check instead of ad hoc reviews when cash gets tight.

tasks.altitude: The controller spends time on choosing between scenarios instead of building them; they gain a standing monthly slot with the finance director on funding.

tasks.short: Run the yearly budget and steer planning and procurement across three sites and departments.
tasks.statement: Coordinate and direct the financial planning, budgeting, procurement, or investment activities of all or part of an organization.
tasks.design: Replace the e-mailed Excel templates with a small budget entry app on the data platform, with automated reminders by Teams and a consolidation that is always current. A Power BI view shows variance against prior year and drivers, a bounded model step drafts questions for flagged lines, and the approved budget loads into AFAS by API.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every site and department used its own copy of the Excel template, so consolidation was manual and the version count high.
tasks.enabler_now: A simple entry app and AFAS budget import are quick to build with AI coding, and Power BI already runs on AFAS data.
tasks.still_hard: Getting site managers to plan on drivers instead of last year plus a percentage, and the negotiation itself.
tasks.human_edge: Challenging and agreeing budgets with site and department heads, and balancing site wishes against company targets.

ambition.what: A quarterly budget reforecast with the sites, instead of one yearly budget round.

tasks.altitude: The controller stops chasing and merging files and spends the budget season in review conversations; they own the driver model and variance thresholds.

tasks.short: Advise the MT and Finance Director on financial goals, policies and actions using actuals, forecasts and scenarios.
tasks.statement: Advise management on short-term and long-term financial objectives, policies, and actions.
tasks.design: Replace the monthly Excel pack with a governed Power BI model on a nightly AFAS extract plus a scenario table maintained with FP&A. A small Python job drafts variance commentary and a memo skeleton with a model, inserting figures by code and logging prompt and output in SharePoint; the controller edits and presents.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data sat in AFAS, the agency portals and personal Excel files, and free-text commentary could not be generated reliably.
tasks.enabler_now: Cheap AI-assisted coding for the extract and scenario model, and models that draft decent commentary when figures are locked by code.
tasks.still_hard: Judging what matters for the business, timing of advice, and trust of the MT; Dutch site-level context the data does not hold.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing the MT, the sites and the customers, choosing which trade-off to put forward and carrying it in the room.

ambition.what: A monthly margin review per site and per top-20 customer instead of a quarterly one

tasks.altitude: The controller spends less time building the pack and more time with site managers on margin; they gain a standing slot to propose pricing and flex-staffing policy.

tasks.short: Manage pension, absence, WIA and liability insurance premiums, track rule changes and budget benefit costs.
tasks.statement: Handle all aspects of employee insurance, benefits, and casualty programs, including monitoring changes in health insurance regulations and creating budgets for benefits and worker's compensation.
tasks.design: A shared mailbox feeds a Python job on the governed data platform that extracts premium notes into a premium register, reconciles them nightly against AFAS payroll deductions and ledger accounts, and queues differences. A monthly model digest of UWV, Belastingdienst and pension fund changes goes to the controller and C&B, and the budget is calculated by code from the FP&A headcount plan.
tasks.previous_blocker: Premium notes arrive as PDFs in many layouts and the reconciliation lives in a personal spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Reliable PDF extraction with checks, and fast coding of the reconciliation on the AFAS extract.
tasks.still_hard: Absence and WIA data are special category data under AVG/GDPR; access must stay aggregated and works-council consent may be needed for new processing of employee data.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiating with the broker, choosing to bear WGA risk or insure it, and weighing employee impact with HR.

ambition.what: A yearly, numbers-based review of eigenrisicodragerschap for WGA and ZW instead of rolling over the policy

tasks.altitude: The controller stops checking premium lines and reviews only exceptions; they gain a clear basis to propose insurance choices to the Finance Director.

tasks.short: Check that AFAS payroll deductions are booked right, reconciled and paid to tax office and pension fund.
tasks.statement: Compute, withhold, and account for all payroll deductions.
tasks.design: AFAS keeps computing deductions; a scheduled SQL/Python job on the AFAS extract ties the payroll journal, loonaangifte, pension invoice and ledger to zero each run and shows breaks on a Power BI page. A bounded model step proposes causes for breaks from payroll mutations, and the Rabobank payment batch is released only when the tie-out is green and the controller approves.
tasks.previous_blocker: The checks were simple but nobody had time to code them, so they lived in Excel each month.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes the tie-out job quick to build and maintain.
tasks.still_hard: Retroactive CAO changes and flex workers paid via agencies make some differences slow to explain; payroll data is sensitive under AVG/GDPR.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a difference is acceptable, and owning the payment to the Belastingdienst.

ambition.what: A tie-out after every payroll run, including test runs, instead of once a month after the fact

tasks.altitude: The controller looks only at breaks and signs the payment; they gain a pre-payroll check point to stop a run with errors.

tasks.short: Prepare monthly and annual statements, management reports, forecasts, budgets and filings like VAT, CBS and KVK.
tasks.statement: Prepare or direct preparation of financial statements, business activity reports, financial position forecasts, annual budgets, or reports required by regulatory agencies.
tasks.design: Move the close workbook to scheduled SQL/Python on a governed data platform fed by the AFAS extract and Rabobank CAMT.053 files: it builds statements, runs the tie-outs and publishes a Power BI close page. A bounded model step drafts commentary only after the tie-out is green; VAT stays in AFAS and the KVK SBR filing runs through filing software or the auditor, since AFAS cannot file it for large companies.
tasks.previous_blocker: The close depended on manual Excel links between AFAS, the bank and the agency portals, and commentary needed a person.
tasks.enabler_now: Fast AI-assisted coding of tie-outs and statement builds, and models that draft commentary when numbers are fixed by code.
tasks.still_hard: Dutch GAAP judgement (BW 2 Titel 9), estimates and provisions, and auditor acceptance; benchmarks are US GAAP only.
tasks.human_edge: Accounting judgement on estimates, materiality and disclosure, and signing for the numbers with the auditor.

ambition.what: A weekly flash P&L per site for site managers, available on Monday

tasks.altitude: The controller designs the close rather than running it: they own tie-out rules, thresholds and the commentary review, and they gain time to review the forecast with FP&A each month.

tasks.short: Answer site managers and budget holders on accounting, budget and spending rules, and steer cost control.
tasks.statement: Provide direction and assistance to other organizational units regarding accounting and budgeting policies and procedures and efficient control and utilization of financial resources.
tasks.design: A Teams intake form replaces loose mails and tags each question with cost centre and topic. A small answer desk on the Microsoft 365 tenant retrieves the finance handbook from SharePoint and pulls budget-vs-actual from the nightly AFAS extract, drafts a cited answer, and the controller approves new kinds of answers; approved ones feed a FAQ.
tasks.previous_blocker: The handbook was scattered across SharePoint files and the controller held the context in their head; retrieval over free-text questions was not reliable enough.
tasks.enabler_now: Retrieval with citations over a small document set works well, and the AFAS extract already exists for Power BI.
tasks.still_hard: Handbook must be kept current and unambiguous; questions that are really negotiations about budget stay human.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a site manager needs a firm no versus room to act, and building the trust that makes budget holders follow the rules.

ambition.what: Team leads in Tilburg and Venlo warehouses with small spending authority get same-day answers on what they may spend.

tasks.altitude: Fewer interruptions; the controller spends time in budget conversations and owns the handbook and the answer approval rules.

tasks.short: Analyse past and forecast results per site and customer to find cost savings and improvement areas.
tasks.statement: Analyze the financial details of past, present, and expected operations to identify development opportunities and areas where improvement is needed.
tasks.design: Replace the monthly Excel build with a scheduled Python job on a governed data platform that joins the AFAS ledger with agency hours and invoices and feeds a Power BI margin and unit-cost dashboard per site and customer. A bounded model step drafts flux commentary for variances above materiality, with a code check that amounts tie, and the controller edits before anything reaches the finance director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agency portals and AFAS were only tied together by hand in Excel, so analysis came late and only per quarter.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes the data job and dashboard cheap to build; models can draft variance commentary that code can check.
tasks.still_hard: Allocating shared warehouse and transport costs to customers is a policy choice; agency portal data quality varies.
tasks.human_edge: Judging which savings are real and which hurt service or safety, and convincing site managers to act.

ambition.what: A monthly margin review per customer contract instead of a yearly one, to catch loss-making contracts before renewal.

tasks.altitude: The controller stops building spreadsheets and spends the time on two or three improvement cases a month; owns materiality thresholds and cost allocation keys.

tasks.short: Coordinate the year-end audit and internal checks so accounts meet Dutch law and tax rules.
tasks.statement: Conduct or coordinate audits of company accounts and financial transactions to ensure compliance with state and federal requirements and statutes.
tasks.design: A scheduled job builds the auditor's request list into an evidence pack from AFAS, SharePoint and Rabobank statements and runs fixed control tests all year (duplicate payments, IBAN changes, approvals over limit, segregation of duties) into a Power BI exception view. A bounded model step drafts responses to auditor queries with file references; the controller decides on adjustments and signs off responses.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence gathering and control tests were done once a year by hand because ad-hoc AFAS exports were tedious to repeat.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes repeatable export and test scripts cheap; AFAS bank matching already runs on fixed rules, so tests can focus on what remains.
tasks.still_hard: Dutch GAAP judgements and VAT and wage tax positions are untested for AI drafting; auditors must accept the evidence trail.
tasks.human_edge: Judging materiality and negotiating with the auditor on adjustments and management letter wording.

ambition.what: Monthly control testing instead of once-a-year findings at the audit.

tasks.altitude: Audit season shrinks to review and negotiation; the controller owns the control test set and materiality and gets findings monthly.

tasks.short: Write and maintain internal control policies for budgets, cash, credit and accounting.
tasks.statement: Develop internal control policies, guidelines, and procedures for activities, such as budget administration, cash and credit management, and accounting.
tasks.design: Keep the finance handbook as one versioned SharePoint library tied to the AFAS authorisation matrix and a mandate register. Audit and control-test exceptions feed a gap list; a bounded model step drafts redlines, code checks limits against the matrix, and approved changes are configured as AFAS approval workflows and pushed to budget holders as a short Studytube module.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policies lived as loose Word files, out of sync with AFAS workflow settings, so updates were rare and slow.
tasks.enabler_now: Drafting redlines is fast with a model, and a script can compare policy limits with AFAS settings.
tasks.still_hard: Agreement with site managers on limits, and keeping AFAS configuration in step with the text.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing where control helps and where it only slows operations, and getting the finance director and sites to agree.

ambition.what: A mandate register that shows every budget holder their own signing limits, checked against AFAS each night.

tasks.altitude: Policy updates move from yearly to as-needed; the controller owns the authorisation matrix and the mandate register.

tasks.short: Build the year-end tax pack from AFAS for the outside tax advisor, then review and approve returns.
tasks.statement: Prepare and file annual tax returns or prepare financial information so that outside accountants can complete tax returns.
tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform reads the AFAS trial balance, ledger detail and asset register, applies a versioned fiscal mapping table and builds the fiscal reconciliation and tax pack in a fixed SharePoint folder. A bounded model step proposes fiscal categories only for lines on mixed-cost accounts; the controller reviews those and lines above materiality, and filing stays with the advisor after sign-off.
tasks.previous_blocker: The pack is built once a year, so nobody invested in a pipeline; fiscal treatment of mixed-cost lines needs reading of free text.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes a small reconciliation job cheap to build, and a model can read ledger descriptions with a deterministic tie-out deciding what is used.
tasks.still_hard: Fiscal judgement on unusual items, Dutch tax rules the benchmarks do not cover, and any year with new entities or restructuring.
tasks.human_edge: The controller decides fiscal positions, answers for them to the Belastingdienst and auditor, and signs off before anything leaves the company.

ambition.what: A quarterly provisional Vpb position from the same pipeline, instead of a once-a-year surprise.

tasks.altitude: The controller spends a few days reviewing exceptions instead of two weeks assembling the pack. They gain the right to set the fiscal mapping table and the materiality threshold for review.

tasks.short: Model tax scenarios on planned investments and results, and agree tax choices with the advisor and finance director.
tasks.statement: Perform tax planning work.
tasks.design: A scenario model in Python on the governed data platform reads the FP&A forecast, capex plan and AFAS actuals, and computes tax outcomes per scenario from versioned rule parameters (rates, deduction brackets). A bounded model step digests rule changes and drafts the decision memo; the controller and advisor make the choices.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tax planning lived in one-off Excel files that copied the forecast, so each run was slow and quickly stale.
tasks.enabler_now: Cheap AI-assisted coding of a parameter-driven model linked to the forecast, and models that summarise long rule texts with citations.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing positions with legal and financial risk, interpreting new rules, and timing decisions with the business.
tasks.human_edge: Weighing tax savings against risk and business plans, and agreeing positions with the advisor and finance director.

ambition.what: Test the tax effect of each major capex request (trucks, forklifts, racking) before approval, not only at year end.

tasks.altitude: The controller runs scenarios in minutes and brings options to capex decisions. They gain a seat in capex approval for the tax angle.

tasks.short: Set depreciation on new assets and advise management on buying, leasing or disposing of trucks, forklifts and racking.
tasks.statement: Determine depreciation rates to apply to capitalized items and advise management on actions regarding the purchase, lease, or disposal of such items.
tasks.design: Configure AFAS fixed assets with a maintained asset policy table so useful lives and monthly depreciation run without Excel. A bounded model step proposes capitalise-or-expense and asset class for invoice lines, and a deterministic lease-versus-buy calculator on the data platform reads asset register, maintenance costs and offers to produce a standard analysis for management.
tasks.previous_blocker: Capex invoices arrive with varied descriptions, and the lease-buy analysis was rebuilt in Excel for each request.
tasks.enabler_now: Models can read invoice descriptions under a tie-out check, and a standard calculator is cheap to build with AI-assisted coding.
tasks.still_hard: Judging useful life for unusual assets, impairment, and the operational trade-offs of fleet choices.
tasks.human_edge: The controller weighs operational needs, financing and risk with site managers and the finance director, and owns the depreciation policy.

ambition.what: A standard lease-buy-dispose check for every truck, forklift and racking request from the three sites.

tasks.altitude: The controller reviews exceptions instead of coding every addition, and spends the time on fleet and equipment advice. They gain a formal advisory role in site capex requests.

tasks.short: Analyse actuals, forecasts and cash to judge Noordhaven's current and future financial position for management and board.
tasks.statement: Develop or analyze information to assess the current or future financial status of firms.
tasks.design: Replace the FP&A Excel workbook that ties AFAS, the agency portals and Rabobank with a nightly Python job on a governed data platform. It feeds a Power BI rolling forecast and variance dashboard. A bounded model step drafts variance explanations that code checks against the numbers, and a template builds the memo skeleton.
tasks.previous_blocker: The agency portals and bank files had no clean link to AFAS, so every refresh was manual Excel work. Building and keeping integrations was too slow for a 10-person team.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS Profit has GetConnectors and Rabobank delivers CAMT.053. AI coding makes small pipelines cheap to build. Model steps can read journal text and draft explanations whose numbers code can check.
tasks.still_hard: Volume and customer assumptions come from operations and sales, and those do not sit in any system. Scenario judgement stays with people. Agency portal exports may change format without warning.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which risks matter, such as losing a large shipper, fuel spikes or CAO wage steps, and standing behind the outlook in front of the board and the bank.

ambition.what: A weekly re-forecast of P&L and 13-week cash, not a monthly one, with the director signing off a short outlook each Monday.

tasks.altitude: The director spends Monday reviewing a pre-built forecast and its explanations instead of chasing the workbook. They decide which drivers and thresholds the model uses.

tasks.short: Assess credit limit requests for new and growing shippers, and prepare bank facility applications and covenant files.
tasks.statement: Examine, evaluate, or process loan applications.
tasks.design: A request form in Teams/SharePoint starts a workflow that pulls the KvK extract, credit report and AFAS payment history into one credit file. Deterministic rules from the written credit policy compute a proposed limit. For legal entities a bounded model step extracts ratios from the filed accounts. The director approves in one screen, and the approved limit is written to the AFAS debtor record with a log entry.
tasks.previous_blocker: Credit data sat in PDFs, agency portals and AFAS screens, and the credit policy was mostly in the director's head. Too few requests came in to justify a credit tool.
tasks.enabler_now: KvK and credit agencies offer APIs, AFAS UpdateConnectors can set debtor limits, and model steps can read filed accounts PDFs with checks that the totals balance.
tasks.still_hard: Writing the credit policy as explicit rules. Sole-trader hauliers are natural persons, so model scoring would be high-risk under the EU AI Act and stays out. Small shippers rarely file useful accounts.
tasks.human_edge: Weighing commercial value against risk for a shipper, and agreeing security or shorter terms in a conversation with sales and the customer.

ambition.what: Review every shipper's credit limit each quarter against payment behaviour, not only when a new request arrives.

tasks.altitude: The director approves a prepared file in minutes instead of building it. They own the written credit policy and its thresholds, including which requests below a set amount the Collections Officer may approve alone.

tasks.short: Review aging and collection reports to see overdue balances, DSO and which debtors need action.
tasks.statement: Review collection reports to determine the status of collections and the amounts of outstanding balances.
tasks.design: Replace the weekly Excel aging pack with a Power BI collections page on the nightly AFAS extract, showing DSO, overdue by debtor and site, and dispute status. A bounded model step labels debtor mails in the shared collections mailbox, and the officer confirms the label before it goes into AFAS. A notification flags debtors that cross a set threshold to the director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Dispute and promise information lived in Outlook, not in AFAS, so the report needed manual notes every week.
tasks.enabler_now: Power BI already runs on AFAS data. Model steps can label Dutch and English mails reliably enough for a person to confirm with one click.
tasks.still_hard: Disputes often start in operations (damaged goods, waiting time) and reach finance late. The 30-day cap on payment terms for small suppliers applies on the payables side and needs its own check.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing when to stop deliveries to a large shipper and having that conversation with sales and the customer.

ambition.what: A forward cash-in forecast per week for the next 30 to 60 days, built from promises and payment patterns, instead of explaining DSO after the fact.

tasks.altitude: The director reads a live dashboard and only acts on flagged debtors. They set the escalation thresholds and decide the credit stops.

tasks.short: Prepare the board pack, annual accounts, bank covenant and statutory reports, then sign off and file them.
tasks.statement: Prepare financial or regulatory reports required by laws, regulations, or boards of directors.
tasks.design: A scheduled job reads the closed AFAS period into a reporting dataset and fills fixed templates for the board pack, the bank covenant calculation and the accounts tables, with a reconciliation check against the trial balance. A bounded model step drafts commentary whose numbers code checks. Filing to KVK goes through a separate SBR tool because AFAS cannot file for large companies, and every external submission needs the director's sign-off.
tasks.previous_blocker: Report layouts changed every period and were rebuilt by hand in Excel and Word. Statutory formats such as SBR need tooling outside AFAS.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes template generators and reconciliation checks cheap to build and change. Model steps can draft commentary that code checks figure by figure.
tasks.still_hard: Disclosure judgement, auditor negotiation and new rules: CSRD applies only above 1,000 employees and €450 million turnover, and Dutch B2B e-invoicing reporting is coming from 2030–2031. Report volume tends to grow once reports are cheap to make.
tasks.human_edge: Signing the accounts and the covenant statement, judging disclosures with the auditor, and explaining the results to the board and the bank.
tasks.altitude: The director reviews a ready pack and writes only the key messages. They decide which reports exist and cap their number so the time saved is not spent on more reports.

tasks.short: Review finance processes and controls and recommend changes to procedures, systems or budgets.
tasks.statement: Evaluate financial reporting systems, accounting or collection procedures, or investment activities and make recommendations for changes to procedures, operating systems, budgets, or other financial control functions.
tasks.design: A finance process dashboard in Power BI on a nightly AFAS extract shows close days, touchless AP rate, DSO and audit adjustments per site. A bounded model step maps walk-through notes and the auditor letter to the control matrix, and drafts the memo with code-filled figures. The Finance Director decides and presents.
tasks.previous_blocker: Process metrics sat in separate AFAS screens and Excel files, so every review began with a week of gathering, and free-text findings could not be matched to controls by rule.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes the AFAS extract and metric jobs cheap to build, and a model can map free-text findings to a control list with sources the reviewer can check.
tasks.still_hard: Judging which change is worth the disruption, and getting the team and the auditor to agree, stays slow human work.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing the team, the auditor and the business well enough to pick the two changes that will stick, and being accountable for the controls.

ambition.what: A quarterly control review per value stream (procure to pay, order to cash, record to report) instead of one yearly review after the audit.

tasks.altitude: Less time gathering numbers, more time in walk-throughs and decisions; the Finance Director gains a standing view of control health instead of a yearly snapshot.

tasks.short: Build the monthly operational and risk report pack for management from AFAS, bank and agency data.
tasks.statement: Prepare operational or risk reports for management analysis.
tasks.design: Replace the Excel pack that ties AFAS, Rabobank CAMT.053 and agency portal data with a scheduled Python job on a governed data platform that loads, ties out and flags breaks. It fills a fixed PowerPoint and Power BI pack, and a bounded model step drafts commentary only for variances above a set threshold. The Finance Director reviews and signs.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agency portals and bank files had no clean link to AFAS, so the pack was rebuilt by hand in Excel each month, and commentary needed a person to write it.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes the connectors and tie-out checks cheap to build, and models can draft variance text that code checks against the numbers.
tasks.still_hard: Agency portal exports change format, and the time saved tends to return as more and longer reports unless the pack is capped.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which risks management must hear about, and standing behind the numbers when asked.

ambition.what: A weekly cost and cash flash per site (Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo) instead of a monthly pack only.

tasks.altitude: The Finance Director edits and signs a pack instead of building it, and gains time to discuss risks with site managers; the cap on pack length becomes their decision.

tasks.short: Analyse cost actuals per site and cost type to set next year's budget and reforecasts.
tasks.statement: Evaluate data pertaining to costs to plan budgets.
tasks.design: A scheduled job loads AFAS ledger and headcount data and agency invoices into the data platform, maps them to sites and drivers by rule, and feeds a driver-based scenario model in Power BI with CAO wage steps, flex share and diesel as inputs. No model is needed at run time; unmapped cost lines go to the FP&A Analyst as an exception list.
tasks.previous_blocker: Flex costs sat in agency invoices outside AFAS cost centres, so mapping to sites and drivers was manual Excel work each cycle.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes the mapping rules, connectors and scenario model fast to build and change.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing driver assumptions with site managers, and keeping the mapping right when cost centres or agencies change.
tasks.human_edge: Weighing site managers' plans against the company's targets and deciding where to cut or invest.

ambition.what: A quarterly driver-based reforecast of flex and wage costs per site, instead of one yearly budget round.

tasks.altitude: The Finance Director spends budget time on challenge sessions and choices, not on building the cost base; they set the scenario drivers.

tasks.short: Follow diesel prices, interest rates, currency and supplier tariffs, and judge their effect on margin and cash.
tasks.statement: Review reports of securities transactions or price lists to analyze market conditions.
tasks.design: A daily job fetches public diesel, Euribor and FX data and stores them on the data platform. A one-off bounded model step extracts surcharge and tariff terms from contracts into a reference table that a person confirms, after which code computes margin and interest exposure in a Power BI dashboard with alerts when an index crosses a contract threshold.
tasks.previous_blocker: Surcharge clauses and tariffs lived in PDF contracts, so linking market movements to Noordhaven's margin needed manual reading every time.
tasks.enabler_now: Models can extract clause terms with quotes for a person to confirm once, and AI coding makes the feeds and exposure calculation quick to build.
tasks.still_hard: Contracts with vague or negotiated surcharge terms, and deciding when to hedge or reprice, stay judgement calls.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding with commercial and the bank when to pass costs on, hedge rates or renegotiate, given customer relations.

ambition.what: A monthly fuel surcharge check per customer contract, so missed pass-through is caught within weeks instead of at year-end.

tasks.altitude: The Finance Director reads an exposure dashboard and alerts instead of collecting prices, and gains a fact base for pricing talks with commercial.

tasks.short: Advise managers on cost analysis, allocations and budget preparation using AFAS data pulled into Excel.
tasks.statement: Provide advice and technical assistance with cost analysis, fiscal allocation, and budget preparation.
tasks.design: A certified Power BI semantic model on the AFAS extract holds actuals, budget and the allocation keys as versioned tables. A small Python job on the governed data platform runs standard cost and allocation analyses on request and writes an Excel workpaper. A bounded model step drafts an options memo whose numbers are checked against the workpaper.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each question needed a new Excel build because allocation keys and drivers lived in personal workbooks, not in one model.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes a governed model and analysis scripts cheap to build. Copilot in Power BI and LLM drafting can write commentary on a prepared model [S3].
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing allocation keys across sites and keeping the model in sync with the AFAS chart of accounts. Judgement on what a manager should do stays human [S1].
tasks.human_edge: Knowing the site, the manager and the trade-off, and saying no when the numbers do not support a plan.

ambition.what: Team leaders in warehouses and transport get a self-service cost view for their own cost centre, with the analyst handling only the questions it cannot answer.

tasks.altitude: The analyst answers fewer how-much questions and more what-should-we-do questions. They gain the right to set and change the allocation keys in the model, with Controller sign-off.

tasks.short: Review site and cost-centre budgets for trends in volume, labour and flex costs that change budget needs.
tasks.statement: Review operating budgets to analyze trends affecting budget needs.
tasks.design: Trend tables become a Power BI page on the certified model with drivers (volume, shifts, flex hours, fuel) next to cost per site. Deterministic rules flag trends beyond set thresholds and send the cost-centre owner a Teams form for the cause. A bounded model step drafts the trend note from flags and answers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Driver data such as flex hours and volumes sat in agency portals and site sheets, not next to the ledger, so each review was rebuilt by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Cheap AI-assisted coding of extracts and rules, and LLM drafting of commentary on prepared data [S2][S3].
tasks.still_hard: Getting clean driver data from three agency portals and site systems. Faster trend output may invite more reports rather than better decisions [S1][S4].
tasks.human_edge: Telling a lasting trend from a one-off, and knowing which manager's explanation to trust.

ambition.what: Budget needs per site reviewed monthly instead of at the yearly budget round and mid-year review.

tasks.altitude: The analyst reads flags and causes instead of building tables. They decide which drivers and thresholds count and when a trend changes the forecast.

tasks.short: Check monthly budget against actuals per cost centre and chase overruns to keep spending in control.
tasks.statement: Analyze monthly department budgeting and accounting reports to maintain expenditure controls.
tasks.design: The Excel sheet that ties AFAS and the agency portals becomes a scheduled Python job on the governed data platform that loads the ledger and agency invoices and hours, ties them and feeds a variance page in Power BI. A bounded model step proposes a cause for each flagged line, and a workflow sends approved overrun notices to cost-centre owners and tracks answers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agency invoices and hours came from three portals in different formats, so tying them to the ledger was manual every month.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes portal parsers and tie-out rules quick to build; small model calls can read free-text invoice lines [S2].
tasks.still_hard: Portal formats change, and the ledger posting timing at month end makes variances noisy. 'A good guess isn't good enough' in finance, so causes need confirmation [S5].
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which overruns matter and pressing a manager to act without damaging the relationship.

ambition.what: Weekly flex-cost control per site during peak season instead of a monthly look after close.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends close week on causes and action, not tie-outs. They gain the right to set the overrun thresholds that trigger a notice.

tasks.short: Check managers' budget estimates for completeness, correct sums and conformance with budget rules and CAO rates.
tasks.statement: Examine budget estimates for completeness, accuracy, and conformance with procedures and regulations.
tasks.design: Managers enter budgets in a simple input app (Power Apps or a small web form on the governed platform) that enforces the account list and cost centres, so the mail round disappears. Deterministic checks test completeness, sums, CAO wage scales and headcount against AFAS, and a bounded model step checks free-text justifications against the budget policy on SharePoint.
tasks.previous_blocker: Budgets arrived as free-form Excel files with changed layouts, so checks could not be coded once.
tasks.enabler_now: A structured input app and rule checks are cheap to build with AI coding; models can read justifications against a policy text.
tasks.still_hard: Getting managers to use the app, and keeping CAO tables current after each wage round. Headcount lines with named people are personal data under the AVG.
tasks.human_edge: Sensing padding or rollover budgets and challenging a manager on it face to face [S4].

ambition.what: A budget input app with instant feedback to site managers on errors and policy gaps before they submit.

tasks.altitude: The analyst no longer chases files or checks sums. They decide the budget rules and checks and spend the budget round on challenge conversations.

tasks.short: Work out what a new initiative will cost, such as an extra shift, a new client or peak-season flex staffing.
tasks.statement: Compile and analyze accounting records and other data to determine the financial resources required to implement a program.
tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on a governed data store pulls AFAS GetConnector data (GL, cost centres, headcount) and the agency hours and invoices into one cost base. An Excel or Power BI template then applies defined drivers (CAO rates, shift allowances, agency rates) to the scope the analyst enters. A bounded model step drafts the summary text, and code checks every figure in it against the model.
tasks.previous_blocker: The data sat in three places (AFAS, three agency portals, personal Excel). Driver logic lived in each analyst's spreadsheet, so nothing could be reused or scheduled.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes small extract jobs and driver templates cheap to build and maintain. Models can draft explanatory text that code checks against the numbers.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing the drivers and keeping the CAO and agency rate tables current. Agency portals may only offer file exports, not APIs. The volume assumptions come from managers and stay uncertain.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a manager's volume and timing assumptions are realistic, and knowing which past initiative is a fair comparison.

ambition.what: Cost every client tender and shift change before it is agreed, not only the large ones

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends their time on scoping talks and checking assumptions instead of pulling data. They own the driver and rate tables that every cost model uses.

tasks.short: Review site and department funds requests against budget and recommend approval or rejection to the finance director.
tasks.statement: Summarize budgets and submit recommendations for the approval or disapproval of funds requests.
tasks.design: Replace the mailbox and Excel log with a Microsoft Form and SharePoint list, routed by Power Automate. A scheduled check against the AFAS extract shows remaining budget and commitments for the cost centre in Power BI. A bounded model step drafts the memo from the analyst's notes, and the finance director's decision is recorded in the list and sent back to the requester automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests came in by mail in any format, and budget headroom needed a manual AFAS and Excel lookup each time. Memo writing was not worth templating for the volume.
tasks.enabler_now: Microsoft 365 already has Forms, Lists and Power Automate. AI coding makes the headroom check quick to build. A model can draft a memo from structured fields and notes, with a code check on the figures.
tasks.still_hard: Judging whether the business case is sound and how the request fits company priorities. Open commitments may not all be in AFAS when the check runs.
tasks.human_edge: Weighing a site manager's case against the company's priorities and cash position. Telling a manager no and keeping the relationship.

ambition.what: Give a decision within one week on every funds request above a set threshold, with a monthly overview of approved spend per site

tasks.altitude: The analyst no longer chases forms or looks up budgets. Their week is spent on the business cases and on proposing approval thresholds to the finance director.

tasks.short: Produce the monthly budget-versus-actual pack per site and cost centre, plus ad hoc reports.
tasks.statement: Direct the preparation of regular and special budget reports.
tasks.design: Replace the monthly Excel pack with a scheduled job that loads the AFAS extract and budget into a governed store and fills a Power BI paginated report per site. Power Automate sends each cost-centre owner their lines above a threshold with a short form to explain them. A bounded model step drafts the commentary from those answers, and the analyst and controller review the pack before it goes out.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cost-centre mapping changed by hand in Excel each month, and explanations came back by mail in any form. The pack needed someone to stitch it together.
tasks.enabler_now: Power BI is already in use and AI coding makes the extract, mapping checks and report templates fast to build. Models can turn free-text explanations into consistent commentary, with numbers checked by code.
tasks.still_hard: Getting owners to explain on time, and keeping the mapping table right when cost centres change. Copilot in Power BI needs a prepared model and is not officially supported in Dutch. Faster packs may invite more report requests.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which variances matter for the business and telling a site manager or the board what it means.

ambition.what: A mid-month flash report per site for site managers, built from the same pipeline

tasks.altitude: The analyst stops building tables and chasing mails. They review commentary, decide the variance thresholds and spend time with site managers on the large variances.

tasks.short: Reconcile cost-centre budgets to site and company totals and track the contingency reserve.
tasks.statement: Match appropriations for specific programs with appropriations for broader programs, including items for emergency funds.
tasks.design: Hold the cost-centre hierarchy as a maintained dimension in AFAS or a small governed mapping table instead of an Excel tab. A scheduled Python job reconciles every sub-budget to its site and company total after each AFAS refresh, lists breaks, and keeps a contingency register in a SharePoint list or small app. Approved transfers are posted to AFAS through its update connector after the controller signs off.
tasks.previous_blocker: The hierarchy and the contingency reserve lived in Excel tabs that only the analysts understood. Transfers were typed into AFAS by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes reconciliation scripts and a small register app cheap. AFAS connectors allow reading and posting budget lines without screen work.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping the hierarchy right when cost centres are added or merged. Deciding who may draw on the contingency reserve. AFAS write access needs tight control and an audit trail.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether an overrun should come from contingency or be absorbed by the site, and explaining that choice to the controller.

ambition.what: Show contingency use and remaining reserve per site every week instead of at quarter end

tasks.altitude: The analyst stops rebuilding the reconciliation each month. They own the hierarchy, review breaks and propose reallocations for the controller to approve.

tasks.short: Turn board and Finance Director budget guidelines into budget rules, templates and instructions for site and cost-centre managers.
tasks.statement: Interpret budget directives and establish policies for carrying out directives.
tasks.design: Keep budget parameters (wage increase from the CAO, flex caps, cost ceilings per site) in one versioned parameter table on a governed data platform instead of scattered Excel tabs. Code recalculates the impact on every cost centre and regenerates the manager templates; a small model loop reads new directives and drafts the change list and instruction text, which the analyst approves before a Power Automate flow publishes to SharePoint and notifies managers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Budget rules lived in people's heads and in last year's Excel files, so each directive meant manual re-reading and re-keying; free-text directives could not be parsed by rules.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes a parameter-driven budget model cheap to build, and models can now reliably extract and cite clauses from a directive when every claim is checked against the source.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding how a vague directive should apply to a specific site or the flex pool is judgement and negotiation; parameters must first be defined and agreed, which is organisational work, not software.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what the board actually means, where site managers will pad or push back, and what the Finance Director will accept.

ambition.what: Re-issue budget rules each quarter when CAO, fuel or volume assumptions move, instead of once a year.

tasks.altitude: The analyst stops re-keying templates and spends the time defining parameters and settling disputes with site managers; they gain ownership of the budget parameter table, with sign-off staying with the Finance Director.

tasks.short: Build cost-benefit cases for investments, financing and operating choices, such as forklift lease versus buy or flex versus own staff.
tasks.statement: Perform cost-benefit analyses to compare operating programs, review financial requests, or explore alternative financing methods.
tasks.design: A standard cost-benefit template in Python on the governed data platform, with fixed rules for discount rate, depreciation, tax and CAO labour cost, fed by scheduled pulls of the AFAS ledger and agency hours and invoices. A bounded model loop extracts supplier and lease quotes and drafts the options memo; Power BI shows scenarios to the requester, and the Finance Director decides.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each case was a new Excel build because data came from three systems and PDF quotes, and there was no agreed template for discount rate or labour cost.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes a reusable, tested template and data pulls cheap; models extract varied quotes well when totals are checked.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing assumptions such as volume growth or a client contract renewal, and dealing with requesters who want a given answer.
tasks.human_edge: Challenging optimistic assumptions from site managers and judging strategic value the numbers miss, such as client retention or safety.

ambition.what: Run a cost-benefit check on every flex-versus-own-staff choice per site each season, not only on large investments.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time building spreadsheets and more time questioning assumptions; they gain the right to set the standard assumptions in the template, while the Finance Director keeps the decision.

tasks.short: Look for ways to cut cost or raise margin, such as agency overbilling, overtime, idle hours or unprofitable customers.
tasks.statement: Seek new ways to improve efficiency and increase profits.
tasks.design: Replace the ad-hoc Excel digging with scheduled rule checks on the governed data platform: agency invoices versus approved hours and agreed rates, overtime and idle hours per site, cost per pallet and margin per customer. Results appear as a ranked opportunity list in Power BI with a weekly Teams notice; agreed savings are tracked against AFAS actuals on the same dashboard.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agency, hours and ledger data sat in separate systems joined by hand, so scanning happened only when someone had time or a hunch.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes the joins and rule checks quick to build and maintain; the nightly AFAS extract already feeds Power BI.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing whether an outlier is waste or a reason, such as a peak client order; getting site managers to act; defining cost per pallet consistently across sites.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing from the floor why a cost is high and persuading a site manager to change practice.

ambition.what: A monthly margin-per-customer review for the commercial team, which today gets no such view.

tasks.altitude: The analyst stops hunting in spreadsheets and spends the time with site managers on the top five items; they gain the right to put opportunities on the monthly management agenda.

tasks.short: Send benefit and pension changes to carriers, check their invoices, answer questions, renew contracts with brokers.
tasks.statement: Administer employee insurance, pension, and savings plans, working with insurance brokers and plan carriers.
tasks.design: A scheduled job on the governed data platform reads AFAS mutations, builds carrier mutation files in each carrier's format, and queues them for one-click approval. A second job matches carrier invoices to AFAS headcount and payroll deductions and shows breaks on a Power BI page. A small answer desk on SharePoint documents drafts cited replies to pension questions for the specialist to send.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each carrier wants its own format and portal. The volume was too small to justify custom integration, so the Excel sheet stayed.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes small format mappers and reconciliation scripts cheap to build. Retrieval over fund documents can draft answers with citations.
tasks.still_hard: Carrier portals without an API, the pension transition at Pensioenfonds Vervoer, and exceptions such as long-term sick employees, which need judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiating with brokers and explaining pension choices to a worried employee needs trust and accountability.

ambition.what: A cited pension question service for warehouse and transport staff before and after the Pensioenfonds Vervoer transition to the new scheme on 1 January 2027.

tasks.altitude: Less list-keying, more time on carrier contracts and the pension transition. The specialist signs off submissions and exception lists instead of producing them.

tasks.short: Evaluate a new or changed job, decide its grade, CAO status and salary band.
tasks.statement: Evaluate job positions, determining classification, exempt or non-exempt status, and salary.
tasks.design: A Microsoft Forms or Power Apps intake feeds a bounded model step that drafts the job description and per-factor scores with reasons against Noordhaven's evaluation system and reference jobs. The specialist decides the grade in AFAS Profit job schemes, and every proposal, score and decision is logged for the pay transparency report and AI Act oversight. CAO-covered jobs stay inside the CAO grading system and are only checked, never rescored.
tasks.previous_blocker: Grading needs reading and judgement on free-text job content, and a wrong grade becomes a pay difference nobody can explain.
tasks.enabler_now: Models can draft per-factor scores with reasons that a specialist can check; a pilot reports over 70% agreement with experts. AFAS Profit 8 stores job schemes ready for pay transparency.
tasks.still_hard: About 30% of model scores will be off, so every grade needs a real review. The CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer regrading is still open, and grade recommendations may count as high-risk AI from December 2027.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist weighs the job's real content against the structure, holds the line with managers, and answers for the grade to the employee and the works council.

ambition.what: Re-check every non-CAO office job against the four-factor system once before the first pay transparency report, instead of only when a manager asks.

tasks.altitude: The specialist moves from writing and scoring to deciding and defending grades. They own the job architecture and its evidence file.

tasks.short: Research benefit and health and safety practices and propose policy changes to HR leadership.
tasks.statement: Research employee benefit and health and safety practices, and recommend changes or modifications to existing policies.
tasks.design: A monthly bounded model job reads a fixed source list and writes a cited digest to SharePoint. A Power BI page on the nightly AFAS extract shows benefits uptake, cost and absence by site and group. A reusable Python or Excel costing model replaces one-off spreadsheets, and a model drafts the memo from it.
tasks.previous_blocker: The research was ad hoc and the data sat in several AFAS reports, so each proposal started from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Cheap source monitoring with models, plus quick dashboard and costing builds through AI coding on the existing Power BI extract.
tasks.still_hard: Judging what fits a shift-based workforce and the CAO, and agreeing changes with the works council.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing what Noordhaven should offer and convincing leadership and the works council takes judgement and standing.

ambition.what: A yearly benefits review per site, with uptake and cost shown to the HR Director before the budget round.

tasks.altitude: Research time drops; more time goes to options and talks with the works council. Nothing changes in decision rights.

tasks.short: Answer manager and employee questions on CAO, pay, benefits, procedures and grading.
tasks.statement: Advise managers and employees on state and federal employment regulations, collective agreements, benefit and compensation policies, personnel procedures, and classification programs.
tasks.design: A shared Outlook or Teams intake creates a case in a simple list, and an answer desk indexes the CAO texts, policies and templates on SharePoint to draft cited answers. The specialist approves each draft, and repeat questions feed a FAQ page that managers can read themselves. Personal data from AFAS is only looked up for the case at hand, and access is logged under GDPR.
tasks.previous_blocker: The answers depend on two CAOs and many policies; search over SharePoint was poor, and nobody trusted an unsourced answer.
tasks.enabler_now: Retrieval with cited drafts makes answers checkable in seconds. The case list can be configured in Microsoft 365 that Noordhaven already has.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping CAO and policy versions current, cases with an individual twist, and the cost of a wrong answer on pay or dismissal rules.
tasks.human_edge: Hard or sensitive conversations, and judging when a question is really a complaint or a grading dispute.

ambition.what: Shift leaders in Tilburg and Venlo warehouses get same-day cited answers on CAO allowances and shift pay, which they now rarely ask.

tasks.altitude: Look-up time falls and the specialist spends their time on the hard cases and on fixing unclear policy text. Nothing changes in decision rights.

tasks.short: Run the yearly merit and incentive round for office staff and check proposals against budget and CAO.
tasks.statement: Develop and administer compensation programs, such as merit or incentive pay.
tasks.design: Replace the merit Excel workbook and mail round with a small app on the governed data platform: a nightly AFAS extract feeds a manager entry form with budget, scale ceiling and gap checks built in. The specialist sees one exception dashboard, approves, and the app writes pay mutations to AFAS through its API and generates letters from SharePoint templates.
tasks.previous_blocker: The round runs once a year with rules that change each time, so building an app was never worth it compared to a fresh Excel file.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes a small rule-driven app cheap enough to build and rebuild yearly, and AFAS exposes the data through its connectors.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding the matrix and handling managers who push past budget stays judgement; CAO staff on fixed scales need different rules than office staff.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the merit policy and saying no to a manager with a reason they accept.

ambition.what: Run a mid-year pay check per department instead of one yearly round, flagging people below band or with unexplained gaps.

tasks.altitude: The specialist stops chasing spreadsheets for weeks and spends the round on exceptions and on the merit policy itself, which they propose to the HR Director.

tasks.short: Advise HRBPs and managers on employee complaints about job grade or salary.
tasks.statement: Provide advice on the resolution of classification and salary complaints.
tasks.design: Log complaints in a simple case register (SharePoint list or AFAS workflow) and auto-build a case file from AFAS and the job library, with a bounded model step that reads the complaint and one that drafts the advice memo. The judgement and the talk with the employee stay with the specialist; the same register later handles pay transparency information requests with their two-month deadline.
tasks.previous_blocker: Complaints are few, varied and written in free text, and the facts sit in AFAS, SharePoint and old Excel files, so nothing tied them together.
tasks.enabler_now: Models can reliably read a complaint letter into fields and draft a memo from given facts; the data join is cheap code.
tasks.still_hard: The grading view itself, peers who are not truly comparable, and complaints that are really about the manager. GDPR Art. 22 rules out a model deciding.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether two jobs are really equal and telling an employee no in a way that holds up.

ambition.what: A pay information request desk that answers employees' pay transparency requests within the legal two months.

tasks.altitude: Case prep shrinks to a check, so the specialist spends time on the view and the conversation and sees complaint patterns across jobs that point to grading fixes.

tasks.short: Write job descriptions, grade jobs and maintain salary scales.
tasks.statement: Prepare occupational classifications, job descriptions, and salary scales.
tasks.design: Build a job library on the governed platform with SharePoint templates: a bounded model step drafts the description and a per-factor score with reasons, the specialist decides, and an AFAS workflow records the approved job scheme and band. Salary scales become a versioned table fed from CAO tables, replacing the Excel copies.
tasks.previous_blocker: Job descriptions were free text and grading relied on the specialist's reading; no tool could draft or score them.
tasks.enabler_now: Models now draft descriptions and score factors well enough to start from, and AFAS Profit 8 has fields for job schemes ready for pay transparency.
tasks.still_hard: Scores are about 70% right, so every grade needs a real check; CAO jobs stay in the CAO system now being redone by the sector. A grade recommendation tool may be high-risk under the AI Act from December 2027.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what a job really involves on the floor and defending the grade to the manager and works council.

ambition.what: A complete job architecture with a four-factor evaluation for every office job, ready for the 2027 pay transparency report.

tasks.altitude: The specialist moves from grading jobs one by one to owning the job architecture, deciding which roles need regrading and which drift does not count.

tasks.short: Cost CAO proposals and pay scenarios from payroll data for negotiators and Finance.
tasks.statement: Perform multifactor data and cost analyses that may be used in areas such as support of collective bargaining agreements.
tasks.design: Replace the costing workbooks with a scheduled extract of AFAS payroll and agency portal hours on the governed data platform, reconciled to the ledger, plus a scenario calculator where the specialist sets wage, allowance and pension parameters. A Power BI page shows results and a bounded model step drafts the memo around code-generated tables.
tasks.previous_blocker: Costing happens a few times a year with new proposals each round, and agency data came in different files, so Excel stayed the cheapest tool.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes a reusable extract and scenario calculator quick to build; the AFAS nightly extract for Power BI already exists.
tasks.still_hard: Agency data quality, pension changes with Pensioenfonds Vervoer's new scheme, and knowing what the other side will accept.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which scenario matters at the table and explaining cost trade-offs to negotiators.

ambition.what: Cost every counter-proposal during CAO talks the same day instead of after a week.

tasks.altitude: The specialist becomes the live costing partner in negotiations, with the right to set scenario assumptions with the controller.

tasks.short: Design and revise pay, promotion and appraisal methods, test their effects, and explain them to managers and staff.
tasks.statement: Plan, develop, evaluate, improve, and communicate methods and techniques for selecting, promoting, compensating, evaluating, and training workers.
tasks.design: A nightly job on a governed data platform joins the AFAS extract already used for Power BI with Recruitee offers and Studytube completions, and feeds a Power BI page showing raises, promotions and offer acceptance per grade, site and gender. A bounded drafting step turns the specialist's chosen options and the CAO text into policy and guide drafts in Word on SharePoint; consultation and consent stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data sat in three systems with no shared key, so each analysis was a one-off Excel job, and drafting policy text had no tool support.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes the joined extract and dashboard a days-long build, and language models draft usable policy and guide text from sources the specialist supplies.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the method is a judgement on fairness, cost and CAO limits; works council consent under WOR 27(1)(c) and sector regrading by CAO parties set the pace.
tasks.human_edge: Weighing fairness, cost and workforce reaction, and winning consent from the works council and managers.

ambition.what: Review offer acceptance and promotion outcomes per grade every quarter instead of once a year at the merit round.

tasks.altitude: Fewer hours in Excel, more in design and consultation. The specialist proposes method changes backed by quarterly evidence rather than yearly anecdotes.

tasks.short: Run the yearly appraisal and merit cycle and check ratings and raises for unequal treatment.
tasks.statement: Develop, implement, administer, and evaluate personnel and labor relations programs, including performance appraisal, affirmative action, and employment equity programs.
tasks.design: Move the appraisal and merit round from mailed Excel files into AFAS Profit workflows and forms, with reminders handled by the workflow. A deterministic job on the AFAS extract computes rating and raise distributions per group and flags outliers in Power BI before calibration, and fills a fixed report template for the HR director and works council. No model is needed at run time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Managers on three sites and shifts worked in mailed spreadsheets, so data arrived late and in different shapes, and equity checks were done by hand at the end.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS workflows can carry the forms, and AI-assisted coding makes the distribution checks and report template quick to build and test.
tasks.still_hard: Getting shift managers to use the forms on time; calibration is a negotiation; rating data is sensitive and a pay decision may not be made solely by a model (GDPR Art. 22).
tasks.human_edge: Challenging managers in calibration and deciding which outliers are justified.

ambition.what: Run the equity check on every merit proposal as it arrives, so outliers are discussed before calibration rather than after.

tasks.altitude: The chasing and merging disappear. The specialist spends the cycle on calibration and on deciding which differences need correction.

tasks.short: Keep job, pay and benefit records in AFAS right, and update the staff handbook and regulations.
tasks.statement: Assist in preparing and maintaining personnel records and handbooks.
tasks.design: Change requests come in through AFAS Profit workflow forms with field validation, so the specialist approves rather than types. A nightly deterministic check on the AFAS extract compares grades and scales with the CAO scale table and the job schemes AFAS Profit 8 stores, and sends an exception list to HR admin. A bounded drafting step turns CAO or policy changes into a handbook redline on SharePoint, with versioned publishing and a change notice.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changes arrived by mail in free form and the CAO-to-handbook mapping lived in the specialist's head, so checks happened only when payroll errors surfaced.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS Profit 8 has fields for job schemes and categories, AI-assisted coding makes the scale check cheap, and models can map a new CAO text onto handbook sections.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping the CAO scale table current while CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer parties regrade the sector; interpreting ambiguous CAO clauses.
tasks.human_edge: Interpreting CAO clauses and deciding how a change applies to edge cases such as part-time shift workers.

ambition.what: A monthly record-quality report to payroll before close, showing every grade and scale mismatch, as a base for the pay transparency report.

tasks.altitude: Record entry becomes approval. The specialist owns record quality as a measured figure rather than fixing errors after payroll finds them.

tasks.short: Build org charts, career path tables and pay analysis reports on jobs, grades and pay.
tasks.statement: Prepare reports, such as organization and flow charts and career path reports, to summarize job analysis and evaluation and compensation analysis information.
tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform reads the nightly AFAS extract, computes band position, compa-ratios and gaps per job group, site and gender, and renders org charts and career path tables; Power BI shows the results with row-level security. A bounded drafting step writes commentary checked number by number, and the report is a live Power BI page instead of a mailed file. The same pipeline produces the yearly pay transparency figures, with agency pay data added from the agency portals.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each report was rebuilt by hand from fresh Excel extracts, and there was no external deadline that justified a build.
tasks.enabler_now: The pay transparency law sets a fixed yearly report and the AFAS extract already exists; AI-assisted coding makes the pipeline and charts a short build.
tasks.still_hard: Grouping jobs of equal value is a judgement needing works council consent; agency pay data from three agencies arrives in different formats.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which gap explanations hold up and which need correction.

ambition.what: Give each site manager a monthly view of band position for their team, including flex workers, which they have never had.

tasks.altitude: No more report building. The specialist reviews gaps monthly and decides on explanations and remediation instead of producing yearly snapshots.

tasks.short: Research what jobs require, how jobs relate to each other, and sector trends affecting Noordhaven's roles.
tasks.statement: Research job and worker requirements, structural and functional relationships among jobs and occupations, and occupational trends.
tasks.design: A scheduled job on the governed data platform reads AFAS job schemes and the SharePoint description library into a job register, and a small CRUD app on top holds job families and levels. A bounded model loop summarises saved CAO and survey documents with quotes and drafts the memo, while the specialist does the interviews and decides.
tasks.previous_blocker: Job data was split between AFAS fields and Word files on SharePoint with no shared key, and sector news only came as free text.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes a small register and an extract cheap to build, and models can now summarise CAO bulletins with quotes. AFAS Profit 8 has fields for job schemes and categories [S2].
tasks.still_hard: Working out what a reach-truck driver or planner really does still takes site visits across shifts. The sector regrading under the CAO has no outcome yet, so trends can be read in more than one way.
tasks.human_edge: Watching the work and earning managers' trust in interviews, and judging whether a role has really changed or just drifted.

ambition.what: A job-change check every quarter for the 30 largest job codes instead of ad hoc reviews every few years, regrading only when core duties have materially changed

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends this time on site and with managers rather than in spreadsheets. They gain the right to flag a job for re-evaluation from register evidence.

tasks.short: Decide which job analysis tools are needed and build questionnaires, interview guides and description templates.
tasks.statement: Assess need for and develop job analysis instruments and materials.
tasks.design: A Power BI page on the AFAS extract and SharePoint metadata shows which jobs lack a current description or four-factor evaluation. A bounded model loop drafts questionnaires and templates tagged by factor, and Microsoft Forms collects the answers into a SharePoint list. The specialist and the works council settle the criteria.
tasks.previous_blocker: There was no legal push for a structured four-factor scheme, and writing tailored instruments for each job group took too long to repeat.
tasks.enabler_now: The pay transparency bill sets the four factors and works council consent [S1]. Models can draft factor-tagged questions quickly, and a UK pilot graded descriptions per factor with over 70% accuracy against experts [S8].
tasks.still_hard: Getting the works council to agree on criteria and grouping, and keeping CAO-graded jobs inside the CAO system while sector regrading is still going on.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing what to measure and why, and building agreement with the works council and managers on fair criteria.

ambition.what: A standard four-factor job analysis kit that HRBPs can use themselves for new or changed roles

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time writing forms and more time designing the evaluation scheme. They get the right to propose the scheme to the works council.

tasks.short: Analyse pay, job and sector data and supply figures to management, sector bodies and government.
tasks.statement: Analyze organizational, occupational, and industrial data to facilitate organizational functions and provide technical information to business, industry, and government.
tasks.design: Replace the Excel workbooks that join AFAS payroll and agency pay files with a scheduled Python/SQL job on the governed data platform. It builds a pay data mart and Power BI pages for gap per category, CAO costing and headcount. A bounded loop drafts replies to data requests around query-filled tables, and the specialist explains gaps and approves anything that leaves the company.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agency pay data came as separate files from three portals, and there was no legal need for gap figures by job category, so manual Excel pulls were good enough.
tasks.enabler_now: The pay transparency law requires yearly gap reports that include agency workers, with agencies supplying their pay data [S1]. AI coding makes the extract and joins cheap to build and test.
tasks.still_hard: Getting clean, timely pay data from three agencies, and explaining gaps fairly when job categories are still being redrawn. The data is confidential and some of it is special-category under the GDPR.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a gap is explained by legitimate factors, and telling the HR Director and works council an uncomfortable finding.

ambition.what: A monthly unexplained-gap check per job category instead of a once-a-year look, so gaps are fixed before the six-month joint evaluation trigger

tasks.altitude: The specialist moves from building workbooks to explaining and fixing pay differences. They gain the right to propose corrections in the yearly pay round.

tasks.short: Plan, build and run training on pay policy, CAO scales, benefits and pay transparency for managers and HR.
tasks.statement: Plan and develop curricula and materials for training programs and conduct training.
tasks.design: A bounded model loop turns SharePoint pay policies, CAO articles and the pay transparency rules into draft slides, quizzes and one-page guides, with a citation for each rule. Studytube is set up to enrol managers, recruiters and HRBPs automatically from AFAS and to report completions. The specialist runs the live sessions at the three sites.
tasks.previous_blocker: Material was rebuilt by hand each year, and there was little need to train managers on pay rules outside the yearly pay round.
tasks.enabler_now: New duties need trained managers and recruiters: band before negotiation, no salary-history question, and pay requests answered within two months [S1]. Models draft teaching material from policy text quickly.
