tasks.still_hard: Reaching shift managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, and keeping the material right while the law's start date and the CAO regrading are still open.
tasks.human_edge: Answering managers' real cases in the room and changing how they talk about pay with their teams.

ambition.what: Short pay transparency training for every shift lead and recruiter, including the rule that offers start from the band

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time making slides and more time with managers in sessions. Nothing changes in decision rights.

tasks.short: Turn pay, benefits and grading research into reports, manuals and explainers for staff, management and the works council.
tasks.statement: Prepare research results for publication in form of journals, books, manuals, and film.
tasks.design: A small Python job on the governed data platform reads the nightly AFAS extract and produces the figure tables and charts, with groups under a set size suppressed. It fills a Word template on SharePoint, and a bounded model step drafts the narrative per section; a script checks every number against the table. The specialist edits, the HR Director approves, and publishing is a SharePoint page or PDF from the same template.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work happens once a year or less, so nobody built a pipeline. Figures were rebuilt by hand in Excel each time.
tasks.enabler_now: The pay transparency law adds a yearly report (first over 2027 pay, due 7 June 2028), which turns a one-off into a recurring job. AI coding makes a small report pipeline cheap, and model drafting is good enough for a first version that a person edits.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining pay differences honestly and choosing what to publish. Small groups at three sites make anonymisation tricky, and the CAO regrading outcome is still open.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding what the numbers mean, what Noordhaven is willing to say in public, and how the works council will read it.

ambition.what: A one-page pay scale and benefits explainer per job group for warehouse and transport shift workers, in Dutch and Polish, refreshed from the same pipeline each year.

tasks.altitude: About 10 of the 16 hours a year go; the specialist spends the rest on interpreting the figures and on the works council discussion. Nothing changes in decision rights.

tasks.short: Receive, check and file personnel documents (contracts, evaluations, leave, certificates, grievances) in the AFAS dossier.
tasks.statement: Process, verify, and maintain personnel related documentation, including staffing, recruitment, training, grievances, performance evaluations, classifications, and employee leaves of absence.
tasks.design: One intake mailbox and the AFAS Pocket upload feed a document queue. AFAS Jonas, or a small extraction step on the governed data platform, reads each non-medical document into dossier fields; code checks them against AFAS and a checklist per document type, and the administrator approves or fixes from an exceptions queue. Scheduled reminders chase missing items; grievance and medical files bypass the model entirely.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documents arrive in free form from many senders, and reading them needed a person. Rule-based OCR could not cope with mixed layouts and handwriting.
tasks.enabler_now: Document-to-field extraction is now in AFAS Profit 8 (Jonas) and in general models, and validation code is quick to write with AI coding tools.
tasks.still_hard: Grievances and medical leave need human handling and strict access. Extraction error rates on Dutch scans are unknown, and a wrong dossier field can carry into payroll or a legal dispute.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a grievance or evaluation is complete and fair, and handling sensitive files discreetly with the employee and HRBP.

ambition.what: A weekly dossier-completeness report per site and manager, with missing signed contracts and expired certificates listed by name.

tasks.altitude: The administrator spends time on the exceptions queue and sensitive files instead of filing. They own the document checklist per type and decide when a dossier counts as complete.

tasks.short: Type employee changes (address, earnings, absence, production, performance notes, exit dates and reasons) into AFAS.
tasks.statement: Record data for each employee, including such information as addresses, weekly earnings, absences, amount of sales or production, supervisory reports on performance, and dates of and reasons for terminations.
tasks.design: Employees change their own address and bank details in AFAS InSite/Pocket, managers report absence and exits in AFAS workflows with mandatory reason codes, so typing disappears. A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform loads site production figures into AFAS and runs validation rules before each payroll cut-off; breaks appear on a Power BI exception page and in a daily mail to the administrator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Self-service was not switched on or trusted, and site sheets differ per location, so retyping was the safe default.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS self-service and workflows are standard configuration; AI coding makes the import job and validation rules a matter of days, not a project.
tasks.still_hard: Getting 750 shift workers to use self-service; harmonising three sites' production sheets; agreeing which production data may be stored per employee at all.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding what a wrong or odd record means and talking to the manager or employee to fix it.

ambition.what: Run the data-quality check every day instead of once before month close, so payroll starts from a clean file.

tasks.altitude: The administrator no longer types changes; they handle the daily exception list and decide on corrections before payroll. They set the validation rules with the Payroll Specialist.

tasks.short: Process hires, exits, leave, transfers and promotions in AFAS, with contract letters and notifications.
tasks.statement: Prepare or maintain employment records related to events, such as hiring, termination, leaves, transfers, or promotions, using human resources management system software.
tasks.design: A Recruitee-to-AFAS connector and an AFAS manager form start every personnel action as one AFAS workflow. Deterministic checks (CAO scale, ketenregeling, notice period, approvals present) run in code, the change is prepared in AFAS for one-click approval, the contract is merged from the SharePoint template, and notifications and Studytube enrolments go out automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recruitee, AFAS, SharePoint templates and Studytube were never connected, and CAO rules lived in people's heads and PDFs.
tasks.enabler_now: Both Recruitee and AFAS have APIs and AI coding makes connectors and rule code cheap; the CAO rules can be written down once and tested.
tasks.still_hard: Writing the CAO and warehouse-CAO rules completely, including exceptions; keeping templates current with CAO changes; non-standard deals agreed by managers.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting deals that do not fit the rules and agreeing them with the HRBP; approving changes that affect pay and contract status.

ambition.what: A same-day contract: an accepted offer in Recruitee becomes a signed-ready contract and AFAS record within one working day.

tasks.altitude: The administrator approves prepared changes and handles rule breaks instead of typing. They own the CAO rule table with the Compensation and Benefits Specialist.

tasks.short: Review incoming job applications for hard requirements and eligibility before the recruiter decides.
tasks.statement: Process and review employment applications to evaluate qualifications or eligibility of applicants.
tasks.design: Recruitee is configured with knockout questions per vacancy type, a structured scorecard and stage-triggered mail templates; managers see status in a Recruitee pipeline view. A small bounded step reads uploaded licences and certificates into type and expiry fields shown next to the scan. The fit judgement and every reject decision stay with a person, keeping Noordhaven outside automated candidate selection.
tasks.previous_blocker: Proof documents are photos and scans, and screening rules per vacancy were never written down, so everything was read by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Recruitee knockout questions and templates are standard; document extraction for licences is reliable enough to pre-fill fields for review.
tasks.still_hard: Fit judgement for warehouse and driver roles stays human. From 2 December 2027 any tool that screens or ranks applicants is high-risk under the AI Act, so scope must stay at fact extraction.
tasks.human_edge: Judging motivation, gaps and fit for shift work, and treating every applicant fairly.

ambition.what: Give every applicant an eligibility answer within one working day in peak season, when flex and seasonal hiring spikes.

tasks.altitude: The administrator spends time on fit judgement and candidate contact, not opening files and checking dates. Nothing changes in decision rights: the recruiter still decides.

tasks.short: Answer employee questions on leave, salary scales, benefits, eligibility and CAO rules by mail, Teams and phone.
tasks.statement: Answer questions regarding examinations, eligibility, salaries, benefits, and other pertinent information.
tasks.design: Put a Teams bot in front of the HR mailbox. It quotes personal entitlements through a deterministic AFAS lookup and answers CAO and policy questions from SharePoint content with named owners, in a bounded retrieve-and-draft loop. Anything it cannot answer becomes a ticket in the existing HR queue with the employee profile attached, and a monthly report shows content gaps.
tasks.previous_blocker: Answers depend on contract type, site, CAO and tenure. Old chatbots could not combine personal data with free-text policy, so wrong answers about pay were a real risk.
tasks.enabler_now: Models can read free-text questions and cite approved content, and AFAS exposes personal data through GetConnectors. A comparable HR bot runs at scale on a daily HR data sync [S1].
tasks.still_hard: Keeping the CAO and policy content current, per site and per CAO, takes owner time every month. Shop-floor workers without a work account need another way in, such as WhatsApp or a kiosk.
tasks.human_edge: Disputes, hardship cases and questions where the honest answer is 'it depends on your manager' need a person who knows the sites and the people.

ambition.what: Flex workers from the three agencies get answers on site rules, shift allowances and certificates. Today they mostly ask their agency or their team lead.

tasks.altitude: The administrator stops typing answers and becomes the content owner for HR answers. They decide which topics the bot may answer and they handle the escalations.

tasks.short: Process new-hire paperwork: collect data, enter employee and contract in AFAS, issue contract, notify others.
tasks.statement: Hire employees and process hiring-related paperwork.
tasks.design: A hire in Recruitee triggers a scheduled integration that creates a draft employee and contract in AFAS for the administrator to approve. AFAS Pocket onboarding collects the new hire's own data and documents, with Jonas reading the documents into fields. After approval, AFAS generates the CAO contract from a template and sends it for signature, and the same job notifies payroll, IT and the manager and enrols the hire in Studytube by role.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recruitee and AFAS were never linked. Contract variants per CAO and site lived in Word templates, and nobody owned building the connector.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS Profit 8 has Pocket pre-boarding and Jonas document reading [S4]. Connector code between documented APIs is now cheap to write and test.
tasks.still_hard: Contract variants for two CAOs, three sites and fixed-term rules need careful templating. The employer must still check original ID documents in person.
tasks.human_edge: Approving the contract terms, handling unusual offers, and checking the ID face to face stay with the administrator.

ambition.what: Check every new hire's dossier for completeness before day one, not after the first payroll run.

tasks.altitude: The administrator approves drafts and handles exceptions instead of typing. They decide whether a dossier is ready for the payroll cut-off.

tasks.short: Search employee files in AFAS and old documents to answer requests and prepare personnel actions.
tasks.statement: Examine employee files to answer inquiries and provide information for personnel actions.
tasks.design: Requests come in through an AFAS workflow form instead of mail. A deterministic job pulls contract history from AFAS, computes chain-rule and CAO checks, and fills standard statements from templates. A bounded extraction loop reads only non-medical scanned documents and flags mismatches. The administrator approves anything that leaves the company.
tasks.previous_blocker: Old dossiers are scans, and chain-rule checks lived in personal Excel sheets. Nobody coded the CAO exceptions.
tasks.enabler_now: Extraction from scanned documents is reliable enough with a check against structured AFAS dates. Rule code for the ketenregeling is quick to write and test.
tasks.still_hard: Special-category data (health, union membership) sits in the same dossiers and must be kept out of model prompts. CAO deviations on the chain rule need careful encoding.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding what a request is really for, and whether sharing a fact is allowed under AVG, stays with the administrator.

ambition.what: A monthly list of contracts nearing the chain-rule limit for every manager, 3 months before the deadline.

tasks.altitude: The administrator stops searching and starts signing off statements and flagging risks. They decide which facts may be shared and with whom.

tasks.short: Chase and collect missing personnel documents and certificates from employees, managers and staffing agencies.
tasks.statement: Gather personnel records from other departments or employees.
tasks.design: Replace the Excel tracking sheet with a nightly job that compares AFAS dossiers, Studytube certificates and agency worker lists against a checklist per role and site. It sends reminders by Teams or mail and shows gaps in a Power BI dashboard. Uploads go through AFAS Pocket, a bounded classification loop files them, and the administrator handles only unmatched items and staff who must be approached in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: The data sat in three systems and three agency portals with no shared key. The checklist per role lived in someone's head and an Excel sheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Connector and matching code is now cheap to build, and AFAS Pocket gives employees an upload channel [S4]. Document classification with a match check is good enough for filing.
tasks.still_hard: Agency portals may have no API, so exports or scraping are needed. Warehouse staff without email still need a face-to-face reminder from a team lead.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a reluctant employee or a busy shift lead to hand over a document is a people job.

ambition.what: Track forklift, VCA and food-safety certificates for agency flex workers, not only for own staff.

tasks.altitude: The administrator stops chasing and works from an exceptions list. They decide when a missing certificate is escalated to the site manager.

tasks.short: Read applications in Recruitee, check them against job requirements, and pass suitable candidates to hiring managers.
tasks.statement: Select applicants meeting specified job requirements and refer them to hiring personnel.
tasks.design: A small extraction job reads new Recruitee applications and writes certificate, shift and permit fields back to the candidate profile. Deterministic rules per vacancy then mark each criterion as met, missing or unclear, and show it on the candidate card. The administrator confirms the shortlist; Recruitee automations send it to the hiring manager and send Teams reminders if there is no feedback after two days.
tasks.previous_blocker: Free-text CVs in several languages could not be turned into reliable fields without a person reading them. Knock-out criteria lived in people's heads, not in a table.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models extract fields from CVs with a quoted source span that can be checked. Recruitee exposes candidates and custom fields through its API. AI coding makes the rules table and job cheap to build.
tasks.still_hard: Judging near-misses: an expired VCA certificate, transferable experience, a candidate for another site. The legal frame also limits automation: from December 2027 screening becomes high-risk, so ranking or rejecting by machine is not an option.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing potential behind a thin CV and weighing it against what this manager and team need. The shortlist decision stays with a person, who can explain it.

ambition.what: Re-screen the whole Recruitee talent pool each time a new vacancy opens, so earlier applicants with a forklift or VCA certificate get referred again.

tasks.altitude: Screening time drops by about half. The administrator decides from a pre-filled criteria card instead of reading every CV, and owns the knock-out table per job family.

tasks.short: Tell applicants by mail or phone that they are hired or rejected, and record it in Recruitee.
tasks.statement: Inform job applicants of their acceptance or rejection of employment.
tasks.design: Configure Recruitee so the hiring manager or recruiter records the decision as a stage move with a reason code. That move triggers the matching Dutch or English template with a short delay so it can be undone, and sets the retention date for deletion. Interviewed candidates who are rejected get a phone call from the recruiter or administrator, prompted by a task. No custom code is needed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Decisions arrived by mail and phone, not as a stage in the system, so nothing could trigger a message. Templates sat in Word on SharePoint.
tasks.enabler_now: Recruitee stage automations, templates and retention settings already exist; the work is configuration and getting managers to record the decision in Recruitee. A model is not needed at run time.
tasks.still_hard: Getting hiring managers on three sites to record decisions in Recruitee instead of calling HR. Delicate cases, such as internal candidates or people who were close, still need a human message.
tasks.human_edge: The call to a rejected internal candidate or a strong finalist, and handling questions about why. That conversation keeps people willing to apply again.

ambition.what: Applicants who are never interviewed get a clear answer within five working days, plus an offer to stay in the talent pool for 12 months with consent.

tasks.altitude: The administrator no longer writes letters. They own the template set and reason codes, check the weekly list of applicants without an answer, and keep the calls that matter.

tasks.short: Handle employee requests for pension, allowances, bike plan and sickness-insurance matters; check eligibility and process changes in AFAS.
tasks.statement: Provide assistance in administering employee benefit programs and worker's compensation plans.
tasks.design: Employees request bike plan, allowance and pension changes through AFAS InSite or Pocket workflow forms. Deterministic rules on contract group and CAO check eligibility, and after the administrator approves, the workflow writes the mutation to AFAS before the payroll cut-off. A Teams answer desk on owned SharePoint policy pages answers general questions, quotes personal entitlements from an AFAS lookup, and opens a ticket for anything about sickness or personal circumstances. Pension fund and insurer reports are generated from AFAS for the administrator to check and send.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests came by mail and phone, and the CAO and policy rules were in PDFs, not in a table, so every case was read and re-keyed by hand. Health and absence data made people wary of automation.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS workflows and InSite forms are already licensed and only need configuring. Answer desks grounded in owned content, with ticket escalation, are proven in HR. AI coding makes the rules table and report exports cheap to build.
tasks.still_hard: Exceptions such as part-time changes mid-month, retroactive corrections, and staff covered by both CAOs. Sickness insurer and UWV cases involve special-category health data, which must stay out of model prompts. The works council must agree, and the policy content must be kept current.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining a pension or sickness-pay consequence to a worried employee, and spotting when a benefit question is really about illness or money trouble.

ambition.what: Warehouse and transport shift workers without a desk get Dutch and Polish answers on their phone through Teams or AFAS Pocket, outside office hours.

tasks.altitude: The administrator approves mutations from a queue instead of typing them, owns the policy pages and rules table, and handles the tickets that need a person.

tasks.short: Turn approved vacancy requests into ads, publish them externally and internally, and close them when filled.
tasks.statement: Arrange for advertising or posting of job vacancies and notify eligible workers of position availability.
tasks.design: Managers submit vacancies through a Recruitee requisition or a Microsoft Forms and Power Automate flow, which checks approval against the AFAS formation. A drafting step fills the house template from the function profile and the CAO scale table; the administrator edits and approves. Recruitee multiposting then publishes it, a small job posts it to Teams, the SharePoint vacancy page and the warehouse screens, and the ads close when the stage changes to hired.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests came by mail without a fixed format. Ad texts were rewritten by hand each time. Internal notices depended on someone remembering to post them on each site.
tasks.enabler_now: Recruitee requisitions and multiposting are configuration. Models draft acceptable ad text when facts come from tables. Teams and SharePoint posting can be scripted cheaply.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping function profiles and the CAO scale table current. Deciding where to advertise for scarce roles such as truck drivers. Reaching shift workers who rarely open Teams.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what makes a job at the Venlo or Tilburg site attractive and which channel works for scarce roles, and pushing back on managers whose requirements are unrealistic.

ambition.what: Flex workers from the three agencies see every internal vacancy at the same time as employees, so good flex workers move into permanent roles.

tasks.altitude: The administrator edits and approves instead of writing and posting. They own the ad templates and the channel list, and a vacancy is live within a day of approval.

tasks.short: Answer requests from banks, bailiffs, UWV and lenders by looking up employee data in AFAS and filling forms.
tasks.statement: Search employee files to obtain information for authorized persons and organizations, such as credit bureaus and finance companies.
tasks.design: A shared HR mailbox feeds a small intake workflow (Power Automate or a scheduled Python job on the governed platform). A bounded model step classifies each request and maps the form, a deterministic AFAS lookup fills the statement, and the administrator approves and sends from a review queue. Each disclosure is logged back into the AFAS dossier, and loonbeslag requests are also routed to Payroll.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests come in many formats, from many outside parties, and each one needs an authority check. Building templates per form type cost more than the volume justified.
tasks.enabler_now: Models can read varied PDFs and mails into fixed fields, and AI coding makes templates and AFAS connector queries cheap to build.
tasks.still_hard: Judging whether a requester may receive data, and handling odd cases such as a pending dismissal or a variable-hours contract, stays with the administrator. Every outgoing statement is irreversible.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a disclosure is lawful and proportionate under AVG, and answering questions from the employee or a bailiff when the facts are unusual.

ambition.what: Employee self-service for their own werkgeversverklaring and salary statement, generated from AFAS the same day.

tasks.altitude: The administrator approves a queue of prepared statements instead of building each one. They gain the right to decide which request types are fully templated and which need a check by the HRBP.

tasks.short: Compile monthly and ad hoc personnel reports from AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube and agency exports in Excel.
tasks.statement: Compile and prepare reports and documents pertaining to personnel activities.
tasks.design: Replace the monthly Excel workbook that combines AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube and agency exports with scheduled extract jobs into the governed data platform behind the existing Power BI model. Standard reports become Power BI pages with row-level security per site, and a bounded model step drafts commentary that the administrator checks before a subscription sends the report.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recruitee, Studytube and the agency portals were never connected to the nightly AFAS extract. Each report was a one-off Excel job that nobody had time to rebuild properly.
tasks.enabler_now: APIs exist for AFAS, Recruitee and Studytube, and AI coding makes the extract jobs and Power BI measures fast to build. Agency portals still need file drops.
tasks.still_hard: Agency data comes as different exports from three portals, and definitions (FTE, flex headcount, verzuim percentage) must be agreed once. Ad hoc requests from the OR or management still need judgement about what to show.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what a manager or the OR actually needs to see, and spotting a figure that is technically right but misleading.

ambition.what: A weekly view per site of open roles, offer acceptance, week-one onboarding and 90-day retention, instead of a monthly Excel report.

tasks.altitude: The administrator checks and explains reports instead of building them. They own the report definitions and decide, with the People Analyst, which ad hoc questions become standard pages.

tasks.short: Keep org charts, the employee handbook, directories and evaluation forms current after changes in AFAS, the CAO or policy.
tasks.statement: Maintain and update human resources documents, such as organizational charts, employee handbooks or directories, or performance evaluation forms.
tasks.design: Org charts and directories are generated each night from the AFAS org structure, either in Power BI or through the Microsoft 365 directory, so they are no longer kept by hand. Handbook changes run as a SharePoint approval flow: a bounded model step drafts a redline from the CAO or policy change, the HRBP approves it, and publishing and the Teams notice are automatic.
tasks.previous_blocker: Org data in AFAS was not trusted enough to publish directly, and handbook updates needed someone to read the CAO and find every affected section.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS can feed the M365 directory and Power BI, and models can draft redlines from legal text with a person checking them.
tasks.still_hard: AFAS data quality (managers, cost centres, flex workers who are not in AFAS) sets the quality of the generated org charts. Handbook wording that has legal effect still needs an HRBP and sometimes OR consent under WOR art. 27.
tasks.human_edge: Judging how a CAO change applies to Noordhaven's own warehouse arrangements, and writing policy text that shift workers on the floor understand.

ambition.what: A handbook Q&A in Teams for all 1,200 staff, labelled as AI and answering from the maintained handbook, with a ticket to HR when it cannot answer.

tasks.altitude: The administrator becomes the handbook content owner instead of the person who copy-edits charts. They decide the structure of the handbook and flag which changes need the HRBP or the OR.

tasks.short: Set weekly priorities for the 13-person HR team, chase status, approve exceptions, coach direct reports.
tasks.statement: Plan, direct, supervise, and coordinate work activities of subordinates and staff relating to employment, compensation, labor relations, and employee relations.
tasks.design: Replace the Excel tracker and the status mail round with a Power BI team-workload page fed nightly from AFAS (absence cases, mutations), Recruitee (open vacancies, stage age) and Studytube (overdue certificates), plus Teams notifications when an item breaches its agreed age. Exceptions run through configured AFAS workflow approvals with CAO-table pre-checks, and a small drafting step writes the MT update around code-inserted figures.
tasks.previous_blocker: Status lived in three systems and people's heads; building cross-system views cost more analyst time than the chasing it saved.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS, Recruitee and Studytube all expose APIs and Power BI already holds a nightly AFAS extract; AI-assisted coding makes the joins and alert rules a matter of days.
tasks.still_hard: Case age is a weak proxy for case difficulty; the dashboard will flag slow cases that are slow for good reasons.
tasks.human_edge: Coaching HRBPs, weighing a manager's request against fairness across sites, and carrying accountability for approvals stay with the director.

ambition.what: Re-balance team workload weekly across the three sites instead of at quarterly planning.

tasks.altitude: Less chasing, more time on direct reports; the director gains the right to set which exception types auto-approve within CAO bounds and which always need sign-off.

tasks.short: Answer managers' policy questions, advise on harassment and equal treatment cases, propose policy changes.
tasks.statement: Advise managers on organizational policy matters, such as equal employment opportunity and sexual harassment, and recommend needed changes.
tasks.design: A Teams policy desk answers routine manager questions from SharePoint policies and the two CAOs with cited articles, discloses that it is an assistant (AI Act Art. 50) and hands sensitive topics straight to the HRBP queue. Every question is logged; a monthly Power BI page shows question themes by site, which feeds policy proposals, and the director drafts sensitive advice with a bounded drafting step.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policies and CAO texts were too long and inconsistent for keyword search, and a wrong answer on law carries legal cost.
tasks.enabler_now: Retrieval with forced citation now answers from long documents reliably enough for routine questions, with routing as the safety net.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping SharePoint policies current and consistent; a stale document gives a confidently cited wrong answer.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing both sides in a harassment case, weighing credibility and protecting the reporter cannot be delegated.

ambition.what: Shift leads and team leaders in the Tilburg and Venlo warehouses, who rarely reach HR today, get answers at night and on weekend shifts.

tasks.altitude: Fewer interruptions on routine questions; the director decides which topics the desk may answer and owns the hand-off list.

tasks.short: Pull HR data, find causes of turnover, absence and hiring problems, recommend policy changes.
tasks.statement: Analyze statistical data and reports to identify and determine causes of personnel problems and develop recommendations for improvement of organization's personnel policies and practices.
tasks.design: Extend the nightly AFAS extract into a governed metric layer that also loads Recruitee stages, Studytube completions and agency hours, and publish fixed Power BI pages for the North Star: hire-to-day-90 retention, time to hire, week-one onboarding and verzuim by site, shift and agency. A bounded classification step tags pseudonymised exit comments into fixed themes; the director keeps the reading of causes and the recommendation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Four sources with different employee keys and no analyst time to join them; every question became a one-off Excel job.
tasks.enabler_now: Power BI and the AFAS extract already exist; AI-assisted coding makes the Recruitee, Studytube and agency joins cheap to build and maintain.
tasks.still_hard: Matching flex workers from agency portals to later AFAS hires, and small group sizes per shift that make causes noisy and identities guessable.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which correlation is a cause, and which recommendation managers and the OR will accept, needs the director's knowledge of the sites.

ambition.what: Review 90-day retention by site and agency every month instead of once a year.

tasks.altitude: From ordering numbers to reading them; the director decides each month which site or agency gets an intervention.

tasks.short: Plan the HR year: training, certificates, works council and union agenda, HR budget with Finance.
tasks.statement: Plan, organize, direct, control, or coordinate the personnel, training, or labor relations activities of an organization.
tasks.design: Configure Studytube expiry alerts and a Power BI certificate page joined to AFAS rosters so forklift and VCA gaps reach shift leads before they lapse. A Python costing model on the governed data platform prices CAO demands and budget scenarios from AFAS payroll and agency hours, with a bounded extraction step reading union demand letters; the director keeps the plan, the OR consultation and the bargaining.
tasks.previous_blocker: Costing CAO demands meant rebuilding payroll logic in Excel each round, and certificate tracking depended on manual exports.
tasks.enabler_now: Studytube has native expiry reminders; AI-assisted coding makes a reusable costing model affordable, and the 2027 transport CAO round is starting now.
tasks.still_hard: Modelling the pension switch and the in-house warehouse CAO interactions; scenario assumptions remain a judgement call.
tasks.human_edge: Building trust with the OR and unions and choosing what to trade at the table are the director's work.

ambition.what: Same-day costing of any union counter-proposal during the 2027 CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer round.

tasks.altitude: More time at the bargaining table and with the OR; the director decides scenario assumptions and which AI uses go to the OR for consent.

tasks.short: Build the yearly HR personnel budget in Excel from AFAS data and CAO tables, then track it monthly.
tasks.statement: Prepare and follow budgets for personnel operations.
tasks.design: Replace the budget workbook with a scheduled Python job on the governed data platform that reads AFAS positions and payroll, the agency invoices and a versioned CAO rate table, and writes a cost baseline plus editable scenario parameters. A Power BI page shows scenarios side by side and the monthly actual-versus-budget variance per site and cost type, refreshed with the nightly AFAS extract.
tasks.previous_blocker: CAO rules, agency rates and AFAS exports lived in separate files, and building a reliable rate engine cost more than one yearly Excel exercise.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes a small, tested rate engine and data job cheap to build, and the nightly AFAS extract for Power BI already exists.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping the CAO rate table correct after each wage round, and flex costs that swing with seasonal volume.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing where to spend scarce money (wages, flex, training) and defending that choice with Finance and the works council.

ambition.what: Re-forecast the personnel budget monthly per site instead of once a year, including the cost of each CAO offer during the 2027 round.

tasks.altitude: Less time in Excel, more time on trade-offs; the director owns the scenario assumptions that Finance accepts as input.

tasks.short: Read new labour law, court rulings and CAO news and judge what they mean for Noordhaven.
tasks.statement: Study legislation, arbitration decisions, and collective bargaining contracts to assess industry trends.
tasks.design: A scheduled job fetches fixed sources (rechtspraak.nl, overheid.nl, Staatscourant, FNV, CNV, employer association pages) into a SharePoint list, and a bounded model step labels relevance and writes cited summaries for a weekly digest in Teams. The director writes the impact notes; a second bounded step drafts the monthly brief from them, marked as AI-generated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Legal text is unstructured and Dutch, and summarisers made up points without sources.
tasks.enabler_now: Current models summarise Dutch legal text with quoted citations well enough for a reviewed digest, at low cost.
tasks.still_hard: Judging what a ruling means for Noordhaven's own CAO and staff, and sources behind paywalls.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which change matters for the people and the bargaining position, and taking responsibility for advice.

ambition.what: A monthly plain-language legal and CAO brief for the 30 site and shift managers, who get nothing today.

tasks.altitude: Reading time drops; the director spends it on impact judgement and on the 2027 CAO round preparation.

tasks.short: Run job evaluation: describe jobs, score them in the function system, set the scale, handle objections.
tasks.statement: Oversee the evaluation, classification, and rating of occupations and job positions.
tasks.design: Configure an AFAS workflow for evaluation requests with the description attached, and add a bounded model step that rewrites descriptions into the template and lists nearest reference jobs, without scoring. A Power BI page shows the cost and pay-gap effect of a proposed grade; the committee scores, and AFAS generates the letter after approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Descriptions arrived as free text in mail, and matching them to the function house needed an expert reading each one.
tasks.enabler_now: Models now rewrite and compare job texts reliably, and the AFAS workflow and Power BI extract already exist.
tasks.still_hard: Scoring remains judgement, objections are personal, and the works council must trust that the method is neutral.
tasks.human_edge: Weighing a job's real content fairly and explaining a grade face to face when someone objects.

ambition.what: An equal-pay check per job family, refreshed yearly, ready for the EU pay transparency rules.

tasks.altitude: The director chairs fewer, better prepared committees and owns the reference job set.

tasks.short: Forecast staffing needs per site and shift from volume plans, turnover and absence.
tasks.statement: Prepare personnel forecast to project employment needs.
tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform builds the workforce baseline from AFAS and the agency portals, and a small form (Microsoft Forms or a SharePoint list) collects site volume plans in a fixed format. A deterministic model with stated assumptions turns them into FTE need per site and shift under three scenarios in Power BI, feeding the budget and the recruiters' pipeline.
tasks.previous_blocker: Volume plans came in different shapes by mail, and agency hours were not joined to AFAS data.
tasks.enabler_now: The nightly AFAS extract and cheap AI-assisted coding make the joins and a transparent scenario model a few days of work.
tasks.still_hard: Client volume is uncertain and seasonal; forecast quality only shows months later.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding how much risk to carry between fixed staff and flex, and getting site managers to commit to their numbers.

ambition.what: Quarterly rolling forecast per site and shift, instead of one yearly plan, timed before the seasonal flex peak.

tasks.altitude: The director moves from compiling numbers to setting the fixed-versus-flex policy per site with operations.

tasks.short: Field manager and employee questions, apply contracts and CAO to cases, help resolve work problems.
tasks.statement: Serve as a link between management and employees by handling questions, interpreting and administering contracts and helping resolve work-related problems.
tasks.design: A Teams front door (Copilot Studio or a small app on the M365 tenant) takes questions, classifies them with one bounded model call and answers general policy from the indexed SharePoint and CAO content; personal and conflict cases open a case in a SharePoint list with an auto-built case brief from the AFAS API. The HRBP gets a draft clause reading with citations, does the conversation, and a Power Automate flow turns the agreed outcome into a template letter and an AFAS change request for HR admin.
tasks.previous_blocker: Questions arrive as unstructured talk and mail, and pulling contract, absence and CAO context took manual clicks in three places.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS Profit connectors and cheap retrieval over owned documents make a case brief and a cited clause draft a few days of build.
tasks.still_hard: Trust from shift workers and managers who expect a person, and cases where the facts are disputed; the model must never decide a personal case.
tasks.human_edge: Reading the room between a site manager and a worker, choosing what to concede, and being trusted by both sides.

ambition.what: Night and weekend shift workers in the warehouses get answers to contract and roster questions in their own shift instead of waiting for an office-hours HRBP.

tasks.altitude: The HRBP spends less time looking things up and more time on the 20-30 real conflicts per month per site; they decide which case categories the desk may answer alone.

tasks.short: Explain HR policies, CAO rules, procedures and Dutch law to managers and employees.
tasks.statement: Interpret and explain human resources policies, procedures, laws, standards, or regulations.
tasks.design: An answer desk in Teams built on the M365 tenant retrieves from one approved SharePoint library (policies, both CAOs, poortwachter procedure) and answers general questions with citations and an AI disclosure; anything personal becomes a ticket for the site HRBP. A weekly report of unanswered and escalated questions feeds policy fixes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Earlier bots needed hand-built intent trees and failed on Dutch everyday wording and CAO detail.
tasks.enabler_now: Retrieval with a model that cites clauses, on content HR already owns, is now standard in M365 and similar tools.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping the source library current and versioned, and a wrong answer on law (ontslag, verzuim) has legal cost; the escalation line must be strict.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a 'general' question is really about one person, and explaining a hard rule so it is accepted.

ambition.what: Every new team leader gets a policy answer within minutes for every question, instead of saving them up for the monthly HRBP meeting.

tasks.altitude: The HRBP stops answering the same leave and overtime questions and owns the escalated cases and the quality of the policy library.

tasks.short: Match staff to roles, shifts and sites: redeployment, internal moves, peak-season staffing.
tasks.statement: Allocate human resources, ensuring appropriate matches between personnel.
tasks.design: Replace the site Excel sheets with a Power Apps request form and a nightly job on the existing Power BI extract that joins AFAS contracts and absence, Studytube certificates and agency headcount into a filterable availability view with hard-rule filters (valid forklift or VCA, contract hours, CAO working-time limits). The HRBP picks matches by hand; a Power Automate flow sends approved moves to HR admin and the agency order.
tasks.previous_blocker: Certificate, contract and absence data sit in three systems and the agency portals, so matching ran on memory and Excel.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes the join, filters and form a short build on data that already reaches Power BI nightly.
tasks.still_hard: No ranking or scoring of people: allocating tasks on traits or behaviour is high-risk under Annex III 4(b) from December 2027 and needs OR consent; agency portal data may only come as files.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing who works well together, who is fragile after absence, and negotiating a move a person accepts.

ambition.what: Weekly redeployment review across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo before ordering flex workers, instead of each site ordering agency staff alone.

tasks.altitude: The HRBP reviews a cross-site availability view weekly and decides internal moves before agency orders go out.

tasks.short: Advise management on recruiting and retention programmes using hiring and turnover data.
tasks.statement: Advise management on organizing, preparing, or implementing recruiting or retention programs.
tasks.design: Extend the nightly Power BI model with Recruitee pipeline data so the North Star (filled roles still productive at day 90) and its inputs show per site and job family; a bounded model step tags pseudonymised exit and onboarding comments into fixed themes. A Word template plus one draft step produces the advice note, which the HRBP rewrites and presents.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recruitee and AFAS data were never joined, so each advice note started with a manual Excel exercise and exit comments went unread.
tasks.enabler_now: Recruitee's API and the existing AFAS extract can be joined with little code; theme tagging of short comments is cheap and checkable.
tasks.still_hard: Proving cause: a retention dip may be the season or one manager; the advice still rests on HRBP judgement and site knowledge.
tasks.human_edge: Telling a site director that their own team leader is the retention problem, and getting a programme funded.

ambition.what: A quarterly retention review per site with each site director, instead of an ad hoc note when turnover is already high.

tasks.altitude: The HRBP spends advice time on options and persuasion, not on building figures, and brings a site-level retention agenda to each quarterly review.

tasks.short: Answer managers' questions and train them on interviewing, appraisals, difficult talks and documenting performance issues.
tasks.statement: Provide management with information or training related to interviewing, performance appraisals, counseling techniques, or documentation of performance issues.
tasks.design: A Copilot Studio answer desk in Teams answers managers' general questions from the approved SharePoint policy and CAO library, says it is AI, and opens a ticket to the HRBP for anything about a named person. A drafting step builds training kits and guides from house templates for HRBP review, and a Power Automate checklist on the AFAS performance file reminds managers of missing steps in an improvement plan (meeting notes, signed plan, review dates).
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy answers depended on the HRBP knowing where everything sat; chatbots before 2023 could not read free-text questions against long policy texts well enough.
tasks.enabler_now: Retrieval over owned SharePoint content with source citations is a configurable product feature, and drafting Dutch training material is cheap; IBM and Coca-Cola Andina run such front doors at scale.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping the policy library current and correct; managers trusting the answers; the coaching itself and the judgement in a performance case.
tasks.human_edge: Coaching a team lead through a first hard conversation with a long-serving warehouse worker, and judging when a performance issue is really an absence or personal problem.

ambition.what: Short just-in-time guidance for the roughly 60 shift and team leads in the warehouses, who now rarely get HR training.

tasks.altitude: The HRBP spends less time on repeat questions and more on the escalated cases and coaching; they decide which guidance goes into the library and when a case needs their direct involvement.

tasks.short: Design ways to track employee satisfaction and run grievance and complaint procedures, with the works council.
tasks.statement: Develop methods to monitor employee satisfaction with policies or working conditions, including grievance or complaint procedures.
tasks.design: Replace the complaint mailbox and Excel list with a restricted SharePoint grievance register fed by a Microsoft Forms intake, with Power Automate routing, response-time reminders and an appeal step. A Power BI page on the nightly AFAS extract combines absence, turnover and register counts per site, with a minimum group size so nobody is identifiable; a bounded drafting step helps write the procedure and survey for OR review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Signals sat in separate mailboxes, AFAS and notes, and nobody owned joining them; drafting procedures was slow work done rarely.
tasks.enabler_now: Power BI already runs on the AFAS extract, and Forms, SharePoint lists and Power Automate are in the existing Microsoft 365 licence; drafting help makes procedure text fast.
tasks.still_hard: Trust that complaints stay confidential, OR consent, small sites where anonymity breaks, and special-category data in complaints.
tasks.human_edge: Agreeing the method with the OR and building trust that warehouse and flex workers can complain without consequences.

ambition.what: A complaint and pulse route open to the 150 to 300 agency flex workers, who today fall outside HR's channels.

tasks.altitude: The HRBP sees satisfaction signals per site each month instead of once a year, and decides with the OR when to act on a hotspot.

tasks.short: Build reports and slides on employee satisfaction and related data for management and the works council.
tasks.statement: Prepare reports or presentations to communicate employee satisfaction or related data to management.
tasks.design: A scheduled job loads survey and register data next to the nightly AFAS extract into Power BI, which produces the site and department tables with a minimum group size. A bounded model step themes anonymised comments, and a report generator fills the house PowerPoint template with tables and a draft narrative for the HRBP to edit before the MT and OR meeting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each report was a one-off Excel job; reading hundreds of comments by hand was the slowest part and could not be scripted.
tasks.enabler_now: Power BI on AFAS already exists, and models can theme Dutch free text reliably enough for a reviewed first pass.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping anonymity in small groups, explaining causes rather than numbers, and handling bad news with managers.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding what the numbers mean for a site and which two actions to push with management and the OR.

ambition.what: Quarterly instead of yearly satisfaction review per site, linked to verzuim and 90-day retention.

tasks.altitude: The HRBP stops building spreadsheets and spends the time on the follow-up with site managers; they choose which findings go to the MT.

tasks.short: Run training sessions with role play, toolbox talks, group exercises, videos and short lectures on three sites.
tasks.statement: Present information with a variety of instructional techniques or formats, such as role playing, simulations, team exercises, group discussions, videos, or lectures.
tasks.design: Studytube AI Authoring and Microsoft 365 Copilot draft session plans, scenarios and slides from existing outlines; the specialist edits and the safety lead signs safety content. Studytube sessions and Outlook handle booking, reminders and the follow-up survey. Delivery stays in person; a disclosed AI practice partner lets team leads rehearse feedback conversations between sessions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing good scenarios and exercises took expert time and could not be templated; booking ran through mail because nobody set up Studytube session management.
tasks.enabler_now: Studytube AI Authoring and Copilot draft outlines, scripts and questions from a title or document, and a model can play a counterpart in a practice conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Reading the room, handling resistance on the warehouse floor and judging practical skill stay human; drafted scenarios still need local facts checked.
tasks.human_edge: Leading a group of shift workers in person, adapting on the spot, and judging whether people can actually do the task.

ambition.what: A disclosed AI feedback-practice partner for shift leaders, using the Situation-Behavior-Impact rubric, between classroom sessions.

tasks.altitude: About half of preparation time comes back and goes into more floor sessions and coaching. The specialist decides which sessions get a practice follow-up.

tasks.short: Write and update manuals, handouts, slides and e-learning from work instructions and safety rules.
tasks.statement: Obtain, organize, or develop training procedure manuals, guides, or course materials, such as handouts or visual materials.
tasks.design: A SharePoint library holds approved work instructions; Studytube AI Authoring turns them into course drafts and quizzes, and a bounded translation step with a fixed safety glossary produces plain Dutch, English and Polish versions. A Power Automate flow routes drafts to the safety lead for sign-off, then publishes to Studytube and flags courses whose source instruction changed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drafting and translating material was skilled writing work with no tool that could produce a usable first version from a PDF.
tasks.enabler_now: Studytube AI Authoring drafts from uploaded files, and models now rewrite and translate text well enough to edit instead of write.
tasks.still_hard: Getting correct, current work instructions from sites, and expert time for safety review; errors in safety content can hurt people.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding what workers really need to know, checking facts against how the job is done on the floor, and owning sign-off on safety content with the safety lead.

ambition.what: Flex workers from the three agencies get induction and safety handouts in their own language before their first shift.

tasks.altitude: Writing time drops to editing; the specialist spends more time on site checking that material matches practice. They own the glossary and the source-to-course link.

tasks.short: Plan, schedule and enrol staff in mandatory and skills training, mostly certificates for shift staff.
tasks.statement: Offer specific training programs to help workers maintain or improve job skills.
tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform joins Studytube certificate expiry dates, AFAS employees and shift rosters, and agency flex worker orders, and proposes session dates per site 60 days before a lapse. The specialist approves the proposal and trainer bookings; Studytube then enrols people, Teams notifies team leads, and no-shows are rebooked automatically with an escalation list.
tasks.previous_blocker: Certificates, rosters and flex orders sat in separate systems, tied together by an Excel sheet and mail; nobody had time to build and maintain the link.
tasks.enabler_now: Studytube and AFAS expose data by API or export, and AI coding makes a small join-and-schedule job a matter of days.
tasks.still_hard: Rosters change late, external trainers have limited dates, and flex worker data from agency portals may be thin or late.
tasks.human_edge: Agreeing with site managers when people can leave the floor, choosing trainers, and handling the person who keeps missing training.

ambition.what: Flex workers' forklift and VCA status checked against the agency order before their first shift.

tasks.altitude: The specialist stops building the monthly certificate sheet and approves schedules instead. They gain the right to block a shift booking for someone without a valid certificate, agreed with site managers.

tasks.short: Record attendance, collect evaluations and report on whether training works.
tasks.statement: Monitor, evaluate, or record training activities or program effectiveness.
tasks.design: Studytube session check-in by QR code replaces paper lists, and the nightly AFAS extract plus a Studytube feed land in a Power BI L&D page showing week-one onboarding, first-shift certification and 90-day retention by course and site. A bounded model step clusters anonymised comments at group level only, and the quarterly report is generated from the dashboard for the specialist to edit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Studytube data was not in the Power BI extract, attendance was on paper, and free-text comments took too long to read.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS already feeds Power BI nightly, adding a Studytube source is small, and models cluster short comments reliably enough for review.
tasks.still_hard: Showing that a course caused better retention; small groups, seasonal flex swings and no baseline make cause hard to prove.
tasks.human_edge: Agreeing measures with managers before a course starts and judging what the numbers mean for the programme.

ambition.what: Keep, fix or stop each course decided quarterly on outcome data instead of once a year on attendance.

tasks.altitude: No more monthly Excel merges; the specialist sets baselines with managers and decides course changes. Data stays at group level and outside appraisals.

tasks.short: Design and run onboarding and training programmes for shift and office staff across three sites.
tasks.statement: Design, plan, organize, or direct orientation and training programs for employees or customers.
tasks.design: Replace the scheduling spreadsheet with a nightly Python job on the governed data platform that reads new hires, start dates and shift rosters from AFAS, enrols people in the right Studytube onboarding path, sends Outlook invites, and flags missed week-one modules in a Power BI tile for the HR business partner. Materials are drafted in Studytube AI Authoring and approved by L&D; the site safety lead signs any safety content.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rosters, new-hire data and LMS enrolments live in separate systems and were tied together by hand in Excel; drafting material from scratch took days per course.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS and Studytube expose APIs, AI coding makes the glue job a few days of work, and Studytube's own authoring tool now drafts outlines and questions from existing documents.
tasks.still_hard: Matching sessions to rotating shifts and flex workers who start at short notice, and keeping safety content correct across three sites.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding what a forklift driver or team lead actually needs to learn, and earning manager buy-in on the floor.

ambition.what: Agency flex workers get a short pre-start safety and site induction in Studytube before their first shift.

tasks.altitude: The specialist stops booking rooms and chasing completions and spends the week on programme design with managers; they decide which onboarding path each job family gets.

tasks.short: Compare classroom, e-learning and blended delivery on cost, results and travel, and advise.
tasks.statement: Evaluate modes of training delivery, such as in-person or virtual, to optimize training effectiveness, training costs, or environmental impacts.
tasks.design: A Power BI report on the existing nightly AFAS extract plus a Studytube export shows cost per trained person, pass rate and travel per course and delivery mode, at group level only. A small model step clusters evaluation comments into themes; the specialist writes the advice.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cost sat in AFAS ledger lines and hours, results in Studytube, and nobody joined them; comment reading was manual.
tasks.enabler_now: Power BI already runs on AFAS; joining a Studytube export is cheap to build, and models cluster short comments reliably enough for a reviewed summary.
tasks.still_hard: Linking delivery mode to real on-the-job results, such as first-time pass at the outside VCA exam or fewer incidents, with small groups.
tasks.human_edge: Judging trade-offs a table cannot show, like whether shift workers will actually do e-learning at home or need paid classroom time.

ambition.what: Review delivery mode per course every quarter instead of once a year at budget time.

tasks.altitude: The specialist moves from building cost sheets to owning the delivery-mode decision per course, with evidence in hand.

tasks.short: Read journals, newsletters and legal updates to stay current in L&D.
tasks.statement: Keep up with developments in area of expertise by reading current journals, books, or magazine articles.
tasks.design: A weekly scheduled job pulls a fixed list of feeds and official pages (EU AI Act, wetten.overheid.nl, VCA scheme owner, Studytube release notes), a bounded model step ranks and summarises them into a digest in Outlook, and page-change watchers flag rule changes. Deep reading stays with the person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources are scattered and unstructured, and relevance filtering needed a reader.
tasks.enabler_now: Cheap model summaries and feed watchers make a filtered weekly digest a small build.
tasks.still_hard: Telling vendor claims from evidence; much L&D research is vendor-sponsored.
tasks.human_edge: Judging what applies to a Dutch warehouse workforce and what is hype; delegating the reading itself weakens learning.

ambition.what: A monthly two-paragraph 'what changed' note for HR covering AI Act Article 4, CAO training rules and certificate schemes.

tasks.altitude: Less time scanning, same time reading; the specialist becomes the team's named source on L&D rule changes.

tasks.short: Review outlines, slides and handouts from instructors before they are used.
tasks.statement: Evaluate training materials prepared by instructors, such as outlines, text, or handouts.
tasks.design: A SharePoint intake library with a Power Automate flow replaces the mailbox and tracker; each upload triggers a bounded model check against house style, B1 reading level and the linked procedure and syllabus, and posts a findings list to the specialist. The specialist and, for safety content, the site safety lead approve before publishing to Studytube.
tasks.previous_blocker: Material arrives in many formats by mail, and checking it against procedures needed a careful reader every time.
tasks.enabler_now: Models now read slides and documents and quote sources reliably enough for a checklist a person reviews; SharePoint flows are standard configuration.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping SharePoint procedures current, since checks are only as good as the reference; the model cannot judge whether a safety method is safe.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a trainer's method will work on a warehouse floor, and holding the conversation with the trainer.

ambition.what: Check every updated version of instructor material, not only new courses.

tasks.altitude: Review time per file drops by about half; the specialist sets the quality bar for external trainers and can refuse material.

tasks.short: Plan training sessions around rooms, forklifts, instructors and shift rosters, then book and enrol people.
tasks.statement: Schedule classes based on availability of classrooms, equipment, or instructors.
tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform reads Studytube expiry dates and enrolments, AFAS employee and site data, the shift roster and Outlook resource calendars for rooms, forklifts and instructors, and proposes a session plan per site. The L&D specialist approves or edits it in a small planning app; approved sessions are created in Studytube with Outlook invites, and team leads get a notice of who is released when. No model is needed at run time.
tasks.previous_blocker: The data sat in three places (Studytube, AFAS, team-lead rosters) and nobody would fund custom integration for a 140-hour-a-year task.
tasks.enabler_now: Studytube and AFAS have APIs and AI-assisted coding makes a small scheduler and approval screen a matter of days, not a project.
tasks.still_hard: Shift rosters may live outside AFAS or in team-lead spreadsheets, and external VCA and forklift instructors confirm by mail, so their availability stays partly manual.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiating release of shift staff in peak season with team leads, and judging which lapse risk matters most when slots are scarce.

ambition.what: Re-plan certificate sessions weekly per site instead of quarterly, so no shift worker starts a shift with a lapsed forklift or VCA certificate.

tasks.altitude: The specialist stops building the schedule and approves a proposed plan in about 30 minutes a week; they gain the right to book shift staff for training within agreed release windows.

tasks.short: Track training spend against budget and write reports that justify the cost to HR and finance.
tasks.statement: Monitor training costs and prepare budget reports to justify expenditures.
tasks.design: Replace the training-cost Excel file with a nightly job on the governed data platform that pulls training-related invoices and ledger lines from AFAS and enrolments from Studytube, allocates them by rules plus a small classification loop for unclear invoice lines, and feeds a Power BI training-spend page next to the existing HR dashboards. Each quarter a generator drafts the budget report from the same tables; the specialist edits it and the controller sees the same numbers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training invoices are booked on generic cost accounts in AFAS and supplier descriptions do not match course names, so matching took manual work every month.
tasks.enabler_now: The nightly AFAS extract already exists for Power BI, and a bounded model step can now map free-text invoice lines to course codes with a reconciliation check.
tasks.still_hard: Spend that is not invoiced (internal instructor hours, lost shift hours) and sector training fund subsidies need agreed rules with finance before they can be counted.
tasks.human_edge: Arguing the case for training spend to the HR director and controller, and choosing which outcomes (certified first shift, 90-day retention) to tie the money to.

ambition.what: A monthly training-spend view per site that the HR director and controller use to move budget between sites mid-year, instead of one year-end justification.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends an hour a month checking allocations and a few hours a quarter on the narrative; they gain a shared number with finance and a say in budget reallocation during the year.

tasks.short: Design and run development programmes that grow warehouse and office staff into team lead and management roles.
tasks.statement: Devise programs to develop executive potential among employees in lower-level positions.
tasks.design: Keep selection and delivery human. Use Studytube AI Authoring and a drafting step in Microsoft 365 to produce programme outlines and modules from the competence profile, and a Power BI page that follows participants' completion, promotion and retention at group level with a comment-clustering step for feedback. A feedback-practice copilot can support new team leads, disclosed as AI.
tasks.previous_blocker: Programmes were built from scratch each time and the specialist had little time beside scheduling and compliance training, so floor staff rarely got a development track.
tasks.enabler_now: Studytube's authoring feature drafts modules from uploaded material, freeing design time, and drafting tools make outlines quick to produce and revise.
tasks.still_hard: Picking candidates fairly across sites and shifts, and showing results, which only appear after months. Any AI that scores candidates would be high-risk under the AI Act from December 2027 and needs works council consent.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting potential in people on the floor, convincing managers to release them, and coaching them through the first lead role.

ambition.what: A team-lead track for warehouse and transport shift workers on all three sites, including night shifts, who have had no development route so far.

tasks.altitude: Less time on slide building, more time with candidates and managers; the specialist gets a recognised voice in succession talks with HR business partners.

tasks.short: Build and roll out training on energy, fuel, waste separation and recycling for warehouse, transport and office staff.
tasks.statement: Develop or implement training programs related to efficiency, recycling, or other issues with environmental impacts.
tasks.design: Draft modules and toolbox cards in Studytube AI Authoring from the site procedures on SharePoint, with translated versions for non-Dutch-speaking shift and flex staff, and a SharePoint approval flow for the site lead's sign-off. Studytube audience rules fed by AFAS function and site enrol people automatically, and a Power BI page puts completion next to site waste and fuel figures at site level.
tasks.previous_blocker: Low priority and low frequency: producing multilingual content for a yearly topic cost more than it seemed worth, so it stayed a slide deck at a toolbox meeting.
tasks.enabler_now: AI authoring and translation make short multilingual modules cheap, and Studytube audience rules can enrol by function and site without manual lists.
tasks.still_hard: Showing an effect: waste and fuel figures may not be tracked per site or team, and behaviour change depends on site managers, not the course.
tasks.human_edge: Working with site leads to choose the few behaviours that matter on each site and making the toolbox talk land with drivers and warehouse staff.

ambition.what: Flex workers from the three staffing agencies get the site waste and energy instruction in their own language on their first shift.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends time with site leads and on measuring, not producing slides; little else changes for this yearly task.

tasks.short: Check shift hours, overtime and pay adjustments against roster and contracts, then post approved mutations in AFAS.
tasks.statement: Verify attendance, hours worked, and pay adjustments, and post information onto designated records.
tasks.design: Replace the Excel hours worksheet with a scheduled Python job on the governed data platform. It reads hours, rosters, contracts and absence through AFAS GetConnectors and runs explicit CAO rules. Clean lines are posted through UpdateConnectors once payroll approves the batch. Team leads get a Teams message for each break, and payroll works from an exception list in Power BI.
tasks.previous_blocker: Two CAOs, shift allowances and data in several places made a rules engine look costly. The Excel sheet was quicker to change than custom code.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes it cheap to write and test the rule code and connectors. AFAS connectors and a nightly extract already exist for Power BI.
tasks.still_hard: Hours that are late or wrong at the source, and CAO edge cases such as split shifts and public holidays, still need a person. Rules must be maintained every time a CAO changes.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding with a team lead whether disputed overtime was worked and agreed, and knowing which teams always submit late.

ambition.what: Check hours weekly instead of only at month close, so errors are fixed before the pay run.

tasks.altitude: Payroll spends about a third of today's time on this, all of it on exceptions. Payroll gains the right to block a team's mutations until its lead confirms the hours.

tasks.short: Enter variable pay, calculate exceptions in Excel, run and check the AFAS trial payroll, then finalise.
tasks.statement: Compute wages and deductions, and enter data into computers.
tasks.design: Gross-to-net stays in AFAS Profit. Retroactive raises and final settlements move from Excel into AFAS configuration where possible. A scheduled Python job reads the trial run and checks it against last month and explicit rules, for example: gross pay moved more than expected, pension stopped while still enrolled, leaver paid twice, rate below minimum wage. A bounded model step drafts a short cause for each hit, and payroll approves the run from the report.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comparing runs needed custom reports, and writing plain explanations of exceptions took a person.
tasks.enabler_now: Rule code is cheap to write and test now, and a bounded model step can explain an exception from the structured run data. Vendors already run such checks in production.
tasks.still_hard: Thresholds must be tuned so the list is short enough to read. Retroactive CAO raises across two CAOs stay error-prone, and a wrong check that stays silent is worse than no check.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether an unusual result is right, for example a large back payment, and deciding to hold or release the run.

ambition.what: A short report for each pay run, for the Controller, with exceptions found, corrections and first-time-right rate.

tasks.altitude: Payroll checks a ranked exception list instead of scanning spreadsheets, and close is about a day shorter. They own the check rules and the go or no-go decision for each run.

tasks.short: Record holiday, special and sick leave, keep balances right and reconcile leave with pay.
tasks.statement: Keep track of leave time, such as vacation, personal, and sick leave, for employees.
tasks.design: Move leave requests into AFAS InSite and Pocket workflows, so the team lead approves and the record posts without a mail. Leave schemes for both CAOs, including expiry and part-time accrual, are configured in AFAS. A check in the same scheduled job compares absence and leave with pay mutations and lists breaks. Employees see their own balance in AFAS Pocket.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shift workers without a desk or AFAS login send requests to supervisors on paper and in mail. CAO leave rules were never fully configured in AFAS.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS self-service on phones is now normal for shift staff. Configuration and the check code are fast to build and test.
tasks.still_hard: Sick leave data is special-category data under GDPR, so access must be tight. Supervisors without login, plus CAO special leave and old balances, need cleanup first.
tasks.human_edge: Handling disputed balances and sensitive situations, such as long-term sickness under Wet verbetering poortwachter, with care.

ambition.what: Warehouse and transport shift workers see and request their own leave on their phone for the first time.

tasks.altitude: Payroll stops being the leave mailbox and handles only reconciliation breaks and disputes. They decide how CAO leave rules are configured.

tasks.short: Process joiners, transfers, leavers and tax credit choices into AFAS payroll records, including final settlements.
tasks.statement: Record employee information, such as exemptions, transfers, and resignations, to maintain and update payroll records.
tasks.design: HR admin enters joiners, transfers and leavers once in an AFAS workflow, and payroll approves the payroll fields instead of re-keying them. A deterministic validation checks required fields. A bounded extraction step compares uploaded tax credit forms and contracts with what was entered. Leaver settlements use a fixed calculation script that payroll checks before the last run.
tasks.previous_blocker: HR and payroll worked in separate mail flows, and the forms arrive as scans that rules cannot read.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS workflows already exist but are not used end to end. Document extraction is now reliable enough when every field is checked against the entered data.
tasks.still_hard: Changes that arrive late or out of order around the payroll cut-off. Transition payments and disputed final settlements need legal judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Judging unclear cases, such as a mid-month transfer between CAOs or a disputed final settlement, and explaining them to the employee.

ambition.what: Check every joiner and leaver before the cut-off date instead of finding errors after payment.

tasks.altitude: Payroll approves instead of types and spends the saved time on leaver settlements and checks. They gain the right to reject an incomplete change back to HR admin.

tasks.short: Check the payroll pre-run against hours, contracts and last month, then find and fix discrepancies.
tasks.statement: Review time sheets, work charts, wage computation, and other information to detect and reconcile payroll discrepancies.
tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform pulls the AFAS pre-run, contracts and hours through AFAS GetConnectors. It runs an explicit rule catalogue: gross pay moved more than the set threshold, pension stopped for an enrolled employee, a leaver still paid, below minimum wage, and shift allowance without hours. Results go to a Power BI exception page. A bounded model step drafts a cited cause for each exception, and the specialist accepts it or makes the fix in AFAS.
tasks.previous_blocker: The checks lived in one person's Excel habits. AFAS data had to be exported by hand each month, and nobody had time to write the rules down as code.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes a rule catalogue on the AFAS connectors a small build. Small model calls can now read mutation notes and draft a cause cheaply.
tasks.still_hard: Two CAOs plus shift and site variants mean many rule thresholds, and setting them without drowning in false alarms takes several cycles. Missing hours from team leads stay a people problem.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether an odd amount is right (a back-payment agreed by a manager, a settlement) and owning the correction that changes someone's pay.

ambition.what: Run the full pre-run check every night in the last week of the pay cycle, not once on run day, so team leads can fix hours before the deadline

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends run week deciding on a short list of explained exceptions instead of scanning sheets. They decide which rules block a run and their thresholds.

tasks.short: Turn shift lists and paper or Excel hour sheets from the sites into arrival and departure times for payroll.
tasks.statement: Complete time sheets showing employees' arrival and departure times.
tasks.design: Team leads enter or confirm hours themselves in AFAS hours entry (InSite or Pocket), configured with the shift roster as the default. A manager approval workflow in AFAS replaces the mailed sign-off. A small scheduled job compares entered hours with the roster and sends a Teams reminder to the team lead about gaps two days before the cut-off. A bounded extraction step handles the remaining paper sheets until each site has switched to digital entry.
tasks.previous_blocker: Warehouse team leads work on the floor without desks, so paper and Excel stayed the easy route. Nobody owned the change across three sites.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS mobile hours entry is standard, and a roster-versus-hours gap check is a small job to build. Reading photographed sheets is now cheap enough to bridge the transition.
tasks.still_hard: Getting 750 shift workers' hours entered by team leads on time in three sites. If there is no clock system, the times are still what the team lead says.
tasks.human_edge: Settling disputed hours with a team lead or employee, and deciding on late or retro corrections.

ambition.what: Close and approve hours weekly instead of at month end, so shift allowances and overtime errors are caught within days

tasks.altitude: The specialist no longer keys hours. They watch the gap list and handle disputes, and they decide the cut-off rules and the roster defaults.

tasks.short: Collect new-hire documents and key the employee, contract and pay data into AFAS.
tasks.statement: Process paperwork for new employees and enter employee information into the payroll system.
tasks.design: When a candidate reaches 'hired' in Recruitee, an integration creates an AFAS onboarding workflow pre-filled with offer data. The new hire completes personal data, IBAN and payroll tax choice in an AFAS InSite form.
