Deterministic checks validate the BSN eleven-test, IBAN check digits, required fields and the CAO scale against the offer. The specialist approves the prepared employee and contract record before it is committed. The first pre-run is then checked against the offer amount automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recruitee and AFAS were not connected, so the offer data was keyed twice. Contract variants across two CAOs made a generic import look risky.
tasks.enabler_now: The Recruitee API and AFAS UpdateConnectors can be stitched in days with AI-assisted coding. Explicit CAO scale tables make the mapping testable.
tasks.still_hard: Off-pattern contracts (individual deals, previous service, part-time on shift patterns) need a person. ID copies hold sensitive data and must be handled under AVG rules (BSN masked, limited retention).
tasks.human_edge: Approving the contract record that sets someone's pay and settling odd agreements with the recruiter or manager.

ambition.what: Give every new hire and their manager a confirmed 'your first pay' summary before day one, starting with warehouse shift starters

tasks.altitude: The specialist approves prepared records instead of typing them and handles only the non-standard contracts. They decide which contract variants may flow through on the standard path.

tasks.short: Gather hours, overtime, shift allowances and absence from sites and systems into the monthly payroll input.
tasks.statement: Compile employee time, production, and payroll data from time sheets and other records.
tasks.design: Replace the monthly Excel input sheet with a scheduled Python job on the governed data platform. It pulls approved hours and absence from AFAS and agency hours files from the three portals. It applies the CAO overtime and shift allowance rules from explicit, versioned tables and stages the variable pay lines. After the specialist approves the staged batch, the job posts it to AFAS through an UpdateConnector. A Power BI page shows labour cost per site, own staff versus flex, for the controller.
tasks.previous_blocker: The allowance rules of two CAOs sat in Excel formulas, and agency data came as differing files from three portals, so automation looked fragile.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes per-portal parsers and rule tables with tests cheap to write and change each season.
tasks.still_hard: Agency portal formats change without warning, and CAO changes need rule updates on time. Hours that arrive late after the cut-off still need a decision.
tasks.human_edge: Approving the batch that goes into the pay run and deciding on late hours and CAO interpretation questions with HR and the works council.

ambition.what: A weekly labour-cost-per-site view, own staff and flex together, for the Controller and site managers during peak season

tasks.altitude: The specialist reviews one staged batch per run instead of building it. They own the versioned CAO rule tables and decide the cut-off policy.

tasks.short: Each month, match the payroll paid from Rabobank to the AFAS payroll journal and file the period-end report.
tasks.statement: Prepare and balance period-end reports, and reconcile issued payrolls to bank statements.
tasks.design: Replace the Excel reconciliation with a scheduled Python job on a governed data platform that pulls the AFAS payroll journal through its GetConnector and Rabobank CAMT.053 statements, matches by batch, employee and amount, and writes a break list to a Teams channel. A small model step proposes the cause of each break; the job builds the period-end report on SharePoint for the specialist to sign before it goes to the controller.
tasks.previous_blocker: The match was quick enough in Excel for one person, and building a bank-to-payroll link was a project nobody owned between HR and Finance.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes a small matching job and report a matter of days, and bank statement files and AFAS connectors are standard interfaces.
tasks.still_hard: Off-cycle corrections and advances paid outside AFAS break the match, and the bank feed needs Finance and IT to agree on access.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a break is a real overpayment to reclaim from an employee, and talking to that person, stays with the specialist.

ambition.what: Reconcile every payment batch the day after it runs, including weekly flex and off-cycle runs, instead of once at month end.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends minutes on a break list instead of hours on a sheet, and decides which breaks become reclaims or journal corrections.

tasks.short: Collect pay mutations, run AFAS payroll, check it, pay through Rabobank and publish payslips.
tasks.statement: Process and issue employee paychecks and statements of earnings and deductions.
tasks.design: Move mutations into AFAS InSite workflows and import the rest through a small intake job that reads remaining mails into checked AFAS import lines. AFAS keeps doing the gross-to-net; a pre-run check job applies explicit rules to the draft run and a model step explains each hit, so the specialist approves the run and the Rabobank batch from an exception list.
tasks.previous_blocker: Two CAOs, shift allowances and seasonal staff made mutations messy, and the checks lived in the specialist's head and personal Excel.
tasks.enabler_now: Rule checks around the payroll engine are now common practice, and a bounded model can read free-text mutation mails and explain exceptions without touching the calculation.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping CAO rule variants correct, and staff trust: many employees do not want AI near their pay.
tasks.human_edge: Approving the run and the payment, and calling an employee whose pay is wrong, stay with the specialist.

ambition.what: Run the pre-run check daily during the input window, so managers fix wrong hours before cut-off instead of after payday.

tasks.altitude: The specialist writes and tunes the check rules and approves runs from an exception list, measured on first-time-right runs and corrections per run.

tasks.short: Build pay and benefit summaries for Finance, management, pension fund and statistics bodies, and send them.
tasks.statement: Compile statistical reports, statements, and summaries related to pay and benefits accounts, and submit them to appropriate departments.
tasks.design: Turn the recurring summaries into a Power BI payroll report on the existing nightly AFAS extract, with role-based access for controller, FP&A and HR director, which removes most ad hoc requests. A deterministic job produces the month pack and a checked model draft of variance commentary; external submissions go out only after the specialist approves.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each department wanted its own cut, and pay data is confidential, so it stayed in the specialist's spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: The nightly AFAS extract and Power BI already exist; adding a governed payroll model with row-level security is now quick to build.
tasks.still_hard: Access control on salary data per role, and agreeing one definition of cost per FTE across HR and Finance.
tasks.human_edge: Judging what a pay movement means for the business and explaining it to the controller and HR director stays human.

ambition.what: A quarterly gender pay gap readiness report under EU 2023/970, ahead of the first mandatory report over 2027 pay due 7 June 2028.

tasks.altitude: The specialist stops building cuts and becomes the owner of payroll figures others self-serve, and decides which pay gaps need explaining before the works council sees them.

tasks.short: Balance payroll clearing accounts in the ledger against payments to staff, tax office and pension fund.
tasks.statement: Balance cash and payroll accounts.
tasks.design: Extend the bank-to-payroll matching job with a ledger step: it ties each payroll clearing account (net pay, wage tax, pension, garnishments) to its source files and shows an ageing list of open items on a Power BI page. The specialist explains what remains and approves drafted correcting entries, which are posted to AFAS through its UpdateConnector.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources sit in three places (AFAS ledger, tax return, pension fund invoice) and differences are small and varied, so nobody built a tool.
tasks.enabler_now: Fast code generation makes one job across these sources cheap, reusing the bank reconciliation from task 2528.
tasks.still_hard: Old open items with no paper trail, and pension fund invoices that arrive as PDFs in differing formats.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether an old difference is written off, reclaimed or corrected, and agreeing that with the controller, stays human.

ambition.what: Close the payroll clearing accounts weekly instead of at month end, so open items never age past one period.

tasks.altitude: The specialist works from an ageing list and gains the right to propose correcting entries ready for posting, with the controller signing off.

tasks.short: Work out, enter and explain back-pay or corrections for earlier errors and back-dated CAO raises in AFAS.
tasks.statement: Issue and record adjustments to pay related to previous errors or retroactive increases.
tasks.design: Correction requests come in through an AFAS Profit workflow instead of mail. A back-dated CAO raise is loaded once from the wage table through the AFAS UpdateConnector, and AFAS's own retro calculation handles the periods. A scheduled check job compares the test run with the expected difference and attaches a short model-written explanation to each exception. The specialist approves, and the system sends a templated notice to the employee.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests came in by free-form mail, and bulk CAO raises across two CAOs were cheaper to work out in Excel than to script against AFAS.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes a small connector script and a rule-check job cheap to build. AFAS already does the retro calculation and keeps wage-component history [S5].
tasks.still_hard: Corrections that cross tax years or touch pension and benefits, and errors whose cause is unclear, still need the specialist to investigate.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a correction is right, and agreeing on recovery of an overpayment with an employee in a way that is fair and lawful.

ambition.what: A monthly 'corrections per run' report to HR and the Controller that traces each correction back to its intake error.

tasks.altitude: Instead of rebuilding calculations in Excel, the specialist approves corrections and decides how overpayments are recovered, within agreed limits.

tasks.short: Prepare, check and file the monthly loonaangifte to the Belastingdienst and arrange payment of loonheffingen.
tasks.statement: Prepare and file payroll tax returns.
tasks.design: Configure AFAS Profit to generate and file the loonaangifte through Digipoort, with one click to approve. The Excel reconciliation is replaced by a scheduled job on the AFAS extract that ties journal, return and ledger, sends breaks to the specialist and feeds a Power BI page the Accountant also uses. The job prepares the payment batch for the bookkeeper to release in Rabobank.
tasks.previous_blocker: Filing itself was already done in software. The reconciliation stayed in Excel because nobody owned a shared payroll-to-ledger check.
tasks.enabler_now: A nightly AFAS extract and Power BI already exist, and AI coding makes a reconciliation job cheap. A model is not needed for this task.
tasks.still_hard: Correction messages for earlier periods, and differences that come from manual ledger entries, still need investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Signing off a filing to the tax authority and deciding how to correct a past period are the specialist's accountable acts.

ambition.what: Reconcile payroll to the ledger daily during close instead of once after filing, so breaks are caught before submission.

tasks.altitude: Close takes less of the specialist's time. They approve the filing on a reconciled dashboard and handle only the breaks.

tasks.short: Complete, check and send pension, UWV and insurance forms, and record them for employees.
tasks.statement: Complete, verify, and process forms and documentation for administration of benefits, such as pension plans, and unemployment and medical insurance.
tasks.design: An AFAS Profit workflow takes in benefit forms. A bounded extraction step reads incoming documents into fields, and deterministic code checks them against AFAS records. Periodic pension data goes out through AFAS's standard pension interface (UPA) wherever the fund supports it. The specialist approves each external submission, and filing in the dossier happens automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inputs were mixed paper and PDF forms from several funds and agencies, so reading them could not be automated cheaply.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction with a bounded model step is now reliable enough when every field is checked against AFAS. Building the workflow is cheap with AI coding.
tasks.still_hard: Health-related data is special-category data under the AVG, and reading the personnel file needs works council consent. Unusual cases such as WIA and partial disability still need expert handling.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining pension or disability consequences to an employee, and judging unusual cases with a fund or UWV.

ambition.what: Send seasonal flex workers who move onto Noordhaven contracts a pension enrolment check in their first week.

tasks.altitude: Less retyping. The specialist approves submissions and spends their time on the unusual cases and on employee questions.

tasks.short: Pull AFAS, Recruitee and Studytube data into Excel, build tables and charts, write commentary, send to managers.
tasks.statement: Generate standard or custom reports summarizing business, financial, or economic data for review by executives, managers, clients, and other stakeholders.
tasks.design: Replace the Excel workbooks with a scheduled extract from AFAS GetConnectors, Recruitee and Studytube APIs into one governed Power BI semantic model with fixed metric definitions. Standard reports become Power BI paginated reports with subscriptions; a bounded model step drafts the commentary from the delta table, and the analyst approves before release. Custom requests are built on the same model, not from fresh exports.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each source needed its own export and the joins (employee to vacancy to course) lived in the analyst's Excel; building and maintaining connectors cost more time than the monthly manual work.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes the connector and transformation code a matter of days, and a model can draft the commentary that used to need the analyst for every report.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing one definition of hire, productive and 90-day retention across sites and flex workers; the reasons behind a trend still need someone who knows the sites.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which change matters to the HR director this month, and what a number means given a reorganisation in Venlo or a peak season, stays with the analyst.

ambition.what: A weekly instead of monthly 90-day retention and onboarding-week-one report per site, so HRBPs act on new hires still in their first month.

tasks.altitude: The analyst stops assembling reports and spends that time on checking definitions and on the questions behind the numbers; they decide which metrics enter the standard pack.

tasks.short: Check nightly refresh, chase late data, send reports and manage who sees which dashboard.
tasks.statement: Manage timely flow of business intelligence information to users.
tasks.design: A scheduled job checks the extract and refresh each morning, runs data checks (missing end dates, open sick reports, unknown cost centres) and posts failures to a Teams channel and a status banner on the dashboards. Power BI subscriptions replace mailed reports, and row-level security is driven by the AFAS manager hierarchy, with a daily diff of access changes the analyst approves.
tasks.previous_blocker: Access lists and mail lists were kept by hand because linking AFAS org changes to Power BI roles needed scripting nobody had time for.
tasks.enabler_now: Power BI subscriptions and row-level security are standard, and AI coding makes the AFAS-to-security-role sync a small job.
tasks.still_hard: The AFAS manager hierarchy is often out of date after reorganisations, and flex workers from agencies are not in AFAS at all.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding who may see per-person absence and pay data, and handling exceptions such as an interim site manager, stays with the analyst and HR director.

ambition.what: Shift leaders on the three warehouse floors get a team view of week-one onboarding and course certificates (forklift, VCA) for the first time.

tasks.altitude: The analyst no longer sends files; they own the access rules and the data checks, and approve access changes once a day.

tasks.short: Change the AFAS extract, Power BI model and dashboards when definitions, sites or CAO rules change.
tasks.statement: Maintain or update business intelligence tools, databases, dashboards, systems, or methods.
tasks.design: Put the AFAS extract, Power Query and the semantic model in version control with a test set of signed-off monthly numbers; changes are drafted with a coding assistant and Copilot DAX help, tested automatically, then deployed through Power BI deployment pipelines. The definitions catalogue is generated from the model and published on SharePoint.
tasks.previous_blocker: Power BI models were edited by hand in the desktop tool with no tests, so every change needed a long manual check against AFAS.
tasks.enabler_now: Coding assistants write DAX, SQL and test scripts quickly, and Power BI supports deployment pipelines and text-based model files.
tasks.still_hard: Getting HR to agree on definitions, and legacy AFAS fields filled differently per site.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the definition (does a flex worker who is converted count as a hire?) and judging whether a new measure is lawful and fair stays with the analyst.

ambition.what: A published HR metric catalogue that FP&A, payroll and HRBPs use as the single source for headcount, verzuim and 90-day retention.

tasks.altitude: The analyst moves from editing dashboards to owning the metric layer: definitions, tests and releases, with sign-off rights on any metric change.

tasks.short: Answer manager questions about HR dashboards, fix access or filters, explain numbers that look wrong.
tasks.statement: Provide technical support for existing reports, dashboards, or other tools.
tasks.design: A Teams answer desk, read-only on the HR semantic model, answers from a list of verified answers and the metric catalogue, under each manager's row-level security with a minimum group size, and says it is AI. It checks refresh status and access first, routes everything it cannot answer to the analyst, and logs every question to a dashboard that drives report fixes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Questions arrived in free text and most needed a look at access, refresh and definitions together, which only the analyst could combine.
tasks.enabler_now: Models now read Dutch free text well enough to classify a question and match it to a definition, and Copilot in Power BI can answer on a prepared model.
tasks.still_hard: Copilot in Power BI does not officially support non-English chat, and wrong answers about absence or pay harm trust quickly; verified answers take ongoing upkeep.
tasks.human_edge: Questions that hide a people problem (a manager asking about one employee's absence) need the analyst's judgment and a redirect to the HRBP.

ambition.what: Site and shift managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo get answers on headcount, flex hours and verzuim rates within minutes, outside office hours.

tasks.altitude: The analyst handles only escalations and keeps the verified answer list; they decide which questions the desk may answer.

tasks.short: Track how HR's internal customers (site and team managers) use HR reports and where their hiring and flex demand is rising.
tasks.statement: Identify or monitor current and potential customers, using business intelligence tools.
tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on Fabric pulls the Power BI activity log, Recruitee vacancies and agency flex orders nightly and joins them to AFAS org units. A Power BI demand dashboard flags thresholds (vacancy open over 30 days, flex hours up 20%) and a weekly Teams post with a checked short narrative goes to each HRBP. Report usage is shown per site or team, never per named manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: The agency portals only gave CSV exports in three formats and the Power BI activity log needed admin scripting, so a weekly Excel merge was the cheapest route.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes the three portal parsers and the activity-log pull a few days of work, and Fabric gives a governed place to run them.
tasks.still_hard: Agency portal exports change format without notice, and agreeing which demand signal counts as 'rising' with HRBPs takes several rounds.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing that a spike in Venlo flex orders is a seasonal client contract and not a retention problem, and choosing which site to raise with the HR Director.

ambition.what: Weekly instead of monthly decision per site on whether to open permanent vacancies or keep using flex workers

tasks.altitude: The analyst checks one dashboard on Monday and spends the time on two or three sites that show a real change. They decide the thresholds and which signals reach HRBPs.

tasks.short: Design and build Power BI models, datasets and Excel tools on AFAS and other HR data for HR and managers.
tasks.statement: Create business intelligence tools or systems, including design of related databases, spreadsheets, or outputs.
tasks.design: Move HR models to Power BI project files (PBIP) in git on Fabric, with the AFAS extract as a versioned Python or Dataflow job. The analyst writes specs and builds with AI coding tools and Copilot for DAX, automated tests reconcile headcount and FTE against AFAS payroll totals on every change, and a script generates the metric definitions page from the model.
tasks.previous_blocker: Power BI files were binary and hand-built, so tests and documentation were manual, and one analyst had no time to write code around them.
tasks.enabler_now: PBIP text formats plus AI coding let one person generate tests, DAX and documentation quickly; Copilot in Power BI writes DAX on a prepared model.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing definitions (what counts as a hire, a transfer, 90-day retention for flex-to-permanent) with HR and finance, and keeping special-category data out of models managers can open.
tasks.human_edge: Translating a vague question from the HR Director into the right metric, and refusing measures that would expose individuals or absence causes.

ambition.what: A shared, documented HR metric layer that FP&A and HRBPs build their own reports on

tasks.altitude: The analyst builds in days what took weeks and spends more time in the request conversation. They gain the right to set the official definition of each HR metric across HR and finance.

tasks.short: Compile monthly HR statistics from AFAS: hires, transfers, appraisals and absence rates, and keep the records clean.
tasks.statement: Maintain records and compile statistical reports concerning personnel-related data such as hires, transfers, performance appraisals, and absenteeism rates.
tasks.design: The nightly AFAS extract feeds a Power BI semantic model with fixed measures for hires, transfers, appraisal completion and verzuim percentage and frequency per site (rates and durations only, minimum group of five). Deterministic checks run after each refresh and post missing end dates or open sick reports to the HR admin queue; a paginated report subscription replaces the Excel/PowerPoint pack, with a checked draft commentary the analyst edits.
tasks.previous_blocker: The checks and calculations lived in the analyst's Excel workbooks, and the AFAS extract was built for finance, not for HR rules like Poortwachter timelines.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes it quick to turn the Excel logic into tested measures and check scripts; Power BI subscriptions and paginated reports are already in the licence.
tasks.still_hard: Some records are wrong at source (late sick reports, missing transfer dates), so the HR admin must still correct them; appraisal data may not be in AFAS at all.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining why verzuim rose at one site and deciding what the HR Director should hear, without exposing a small team or an individual case.

ambition.what: Verzuim and 90-day retention per site available and correct by working day 2 instead of mid-month

tasks.altitude: The monthly pack goes from about two days of work to an hour of review. The analyst decides which data breaks block publication and owns the verzuim and retention definitions.

tasks.short: Follow labour-market, CAO and regional trends around Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo and write what they mean for HR strategy.
tasks.statement: Identify and analyze industry or geographic trends with business strategy implications.
tasks.design: A weekly Python job on the data platform fetches CBS StatLine and UWV open data for the three regions, and a bounded model step summarises new CAO texts and sector publications with links. A Power BI page sets these next to Noordhaven's own time to hire, offer acceptance and turnover per site, and a draft note with checked figures goes to the analyst for edit before the HR Director's meeting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources were scattered PDFs, web pages and tables, and summarising them took hours, so it was done ad hoc before strategy meetings.
tasks.enabler_now: Open statistics APIs plus a cheap model step that summarises free text with source checks make a weekly scan affordable.
tasks.still_hard: Public data lags months and rarely matches Noordhaven's job groups; judging cause and effect stays with people, as trend reports themselves warn.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a regional shortage of drivers or order pickers should change Noordhaven's pay, agency mix or hiring plan, and arguing it with the HR Director.

ambition.what: Site managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo get a quarterly regional labour-market brief for their own site

tasks.altitude: The analyst reads a weekly digest instead of searching, and spends the time on the implications. They gain a regular slot in HR strategy discussions instead of ad hoc requests.

tasks.short: Gather outside labour-market, wage, absence and agency-rate data into Excel for HR benchmarks.
tasks.statement: Collect business intelligence data from available industry reports, public information, field reports, or purchased sources.
tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform pulls CBS StatLine and UWV open data monthly into one benchmark table with source and date, and a small extraction loop adds figures from purchased PDF reports with a page reference. A Power BI benchmark page sits next to the AFAS-based HR dashboards, and a Teams message lists what changed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources are scattered and few; a one-person team copied by hand because building parsers for each publisher did not pay off.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes small connectors cheap to write and maintain, and a model can read varied PDF tables into a fixed schema with a check.
tasks.still_hard: Purchased reports have licence limits and differing definitions (job groups, absence measures), so comparability stays a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which outside figure is really comparable to a Venlo warehouse shift worker, and saying when it is not.

ambition.what: Monthly instead of yearly check of Noordhaven warehouse wages and agency rates against the regional market, feeding C&B and flex-pool decisions.

tasks.altitude: The analyst stops copying numbers and spends the time on comparability notes; they decide which sources enter the benchmark table.

tasks.short: Tell managers and HR about new reports, dashboard changes and metric definitions, and answer how-to questions.
tasks.statement: Disseminate information regarding tools, reports, or metadata enhancements.
tasks.design: A script reads the Power BI semantic model and deployment history to build a change list, and a bounded loop drafts the release note the analyst approves before a scheduled Teams post. How-to questions go to Copilot in Power BI on the prepared HR model with verified answers and row-level security, labelled as AI, with misses routed to the analyst.
tasks.previous_blocker: Change tracking was manual and questions came by mail one at a time; chat over data needed a well-prepared model and capacity licences.
tasks.enabler_now: Copilot in Power BI answers questions on a prepared semantic model, and model metadata can be read by script to list changes.
tasks.still_hard: Copilot misreads unprepared models and Dutch chat is not officially supported, so the model needs synonyms, descriptions and verified answers in English or tested Dutch.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining to a sceptical site manager why the absence figure changed, and noticing who did not understand.

ambition.what: Shift leads on the three warehouse sites get answers on onboarding and verzuim figures for their teams without going through an HRBP.

tasks.altitude: The analyst owns the metric definitions and verified answers that managers query, instead of writing each answer.

tasks.short: Write specifications for HR reports and dashboards: purpose, measures, sources, filters and access.
tasks.statement: Document specifications for business intelligence or information technology reports, dashboards, or other outputs.
tasks.design: A script reads the Power BI semantic model (field names, measures, descriptions) and writes a data dictionary to SharePoint on each deployment; a bounded loop turns intake notes into a spec draft on the standard template, and Copilot in Power BI drafts DAX that the analyst tests. Access and privacy sections stay the analyst's call, signed off by the HR Director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specs and dictionaries were hand-written because tooling to read model metadata and write prose was not worth building for one analyst.
tasks.enabler_now: Model metadata is scriptable, Copilot writes DAX, and a model can fill a template from meeting notes with gaps flagged.
tasks.still_hard: Getting requesters to say what decision the report serves, and deciding which views count as monitoring under WOR 27(1)(l).
tasks.human_edge: Pushing back on a request that would let managers watch individual absence, and finding the real question behind the ask.

ambition.what: A living HR metric catalogue on SharePoint that HRBPs, Finance and Copilot all use as the one source of definitions.

tasks.altitude: The analyst moves from typing specs to approving them and owns the access and privacy decision per report.

tasks.short: Combine HR metrics and outside trends into a short analysis with recommendations for HR leadership.
tasks.statement: Synthesize current business intelligence or trend data to support recommendations for action.
tasks.design: Fixed variance rules on the Power BI HR model flag changes by site and month in 90-day retention, time to hire and verzuim rate against prior periods and the benchmark table. A bounded loop drafts a cited one-page brief that a script checks number by number; the analyst writes the recommendation and presents it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Variance hunting lived in Excel and writing took hours; generated text could not be trusted to keep numbers right.
tasks.enabler_now: Variance rules are quick to code, and a model draft can be checked mechanically against the source numbers.
tasks.still_hard: Cause is rarely visible in the data; small site groups give noisy rates, and absence must stay at rate and duration level.
tasks.human_edge: Linking a retention dip in Tilburg to a known shift-pattern change and judging what HR can actually change.

ambition.what: A monthly site-level 90-day retention and verzuim brief for the HR Director instead of a quarterly deck.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends time on interpretation and recommendations and gets a standing slot in the HR management meeting.

tasks.short: Test that HR reports and metrics match what HR asked for and reconcile to AFAS.
tasks.statement: Conduct or coordinate tests to ensure that intelligence is consistent with defined needs.
tasks.design: Replace the reconciliation spreadsheets with a scheduled test suite (SQL or Python) that runs after the nightly AFAS extract and before the Power BI refresh is published. Results feed a small test dashboard and a Teams message to the analyst; failed tests get a model-drafted cause list that the analyst checks and routes to the HR administrator for AFAS fixes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing and maintaining tests for every measure took more analyst time than checking by hand in Excel, and there was no data platform step between AFAS and Power BI to run them.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding writes the test code and expected values from a metric definition in hours; Power BI and Fabric dataflows allow a check step before publishing.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing one definition of 90-day retention or verzuim with HRBPs and finance; tests only guard what was defined.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what the HR director actually means by a metric and spotting when a number is right but answers the wrong question.

ambition.what: Release the 90-day retention and verzuim figures to site managers daily instead of monthly, because each refresh is tested.

tasks.altitude: The analyst checks exceptions instead of rebuilding reconciliations, and gains the right to stop a release that fails its tests.

tasks.short: Analyse the regional labour market and competing employers' pay and offers for drivers and warehouse staff.
tasks.statement: Analyze competitive market strategies through analysis of related product, market, or share trends.
tasks.design: A quarterly Python job collects public labour market statistics and approved vacancy sources, a bounded extraction step turns vacancy texts into a pay benchmark table, and a Power BI page sets it against Noordhaven's CAO pay, offer acceptance and time to hire per site. A model drafts the quarterly brief from the dashboard; the analyst writes the advice.
tasks.previous_blocker: Competitor pay sits in unstructured vacancy texts; collecting and coding it by hand took days, so it was done rarely and on small samples.
tasks.enabler_now: Cheap, checkable extraction of free text into fixed fields, and AI coding for the collection job and dashboard.
tasks.still_hard: Coverage and bias of vacancy samples, terms of use of job sites, and the fact that advertised pay is not paid pay.
tasks.human_edge: Judging what the market means for Noordhaven's offer to a Venlo reach-truck driver, and weighing it against CAO and budget.

ambition.what: Review entry pay and shift allowances per site each quarter before peak season instead of once a year.

tasks.altitude: The analyst moves from collecting data to advising the HR director and C&B on offers per site, with the brief as input to pay decisions.

tasks.short: Pull HR data from AFAS and agency portals and prepare required reports and filings.
tasks.statement: Analyze employment-related data and prepare required reports.
tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform pulls the AFAS extract and agency hours, runs fixed data-quality checks, and fills a template per required report (works-council social data, statistics surveys, annual-report staff figures, later pay-gap reporting). A bounded model step drafts the explanation; the analyst reviews, and the HR director or controller approves before anything leaves the company.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each report had its own Excel logic and flex workers sat in three agency portals, so the work was rebuilt by hand each cycle.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes per-report scripts and templates cheap to write and test; the nightly AFAS extract already exists.
tasks.still_hard: Changing legal definitions (for example pay transparency) and matching agency flex data to AFAS headcount.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding how to treat edge cases in a legal filing and answering for the figures to the controller, works council or authorities.

ambition.what: A quarterly works-council data pack on headcount, flex use and verzuim rates per site, produced from the same pipeline.

tasks.altitude: The analyst reviews and signs off filings instead of building them, and owns the definitions each filing uses.

tasks.short: Keep the library of metric definitions, report templates, DAX measures and queries current and findable.
tasks.statement: Maintain library of model documents, templates, or other reusable knowledge assets.
tasks.design: Keep templates, queries and Power BI files in a versioned SharePoint library or Git, and run a monthly script that reads model metadata and usage to list undocumented, duplicate and unused measures. A bounded model step drafts definition pages that the analyst approves, and the same definitions feed Copilot in Power BI so colleagues get answers without asking the analyst.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documentation always lost to new report requests; nobody had time to write definitions or prune old files.
tasks.enabler_now: Drafting definitions from DAX and metadata is cheap, and Copilot in Power BI uses model descriptions to answer questions.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping definitions agreed with HRBPs and finance; Copilot misreads poorly described models and Dutch questions are not officially supported.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which definition is the official one and retiring a report people still like.

ambition.what: Site and shift managers look up HR metric definitions and reports themselves in Teams for the first time.

tasks.altitude: Less time on filing and answering where-is questions; the analyst decides which definitions are official and which assets are retired.

tasks.short: Write or review specs for HR reports and dashboards: sources, measures, filters, access, refresh.
tasks.statement: Create or review technical design documentation to ensure the accurate development of reporting solutions.
tasks.design: A request form (Microsoft Forms into a SharePoint list) replaces the mail intake. A scheduled Python job reads Power BI model metadata and the AFAS extract schema into a data dictionary and metric catalogue; a bounded model step fills the SharePoint spec template from the request and dictionary, and a deterministic checker compares the deployed Power BI model against the spec and lists deviations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specs need free-text requests turned into exact measure definitions, and nobody had time to build a metadata extractor for a one-person analytics function.
tasks.enabler_now: Models can draft measure definitions and DAX from plain requests, and AI coding makes a metadata extractor and diff checker a few days of work.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing what a metric means (for example when the 90-day clock starts for a flex worker who converts) stays a negotiation between HR and Finance; models also invent column names, so the dictionary check is not optional.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding the definition, who may see which rows, and whether a group is too small to show without exposing individuals.

ambition.what: A published HR metric catalogue (90-day retention, verzuim rate, time to hire) that HRBPs, FP&A and Copilot read from

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends spec time on definitions and sign-off instead of typing; they gain the right to approve or refuse any new HR measure entering the semantic model.

tasks.short: Scan HR tech and analytics trends and advise which tools or features Noordhaven should adopt or improve.
tasks.statement: Analyze technology trends to identify markets for future product development or to improve sales of existing products.
tasks.design: A weekly Python job pulls release notes from AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube and Power BI plus AP, AWVN and AI Act sources into a SharePoint list; a bounded model step labels and summarises each item with its link and caveat. A Power BI usage report sits next to it, and the analyst turns the shortlist into a quarterly brief that a model drafts and they edit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reading dozens of sources a month for a 13-person HR team never paid off, so it happened ad hoc and from memory.
tasks.enabler_now: Models can label and summarise free-text release notes cheaply with source links, and feed collection is quick to build with AI coding.
tasks.still_hard: Vendor claims are rarely backed by customer results, and trend reports do not show cause; judging what holds for Dutch shift work under a CAO and works council stays with the analyst.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a feature fits Noordhaven's sites, data and works council, and saying 'not yet' to the HR Director with reasons.

ambition.what: An adopt, wait or drop call on each AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube and Power BI release every quarter instead of at the yearly contract renewal

tasks.altitude: Scanning shrinks to a weekly 30-minute review; the analyst becomes the named advisor on the HR system roadmap and proposes pilots to the HR Director.

tasks.short: Read applications in Recruitee against the vacancy and decide who fits the job requirements.
tasks.statement: Review employment applications and job orders to match applicants with job requirements.
tasks.design: Configure a structured intake form in Recruitee so each vacancy has explicit must-haves and nice-to-haves. A small job on the governed HR platform pulls new applications through the Recruitee API, extracts quoted facts with a bounded model step, runs the must-have rules and writes a fact panel and a draft screening note back into Recruitee. The recruiter makes every stage move; nothing rejects automatically and there is no single match score.
tasks.previous_blocker: CVs are unstructured and vary wildly; rule-based parsers were too weak and full matching tools raised legal and works-council concerns.
tasks.enabler_now: Models can extract facts with quoted evidence reliably enough to review, and AI coding makes the Recruitee integration and rules a days-long build.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding fit for people with unusual paths, and keeping extraction errors from silently excluding candidates. Works council consent and, from 2 December 2027, high-risk AI Act duties apply.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing potential in an unusual CV and knowing what a site manager really needs beyond the written requirements.

ambition.what: Every applicant gets a must-have check within one working day of applying, instead of when the recruiter gets to the pile.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter spends less time reading and more time on intake with managers; they gain the right to sharpen must-haves per vacancy with data on why candidates fail them.

tasks.short: Tell candidates about duties, pay, CAO benefits, shifts and working conditions by phone, mail and in vacancy texts.
tasks.statement: Inform job applicants of details such as duties and responsibilities, compensation, benefits, schedules, working conditions, or promotion opportunities.
tasks.design: Keep a small maintained table on SharePoint with CAO scales, allowances, shift patterns and site facts per function, owned by C&B. A generator turns it into a vacancy text and a per-vacancy info pack linked from every Recruitee vacancy and invitation mail. An internal answer desk drafts cited replies to remaining candidate mails for the recruiter to send.
tasks.previous_blocker: Pay and shift facts live in the CAO PDF, AFAS and people's heads, so each answer needed a lookup and a fresh mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Cheap generation of documents from structured tables and cited retrieval over policy text, both quick to build with AI coding.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping the fact table current after CAO changes and indexation; any wrong pay figure has legal and trust costs.
tasks.human_edge: Reading a candidate's doubts in a call and being honest about night shifts, peak season and physical work.

ambition.what: A one-page info pack per vacancy (pay scale, shifts, travel allowance, site, first week) sent with every interview invite.

tasks.altitude: Fewer repeat phone calls; the recruiter spends calls on doubts, not facts, and decides when info packs are good enough to publish.

tasks.short: Shortlist qualified candidates, screen them and recommend hires to hiring managers.
tasks.statement: Select qualified job applicants or refer them to managers, making hiring recommendations when appropriate.
tasks.design: Use Recruitee scorecards as the single record of the recruiter's assessment, and generate the manager profile from them with a bounded drafting step the recruiter approves. A scheduled job reads Recruitee stage dates and nudges managers in Teams when feedback is overdue, with a weekly list of candidates stuck too long. Interviews and the recommendation stay human; no AI notetaker becomes the record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were scattered across mail and Word, and nudging managers took a person watching every pipeline.
tasks.enabler_now: Stage dates are available through the Recruitee API, and profiles can be drafted from structured scorecards in seconds.
tasks.still_hard: Getting managers to act on nudges and to read the profile rather than replace the interview; bias in the recommendation itself.
tasks.human_edge: Judging motivation, reliability and team fit in conversation and standing behind a recommendation to a site manager.

ambition.what: Manager decisions on every shortlisted candidate within three working days, tracked per site.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter stops chasing and spends more time interviewing; they gain a stage-delay view to escalate slow managers to the HRBP with facts.

tasks.short: Tell applicants where their application stands, by mail and by phone, including rejections.
tasks.statement: Contact job applicants to inform them of the status of their applications.
tasks.design: Configure Recruitee to send templated emails on stage changes, with automatic sends for receipt and early-stage rejections after the recruiter's stage move, and recruiter review for post-interview messages. A daily job flags candidates with no contact for five working days in a Teams list. Follow-up replies get a cited draft; post-interview rejections stay a phone call.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates existed but were sent by hand, and nobody saw who had waited too long without a check across all vacancies.
tasks.enabler_now: Stage-triggered email in the ATS plus a simple API job for wait-time flags; AI coding makes the glue cheap.
tasks.still_hard: Writing rejection templates that are kind and specific enough, and keeping stage data accurate so the right mail goes out.
tasks.human_edge: Delivering a rejection after an interview in a way that keeps the candidate willing to apply again or recommend Noordhaven.

ambition.what: Every applicant, including the many early-stage warehouse applicants who now often hear nothing, gets a status within five working days.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter no longer hunts for who is owed an update; they decide the contact standard per stage and spend the time on post-interview calls.

tasks.short: Find candidates for open roles through job boards, agencies, talent pool, referrals and direct outreach.
tasks.statement: Perform searches for qualified job candidates, using sources such as computer databases, networking, Internet recruiting resources, media advertisements, job fairs, recruiting firms, or employee referrals.
tasks.design: Configure Recruitee multiposting, source tags and email templates so ads and tracking stop being manual. A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform reads the Recruitee talent pool via API, applies hard filters in code and runs a bounded model pass that marks must-haves with quoted CV evidence; outreach drafts land in Recruitee for the recruiter to approve. A Power BI page joins Recruitee source tags with AFAS 90-day retention so channels are judged on hires who stay.
tasks.previous_blocker: CVs are free text and the talent pool was unsearchable beyond keywords, and joining Recruitee to AFAS retention needed custom data work nobody had time for.
tasks.enabler_now: Models read CVs reliably enough to cite evidence per criterion, and AI-assisted coding makes the Recruitee and AFAS API jobs a matter of days.
tasks.still_hard: Works council consent and future EU AI Act high-risk duties for any ranking; more AI-written applications lower signal quality; agency portals may lack APIs.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which warehouse team lead will work with which candidate, and the phone call that convinces a passive candidate to come for a shift trial.

ambition.what: Former flex workers and silver-medal applicants in the Recruitee pool get a personal call-back when a matching role opens at their site.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter spends the freed hours on calls and hiring-manager intake instead of posting and copying; they decide which channel mix each site gets based on 90-day retention data.

tasks.short: Check selection criteria, tests and interview kits for fairness, job relevance and legal fit; recommend changes.
tasks.statement: Evaluate recruitment or selection criteria to ensure conformance to professional, statistical, or testing standards, recommending revisions, as needed.
tasks.design: A nightly job on the governed data platform pulls Recruitee stage data and SharePoint documents into a Power BI selection-health page with pass rates per stage, site and source. A bounded model pass checks each ad and interview kit against a written checklist and returns quoted flags the recruiter accepts or rejects; accepted flags feed a drafted memo for the HRBP.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stage data lived in Recruitee exports and documents on SharePoint, so a review meant days of manual Excel and reading, done rarely.
tasks.enabler_now: Cheap API pulls and a model that can read wording against a checklist with quotes make a quarterly review a few hours of work.
tasks.still_hard: Dutch employers do not record ethnicity, so group comparisons rely on thin proxies; small volumes per role make pass rates noisy; legal judgement stays with people.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a demand like a forklift certificate or Dutch B1 is truly needed for safety, and persuading a hiring manager to drop a habit.

ambition.what: Review every role family's criteria each quarter instead of only after a complaint or audit.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter becomes the person who signs off selection criteria per role family and brings evidence to hiring managers; the weekly work shifts from compiling to arguing changes.

tasks.short: Plan how to fill current and seasonal staffing needs per site and role.
tasks.statement: Develop or implement recruiting strategies to meet current or anticipated staffing needs.
tasks.design: Replace the Excel sheet that ties AFAS headcount, Recruitee vacancies and agency orders with a nightly job on the governed data platform feeding a Power BI staffing-demand page per site and week. The recruiter decides the strategy; a bounded model step drafts the plan text around figures inserted by code.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agency orders, AFAS headcount and Recruitee lived apart, so demand was rebuilt by hand in Excel once or twice a year.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes the three-source extract and dashboard cheap to build and maintain.
tasks.still_hard: Agency portal data may only come as exports; seasonal peaks depend on customer contracts the HR team does not see early.
tasks.human_edge: Reading site managers and the commercial calendar, and choosing trade-offs between agencies, permanent hires and CAO limits on flex chains.

ambition.what: A monthly per-site hiring plan for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo instead of one yearly plan.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter runs a monthly planning slot with each site and decides which flex roles to convert to permanent; less time compiling numbers.

tasks.short: Build, schedule, run and score applicant tests such as forklift practicals and reading tests; check they work.
tasks.statement: Develop, administer, and evaluate applicant tests.
tasks.design: Configure Recruitee self-scheduling and templates for test invites; a tablet form (Microsoft Forms or a small Power App) scores multiple-choice and practical checklists by code and writes the result into Recruitee for recruiter sign-off. A Power BI page links test results to AFAS 90-day retention; a bounded model step only drafts new question items for human review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tests ran on paper per site, so scores never reached a system and nobody could check whether tests predicted who stayed.
tasks.enabler_now: Low-code forms and the Recruitee API are quick to wire with AI-assisted coding; question drafting is cheap.
tasks.still_hard: Small numbers per test version make validity checks weak; tests that decide on candidates fall under GDPR Art. 22 and later the AI Act high-risk regime.
tasks.human_edge: Watching a candidate drive a reach truck safely and judging nerves versus lack of skill; deciding pass or fail stays with a person.

ambition.what: A yearly test validity report per site showing which tests predict 90-day retention.

tasks.altitude: Scheduling and paperwork drop out; the recruiter owns test design per role family with evidence of what predicts staying.
